questionEn: To which noble Arab tribe did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ belong?
explanationEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ belonged to the tribe of Quraysh, the custodians of the Kaaba in Makkah.

questionEn: Which specific clan of Quraysh was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ born into?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ belonged to Banu Hashim, named after his great-grandfather Hashim ibn Abd Manaf.

questionEn: What was the name of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ paternal grandfather who cared for him after his mother passed away?
explanationEn: Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim, the respected leader of Makkah, took the young Prophet ﷺ into his care until he passed away at age eight.

questionEn: Which two honorable duties regarding pilgrims did Abd al-Muttalib hold in Makkah?
optionsEn: Guarding the city walls and trade caravans
explanationEn: Banu Hashim held the prestigious offices of Siqayah (providing water from Zamzam) and Rifadah (feeding pilgrims).

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ great-grandfather Hashim earn the title 'Hashim'?
optionsEn: He crumbled bread into broth to feed starving pilgrims
He rebuilt the roof of the Kaaba
He discovered a trade route to Yemen
explanationEn: His birth name was Amr, and he was nicknamed Hashim ('the crusher') because he broke bread into broth to feed people during famine in Makkah.

questionEn: What major event occurred in Makkah in the same year Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born?
optionsEn: The rebuilding of the Kaaba by Quraysh
The digging of the Zamzam well
The Expedition of the Elephant (Am al-Fil)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ was born in the Year of the Elephant (around 570 CE), when Allah protected the Kaaba from Abrahah's army.

questionEn: Who led the army with war elephants from Yemen intending to demolish the Kaaba in the year of the Prophet's ﷺ birth?
explanationEn: Abrahah, the Abyssinian viceroy in Yemen, marched toward Makkah with an elephant to destroy the Kaaba and divert pilgrimage to Sanaa.

questionEn: What famous reply did Abd al-Muttalib give Abrahah when asked why he sought his confiscated camels rather than pleading for the Kaaba?
optionsEn: I am only a merchant of Makkah
Quraysh has hidden the treasures elsewhere
We will negotiate after the pilgrimage
I am the owner of the camels, and the House has a Lord who will protect it
explanationEn: Abd al-Muttalib expressed complete trust in Allah, stating that the Sacred House belongs to its Lord who would defend it.

questionEn: What was the name of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ father, who passed away before his birth?
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib passed away in Yathrib (Madinah) while returning from a trade journey to Syria before the Prophet ﷺ was born.

questionEn: Which clan did the Prophet's ﷺ mother, Aminah bint Wahb, belong to?
explanationEn: Aminah bint Wahb belonged to Banu Zuhrah, one of the most honorable clans of Quraysh.

questionEn: On which day of the week was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ born, according to his own statement in Sahih Muslim?
explanationEn: When asked about fasting on Mondays, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'That is the day on which I was born and the day on which I received revelation.'

questionEn: Which freedwoman of Abu Lahab was the first woman outside his mother to nurse Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explanationEn: Thuwaybah, the freedwoman of Abu Lahab, nursed the infant Prophet ﷺ for a few days before Halimah al-Sa'diyyah took him.

questionEn: Which companion was a foster-brother to the Prophet ﷺ through Thuwaybah, and later became known as 'The Lion of Allah'?
explanationEn: Both Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Abu Salamah were nursed by Thuwaybah, making them foster-brothers of the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: Why did noble Makkan families send their infants to desert Bedouin wet-nurses like Banu Sa'd?
optionsEn: To hide them from tribal feuds
For pure desert air, healthy growth, and eloquent Arabic speech
To learn desert navigation and camel herding
explanationEn: Makkans sent newborns to the desert so they would grow strong in clean air and master pure, eloquent Arabic away from urban illnesses.

questionEn: Why were the other wet-nurses initially reluctant to take the infant Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: They feared a drought in Banu Sa'd
He was an orphan without a living father to pay a large reward
His clan lived too far from Makkah
explanationEn: Wet-nurses hoped for generous gifts from a child's father, so they passed over the orphan until Halimah took him rather than return empty-handed.

questionEn: What immediate blessing did Halimah al-Sa'diyyah notice after taking the infant Muhammad ﷺ into her care?
optionsEn: Rain fell across all of Makkah
Her flock doubled overnight in number
She found a pouch of silver coins
Her weak she-camel and milk suddenly became abundant
explanationEn: As soon as she held the blessed infant, her milk flowed abundantly and her frail riding beast outpaced the entire caravan home.

questionEn: What extraordinary event (Shaqq al-Sadr) happened to the Prophet ﷺ as a young child living with Banu Sa'd?
optionsEn: An angel taught him to read
A spring gushed out near his tent
Two angels opened his chest and purified his heart with Zamzam water
A cloud shielded him during a storm
explanationEn: Angel Jibril and another angel opened his chest, removed a dark clot, and washed his heart in a golden basin of Zamzam water.

questionEn: At what age did the Prophet's ﷺ mother Aminah bint Wahb pass away?
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ was six years old, Aminah took him to Yathrib to visit his father's grave and relatives, and she passed away on the return journey.

questionEn: At which location between Makkah and Madinah was the Prophet's ﷺ mother Aminah buried?
explanationEn: Aminah fell ill on the journey back from Yathrib and passed away at Abwa, where she was buried.

questionEn: Who faithfully escorted the six-year-old orphaned Prophet ﷺ back to Makkah after Aminah's passing?
explanationEn: Umm Ayman (Barakah al-Habashiyyah), whom the Prophet ﷺ later called 'my mother after my mother,' brought him safely back to Abd al-Muttalib.

questionEn: How old was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ when his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib passed away?
explanationEn: Abd al-Muttalib passed away when the Prophet ﷺ was eight years old, entrusting him to his uncle Abu Talib.

questionEn: Which uncle of the Prophet ﷺ raised him from age eight and stood by him in Makkah for over forty years?
explanationEn: Abu Talib, full brother of Abdullah, loved and protected the Prophet ﷺ dearly, raising him alongside his own children.

questionEn: Who was Abu Talib's wife, who treated the young Prophet ﷺ like her own son and later embraced Islam?
explanationEn: Fatimah bint Asad fed and cared for the young Prophet ﷺ before her own children; he honored her deeply at her funeral in Madinah.

questionEn: What early livelihood did the Prophet ﷺ engage in as a youth to help support Abu Talib's household?
optionsEn: Tending sheep for the people of Makkah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ worked as a shepherd for the people of Makkah for a modest wage, noting that every prophet tended sheep.

questionEn: Which Christian monk in Busra (Syria) recognized signs of prophethood in the twelve-year-old Muhammad ﷺ?
explanationEn: The monk Bahira saw a cloud shading the young caravan traveler and noticed the Seal of Prophethood between his shoulders, advising Abu Talib to guard him.

questionEn: What was the Seal of Prophethood (Khatam al-Nubuwwah) described as looking like on the Prophet's ﷺ back?
optionsEn: A dark ring around his wrist
A white crescent mark on his right hand
A golden birthmark on his forehead
A raised mark like a pigeon's egg between his shoulder blades
explanationEn: Companions described the Seal of Prophethood as a slightly raised mark the size of a pigeon's egg or button between his shoulder blades.

questionEn: What role did the young Prophet ﷺ play during the pre-Islamic Battle of Fijar?
optionsEn: He gathered stray arrows for his uncles without fighting
He served as a truce messenger
explanationEn: As a youth around age fifteen, he attended with his uncles and collected fallen arrows to hand to them.

questionEn: What was the 'Hilf al-Fudul' pact that the Prophet ﷺ attended in his youth and praised even after prophethood?
optionsEn: A treaty dividing the keys of the Kaaba
A trade monopoly agreement with Yemen
An alliance to patrol the Red Sea coast
A chivalrous oath to defend the oppressed and restore rights in Makkah
explanationEn: Hosted at the house of Abdullah ibn Jud'an, Qurayshi clans pledged to stand beside any wronged person in Makkah until his right was restored.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ later say about the Hilf al-Fudul pact after Islam came?
optionsEn: It was replaced by the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah
He would not trade his attendance for red camels and would still answer such a call
It was abrogated by the Hijrah
It only applied to Qurayshi nobles
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ praised the pact's commitment to justice, saying that if invited to a similar covenant in Islam, he would gladly respond.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ earn a living in his twenties before managing Khadijah's trade?
optionsEn: Commerce, trade partnerships, and keeping people's deposits
explanationEn: Known for impeccable honesty, the Prophet ﷺ engaged in trade and guarded valuables entrusted to him by Makkans.

questionEn: What prompted Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA) to invite Muhammad ﷺ to lead her trade caravan to Syria?
optionsEn: She heard of his exceptional truthfulness, trustworthiness, and noble character
Abu Talib owed her a debt
He was the only trader fluent in Greek
He offered the lowest commission fee
explanationEn: Khadijah (RA) heard reports of his integrity as Al-Sadiq Al-Amin and offered him double what she paid other merchants.

questionEn: Which trusted servant of Khadijah (RA) accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the trade journey to Syria and reported his noble conduct?
explanationEn: Maysarah witnessed the Prophet's ﷺ honesty, gentle manners, and extraordinary blessings on the trip, including unprecedented profits.

questionEn: Who acted as the intermediary on Khadijah's (RA) behalf to propose marriage to the Prophet ﷺ?
explanationEn: Nafisah bint Munyah, a close friend of Khadijah (RA), discreetly spoke with Muhammad ﷺ about marrying Khadijah.

questionEn: How old was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ when he married Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA)?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ was 25 years old when he married Khadijah (RA), with whom he shared 25 years of devoted monogamous marriage until her passing.

questionEn: Who was the Prophet's ﷺ firstborn son, from whom he derived his honorific kunyah 'Abu al-Qasim'?
explanationEn: Al-Qasim was his eldest child with Khadijah (RA), giving the Prophet ﷺ the beloved kunyah Abu al-Qasim.

questionEn: Which of the following were the four daughters of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Khadijah (RA)?
optionsEn: Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, and Fatimah
Zaynab, Safiyyah, Umm Kulthum, and Hind
explanationEn: All four daughters of the Prophet ﷺ — Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, and Fatimah — were born to Khadijah (RA).

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ adopt Zayd ibn Harithah before Islam prohibited legal adoption erasing lineage?
optionsEn: He bought and freed him after Khadijah gifted Zayd to him, and Zayd chose to stay
Abu Bakr entrusted Zayd to him
He rescued him during a flood
Zayd was his cousin from Banu Zuhrah
explanationEn: Khadijah gifted Zayd to the Prophet ﷺ; when Zayd's father came to ransom him, Zayd chose the Prophet's ﷺ kindness over returning home.

questionEn: Why did the young Prophet ﷺ take his cousin Ali ibn Abi Talib into his household before prophethood?
optionsEn: Because Ali's mother had moved to Madinah
To ease Abu Talib's financial burden during a severe famine
To send him to trade in Yemen
explanationEn: During a severe drought in Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ and Abbas each took one of Abu Talib's sons; the Prophet ﷺ took Ali and raised him closely.

questionEn: At roughly what age did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ mediate the famous dispute over placing the Black Stone (Hajar al-Aswad)?
explanationEn: Five years before revelation, around age 35, Quraysh rebuilt the Kaaba and nearly went to war over who would set the Black Stone.

questionEn: What agreement did the warring Qurayshi clans make to settle who would place the Black Stone in the rebuilt Kaaba?
optionsEn: To accept the judgment of the very next man to enter the Haram gate
To ask the elder of Banu Abd al-Dar
To wait until the next Hajj season
explanationEn: Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah suggested letting the first person to enter through Bab Banu Shaybah decide—and Muhammad ﷺ walked in.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ brilliantly resolve the Black Stone dispute so every clan shared the honor?
optionsEn: He placed it on a cloak and asked leaders of each clan to hold an edge and lift it together
He let the youngest man lift it alone
He left it on the ground for one year
He rotated it between four tribes
explanationEn: He spread his cloak, placed the Black Stone in the center, had each clan chief lift one corner together, and then he himself set it into the wall.

questionEn: Why did Quraysh leave a semi-circular section (Al-Hijr / Hatim) outside the roofed Kaaba during that reconstruction?
optionsEn: To make space for a well
They ran short of purely halal (lawfully earned) funds
Because Abrahah had claimed that corner
explanationEn: Quraysh vowed to use only lawful money free of usury and injustice, so their funds fell short, leaving the Hatim area enclosed only by a low wall.

questionEn: Before receiving revelation, did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ever worship idols or partake in pagan sacrifices?
optionsEn: Never; Allah protected him from idol worship and pre-Islamic immorality
explanationEn: Even before prophethood, Allah guarded him completely from idolatry, intoxicants, and corrupt practices of Jahiliyyah.

questionEn: What spiritual practice did the pre-Islamic monotheist Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl follow in Makkah?
optionsEn: He rejected idols and sought the pure religion of Ibrahim (AS)
He led the pilgrimage rituals of Hubal
explanationEn: Zayd ibn Amr was one of the Hunafa who shunned idols and awaited a prophet from the line of Ibrahim; the Prophet ﷺ spoke fondly of him.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when the pre-Islamic poet Zayd ibn Amr offered him meat sacrificed to idols?
optionsEn: He refused to eat anything slaughtered for other than Allah
He gave it to Abu Talib
explanationEn: Even before prophethood, Muhammad ﷺ met Zayd at Baldah and declared he did not eat what was slaughtered on pagan stone altars.

questionEn: Who was the Prophet's ﷺ close lifelong friend from Banu Taym before and after prophethood, famous for integrity and genealogy?
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (Abdullah ibn Abi Quhafah) was a respected merchant and close companion of the Prophet ﷺ even prior to revelation.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ begin spending days and nights in solitude (Tahannuth) inside Cave Hira around age 37–40?
optionsEn: To reflect, worship Allah, and seek spiritual clarity away from Makkan idolatry
To guard his sheep from wolves
explanationEn: Love of solitude was placed in his heart, so he provisioned himself and retreated to Cave Hira on Jabal al-Nour for contemplation and devotion.

questionEn: Which way did Cave Hira face from the summit of Jabal al-Nour?
optionsEn: Directly toward the Kaaba in Makkah
explanationEn: From the narrow opening of Cave Hira, one gazes straight toward the Kaaba in the valley of Makkah.

questionEn: Who regularly prepared provisions and brought food to the Prophet ﷺ during his retreats in Cave Hira?
explanationEn: Khadijah (RA) lovingly packed his provisions and even climbed Jabal al-Nour herself to bring him food and comfort.

questionEn: What early sign of approaching prophethood did Muhammad ﷺ experience for six months before Cave Hira?
optionsEn: True dreams (Al-Ru'ya al-Sadiqah) that came to pass like the break of dawn
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) narrated that the commencement of divine inspiration was through true dreams that materialized as clearly as morning light.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe what greeted him on the streets of Makkah just before revelation began?
optionsEn: A stone in Makkah used to greet him with salam before he was sent
The doors of the Kaaba opened automatically
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told his companions: 'I know a stone in Makkah that used to greet me with peace before I was commissioned as a prophet.'

questionEn: Which tribe of Makkah originally settled around Zamzam through Hajar and Ismail (AS), from whom the Prophet's ﷺ lineage traces?
explanationEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a direct descendant of Prophet Ismail (AS) through Adnan, whose descendants lived in Makkah after Jurhum.

questionEn: Who was the Prophet's ﷺ ancestor who united the clans of Quraysh and settled them inside the valley of Makkah around the Kaaba?
explanationEn: Qusayy ibn Kilab gathered the scattered clans of Quraysh into Makkah, established Dar al-Nadwah, and organized the guardianship of the Kaaba.

questionEn: What civic council hall near the Kaaba was built by Qusayy ibn Kilab where Makkan leaders later plotted against the Prophet ﷺ?
explanationEn: Dar al-Nadwah was Quraysh's assembly house for major treaties, marriages, and civic decisions—later the site where they plotted his assassination.

questionEn: Which well did Abd al-Muttalib rediscover and excavate in Makkah after seeing a guiding dream?
explanationEn: The well of Zamzam had been buried for centuries since Jurhum left Makkah until Allah guided Abd al-Muttalib in a dream to unearth it.

questionEn: What vow did Abd al-Muttalib make while digging Zamzam that nearly led to sacrificing his son Abdullah?
optionsEn: If granted ten sons to protect him, he would sacrifice one at the Kaaba
To build a golden door for the Kaaba
explanationEn: When Abd al-Muttalib later had ten sons and drew lots, Abdullah was chosen; advisers counseled him to draw lots between Abdullah and camels until 100 camels were ransomed.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ refer to himself as 'the son of the two who were ransomed from sacrifice'?
optionsEn: Referring to Ismail (AS) and his father Abdullah
Referring to Ishaq (AS) and Abd al-Muttalib
Referring to Musa (AS) and Abu Talib
explanationEn: Prophet Ismail (AS) was ransomed by a great ram, and Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib was ransomed by one hundred camels.

questionEn: Where was Abdullah, father of the Prophet ﷺ, visiting when he fell fatally ill?
optionsEn: His maternal uncles from Banu al-Najjar in Yathrib
explanationEn: Abdullah fell ill on his return from Gaza/Syria and passed away among his maternal relatives of Banu Adi ibn al-Najjar in Yathrib.

questionEn: Who named the newborn Prophet 'Muhammad' ﷺ, hoping he would be praised in heaven and on earth?
explanationEn: Abd al-Muttalib carried his grandson into the Kaaba, thanked Allah, and named him Muhammad ('the Praised One'), a name rare among Arabs then.

questionEn: Which foster-sister of the Prophet ﷺ from Banu Sa'd helped carry him on her hip in infancy and later met him respectfully at Hunayn?
explanationEn: Al-Shayma, daughter of Halimah al-Sa'diyyah, cared for the infant Prophet ﷺ; years later after Hunayn, he spread his cloak for her in honor.

questionEn: How long did the young Prophet ﷺ stay with Halimah al-Sa'diyyah before she returned him permanently to Aminah?
explanationEn: After two years of nursing, Halimah asked Aminah to keep him longer due to blessings and fear of Makkan epidemics, returning him around age four or five after Shaqq al-Sadr.

questionEn: How did Abd al-Muttalib show special affection for the orphaned young Muhammad ﷺ inside the Haram?
optionsEn: He forbade him from leaving the house
He allowed only Muhammad ﷺ to sit with him on his special carpet beside the Kaaba
He gave him the keys of Dar al-Nadwah
He sent him to live in Ta'if
explanationEn: None of Abd al-Muttalib's sons dared sit on his shaded mat near the Kaaba, yet when little Muhammad ﷺ sat there, Abd al-Muttalib stroked his back and said, 'Leave my son, for he has a great destiny.'

questionEn: What did Abu Talib notice about his family's food whenever the young Prophet ﷺ ate with them?
optionsEn: They needed extra bread every night
Everyone ate until full and food still remained, whereas without him they were hungry
He only ate dates and milk
explanationEn: Abu Talib's household experienced clear barakah whenever the Prophet ﷺ sat at the meal, so Abu Talib used to say 'Wait until my son comes.'

questionEn: During a severe drought in Makkah, how did Allah send rain when Abu Talib held the young Prophet ﷺ beside the Kaaba?
optionsEn: He sacrificed ten camels on Mount Safa
He stood facing the Kaaba holding the young boy's face toward the sky and asked for rain
He poured Zamzam on the sand
He blew a horn from Dar al-Nadwah
explanationEn: Abu Talib leaned his back against the Kaaba holding the child Muhammad ﷺ; clouds gathered swiftly and rain poured down, revivifying the valley.

questionEn: Who was the cousin of Khadijah (RA) who had embraced Christianity and studied Hebrew scripture in Makkah?
explanationEn: Waraqah ibn Nawfal was an elderly scholar of previous scriptures who later confirmed that the angel who came to Muhammad ﷺ was the same Namus sent to Musa (AS).

questionEn: What dowry (Mahr) did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give Khadijah (RA) upon their marriage?
explanationEn: According to historical Seerah reports, Abu Talib delivered the marriage sermon and the Prophet ﷺ gave Khadijah (RA) a dowry of twenty young camels.

questionEn: Which future Caliph and son-in-law of the Prophet ﷺ married his daughter Ruqayyah (and later Umm Kulthum)?
explanationEn: Uthman ibn Affan (RA) married Ruqayyah and, after her passing, Umm Kulthum, earning the unique title Dhun-Nurayn (Possessor of Two Lights).

questionEn: Which cousin of the Prophet ﷺ married his eldest daughter Zaynab before Islam and later accepted Islam in Madinah?
explanationEn: Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi', Khadijah's nephew, was praised by the Prophet ﷺ for his honesty and faithfulness in marriage, and he later embraced Islam.

questionEn: Who was the second son born to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Khadijah (RA) in Makkah, also known by the titles al-Tayyib and al-Tahir?
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Muhammad was born after Al-Qasim and passed away in infancy; both sons passed away young as a test of patience for the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: Which trade partner of the Prophet ﷺ before Islam testified that Muhammad ﷺ never quarreled or cheated in business?
explanationEn: Al-Sa'ib ibn Abi al-Sa'ib was his pre-Islamic business partner; the Prophet ﷺ welcomed him warmly years later, saying he was an honest partner who never wrangled.

questionEn: Why did Quraysh decide to demolish and rebuild the walls of the Kaaba around 605 CE?
optionsEn: To expand it toward Mount Safa
Its low walls had weakened from flash floods and a theft of its interior treasures
explanationEn: Heavy Makkan torrents cracked the old dry-stone walls, and thieves had climbed the low unroofed structure to steal sacred offerings inside.

questionEn: During the rebuilding of the Kaaba, what happened when young Muhammad ﷺ removed his lower garment to pad his shoulder while carrying stones?
optionsEn: He fainted until his garment was tied back on, showing Allah guarded his modesty
He dropped a stone on his foot
He decided to leave the Haram
explanationEn: When his uncle Abbas suggested using his waist-wrapper as a shoulder pad, he fainted and called out 'My waist-wrapper!'—from then on he never exposed his awrah.

questionEn: Which Qurayshi elder stepped forward with a pickaxe first to begin dismantling the Kaaba's cracked wall after Quraysh feared divine wrath?
explanationEn: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah prayed 'O Allah, we intend only good,' struck the corner, and when nothing harmed him overnight, the people joined the reconstruction.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ earn the deep trust of Makkans even during intense later opposition to his message?
optionsEn: Even his enemies kept their money and valuables entrusted with him for safekeeping
By paying tribute to Dar al-Nadwah
explanationEn: So trusted was Al-Amin that on the very night of Hijrah, he left Ali (RA) behind specifically to return the deposits entrusted to him by Makkans.

questionEn: Which mountain located in Makkah holds Ghar Hira where the Prophet ﷺ used to retreat in worship?
explanationEn: Jabal al-Nour (Mountain of Light) rises northeast of Masjid al-Haram and houses Cave Hira near its peak.

questionEn: What annual pre-Islamic trade and literary gathering near Makkah did the young Prophet ﷺ attend where tribes exchanged goods and poetry?
explanationEn: Souq Ukaz, held between Makkah and Ta'if during the sacred months, was Arabia's premier fair; later the Prophet ﷺ also preached Islam to tribes there.

questionEn: In which season did Quraysh conduct their winter caravan journey mentioned in Surah Quraysh?
explanationEn: Quraysh traveled south to Yemen in winter for warmth and spice/leather goods, and north to Syria in summer.

questionEn: Which ancestor of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ originally established the two seasonal trade journeys to Yemen and Syria?
explanationEn: Hashim secured trade covenants with neighboring rulers, launching Quraysh's famous winter journey to Yemen and summer journey to Syria.

questionEn: Which aunt of the Prophet ﷺ was renowned for her courage, poetry, and devotion, and was the mother of Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam?
explanationEn: Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib embraced Islam early, migrated to Madinah, and displayed remarkable bravery during the Battle of the Trench.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ demonstrate respect for Halimah al-Sa'diyyah when she visited him years after his marriage to Khadijah (RA)?
optionsEn: He asked her to stay in Cave Hira
He introduced her to Dar al-Nadwah
He rose to welcome her, spread his cloak for her to sit, and gave her forty sheep and a camel
explanationEn: During a drought, Halimah visited Makkah; the Prophet ﷺ and Khadijah (RA) honored her warmly and sent her back with abundant livestock.

questionEn: Which Ethiopian woman who raised the Prophet ﷺ after Aminah passed away did he later arrange to marry Zayd ibn Harithah?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said whoever wished to marry a woman of Paradise should marry Umm Ayman; Zayd married her, and their son was Usamah ibn Zayd.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ ask Allah to forgive his mother Aminah's people and recall her tenderly when visiting Abwa decades later?
optionsEn: Out of deep filial love for the mother who bore and cared for him in early childhood
To build a fortress at Abwa
explanationEn: When permitted to visit her grave at Abwa, the Prophet ﷺ wept deeply, moving all the companions around him to tears.

questionEn: What did the Quraysh call the famous pre-Islamic feast and treaty at Abdullah ibn Jud'an's home where Muhammad ﷺ pledged to uphold justice?
explanationEn: Hilf al-Fudul was sparked when a Yemeni merchant from Zubayd was cheated in Makkah by al-As ibn Wa'il and cried out for help near the Kaaba.

questionEn: Which Yemeni merchant's mistreatment in Makkah prompted the formation of Hilf al-Fudul?
optionsEn: A merchant from Zubayd cheated by al-As ibn Wa'il
explanationEn: A man from Zubayd sold goods to al-As ibn Wa'il, who withheld payment; after he appealed at Mount Abu Qubays, Banu Hashim and allied clans formed Hilf al-Fudul.

questionEn: What distinctive practice of Quraysh did the Prophet ﷺ refuse to imitate at Arafah before Islam, standing instead with all other people at Arafah?
optionsEn: The Hums custom of stopping at Muzdalifah instead of going out to Arafah
explanationEn: Quraysh (calling themselves al-Hums) claimed superiority by stopping at Muzdalifah during Hajj, whereas Allah guided Muhammad ﷺ to stand at Arafah even before prophethood.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ later say 'Every prophet Allah sent tended sheep' when asked if he had shepherded?
optionsEn: To highlight that shepherding nurtures patience, vigilance, and compassion for leading people
Because sheep were the only livestock in Arabia
Because agriculture was forbidden in Makkah
explanationEn: Tending weak and scattered sheep trains a leader in gentleness, attentiveness, and responsibility—qualities vital to guiding humanity.

questionEn: How much did the Prophet ﷺ say he was paid when tending sheep for the people of Makkah?
explanationEn: With humility, the Prophet ﷺ told his companions he tended Makkans' sheep for 'qararit' (small fractional coins).

questionEn: Which two rivers or landmarks did the Prophet ﷺ NOT visit during his childhood, unlike the coastal trade route?
explanationEn: In youth he traveled from Makkah to Yathrib (with Aminah) and Busra in Syria (with Abu Talib and later for Khadijah), never to Rome or Constantinople.

questionEn: What did Khadijah (RA) famously seek from Muhammad ﷺ upon his profitable and blessed return from Syria?
optionsEn: A permanent trade office in Damascus
Marriage, recognizing his unmatched nobility and honesty
explanationEn: Despite rejecting wealthy Qurayshi suitors, Khadijah (RA) chose Muhammad ﷺ for his character, lineage, and truthfulness.

questionEn: Who spoke on behalf of the Prophet ﷺ to ask for Khadijah's (RA) hand and deliver the marriage khutbah?
explanationEn: Abu Talib accompanied his nephew to Khadijah's family and delivered an eloquent sermon praising Muhammad's ﷺ unmatched character.

questionEn: Who acted as Khadijah's (RA) guardian (wali) at her marriage to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Her uncle Amr ibn Asad (or brother in some reports)
explanationEn: Her father Khuwaylid had passed away earlier, so her uncle Amr ibn Asad acted as her guardian at the marriage ceremony.

questionEn: Which house in Makkah became the blessed home where the Prophet ﷺ and Khadijah (RA) lived and raised their daughters?
optionsEn: Khadijah's home near the Marwah / Suq al-Layl quarter
explanationEn: After marriage, the Prophet ﷺ moved into Khadijah's home in Makkah, where revelation later visited him and his daughters grew up.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ describe his love for Khadijah (RA) years after her passing?
optionsEn: 'She was merely a helper in Makkah'
'I was blessed with her love (Ruziqtu hubbaha)'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ openly cherished Khadijah's memory, saying 'Indeed I have been provided with her love,' and always honored her friends.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ warn Maysarah and Abu Talib after Bahira's warning in Busra?
optionsEn: The prices of silk had collapsed
There was a plague in Busra
Bahira warned that hostile people of scripture might recognize and harm the boy
explanationEn: Bahira urged Abu Talib to send the young Muhammad ﷺ back to Makkah lest envious scholars recognize the signs of the final prophet and harm him.

questionEn: Before Islam, which brother of the Prophet's ﷺ father was the youngest and closest to him in age, later becoming a fearless champion of Islam?
explanationEn: Hamzah was only a couple of years older than the Prophet ﷺ, shared a foster-mother (Thuwaybah) with him, and became a pillar of strength in Makkah.

questionEn: Which two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ were initially betrothed before revelation to two sons of his uncle Abu Lahab?
explanationEn: Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum were betrothed to Utbah and Utaybah, sons of Abu Lahab, who later divorced them out of hostility after Surah Al-Masad was revealed.

questionEn: What special status did Abd al-Muttalib's family hold in relation to the pilgrimage before Islam?
optionsEn: Guardians of the Kaaba's outer wall
Judges of the Ukaz poetry contest
Custodians of Zamzam and hosts supplying water to pilgrims
explanationEn: Serving pilgrims with Zamzam water (Siqayah) was an honor passed from Abd al-Muttalib to his son Al-Abbas, and confirmed by the Prophet ﷺ after the Conquest of Makkah.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ act when young men of Makkah invited him twice to attend nighttime wedding festivities before prophethood?
optionsEn: Allah caused him to fall deeply asleep until morning both times, protecting his purity
He refused to leave Cave Hira
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ narrated that twice in youth he intended to watch evening gatherings, and each time Allah cast deep sleep over him until sunrise, preserving him from Jahiliyyah.

questionEn: What did the name 'Ahmad', by which Prophet Isa (AS) foretold Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, signify?
optionsEn: The most praiseworthy / one who praises Allah most
explanationEn: In Surah Al-Saff (61:6), Isa (AS) gave glad tidings of a messenger to come after him named Ahmad, sharing the same root of praise as Muhammad ﷺ.

questionEn: Which phrase best summarizes the moral reputation of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ among Quraysh for 40 years prior to revelation?
explanationEn: For four decades before prophethood, everyone in Makkah knew him as Al-Sadiq Al-Amin—providing undeniable proof of his integrity when he proclaimed Islam.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Tafsir); Seerah Ibn Hisham

questionEn: During which blessed month of the Islamic calendar did the first revelation descend upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Cave Hira?
explanationEn: The Qur'an began its revelation in Ramadan, on the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), while the Prophet ﷺ was in devotion at Cave Hira.

questionEn: Which angel descended into Cave Hira to deliver the first verses of the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explanationEn: Angel Jibril (Al-Ruh al-Amin) brought the revelation from Allah to the Prophet ﷺ in Cave Hira.

questionEn: What was the very first command Angel Jibril (AS) spoke to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Cave Hira?
explanationEn: Jibril commanded 'Iqra'' (Read/Recite), and when the Prophet ﷺ replied 'I am not a reader,' the angel embraced him tightly three times before revealing Surah Al-Alaq.

questionEn: Which Surah's opening five verses constituted the very first Qur'anic revelation?
explanationEn: The opening five verses of Surah Al-Alaq (96:1-5) — 'Read in the name of your Lord who created' — were the first verses revealed.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Bad' al-Wahy); Surah Al-Alaq 96:1-5

questionEn: How many times did Angel Jibril (AS) press Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tightly in Cave Hira before releasing him to recite Surah Al-Alaq?
explanationEn: Jibril pressed him three times until his strength was exhausted, then released him and recited the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq.

questionEn: To whom did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ immediately hurry home trembling after the first encounter in Cave Hira?
explanationEn: With his heart trembling, he returned straight to Khadijah (RA) and cried, 'Zammiluni, zammiluni!' ('Cover me, cover me!').

questionEn: How did Khadijah (RA) immediately reassure the Prophet ﷺ when he feared for himself after Cave Hira?
optionsEn: She suggested consulting the elders of Dar al-Nadwah
She urged him to abandon Cave Hira
She affirmed that Allah would never disgrace him because he upholds kinship, helps the needy, honors guests, and aids the distressed
She told him to leave Makkah that night
explanationEn: Khadijah (RA) pointed to his spotless moral character—honoring ties, bearing burdens for the weak, hosting guests, and assisting in hardships—as proof Allah would never abandon him.

questionEn: What did Waraqah ibn Nawfal tell Prophet Muhammad ﷺ when he heard the account of Cave Hira?
optionsEn: That he should stop reciting in Makkah
That he should travel to Jerusalem immediately
That this was the Namus (Jibril) Allah sent to Musa (AS), and he wished he could live to support him when his people expel him
That it was merely a passing dream
explanationEn: Waraqah recognized the angelic revelation as the same Namus revealed to Moses (AS) and foretold that Quraysh would drive him out.

questionEn: Why was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ astonished when Waraqah said, 'When your people drive you out'?
optionsEn: Because he owned no house in Makkah
Because Makkans loved and trusted him as Al-Sadiq Al-Amin
Because he planned to move to Ta'if anyway
explanationEn: He asked in surprise, 'Will they really drive me out?'—knowing how deeply Makkans respected his trustworthiness until then.

questionEn: What period followed the first revelation in Cave Hira before Jibril returned with the next verses?
optionsEn: Fatrat al-Wahy (a temporary pause in revelation)
explanationEn: There was a brief pause in revelation (Fatrat al-Wahy) during which the Prophet ﷺ longed deeply for Jibril's return.

questionEn: Which Surah was revealed right after the pause in revelation when the Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril seated on a throne between heaven and earth and returned saying 'Cover me'?
explanationEn: Allah revealed the opening of Surah Al-Muddaththir (74:1-5): 'O you who covers himself, arise and warn, and glorify your Lord!'

questionEn: Which Surah reassured the Prophet ﷺ during a pause in revelation with the words, 'Your Lord has neither forsaken you nor is He displeased'?
explanationEn: Surah Al-Duha (93:1-3) comforted the Prophet ﷺ when mockers claimed his Lord had abandoned him.

questionEn: Which Surah taught the Prophet ﷺ to stand in night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl) in preparation for the heavy message of prophethood?
explanationEn: Surah Al-Muzzammil (73:1-5) commanded him to stand in prayer most of the night because Allah would cast upon him 'a weighty Word.'

questionEn: Who was the very first person on earth to believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and accept Islam?
explanationEn: Khadijah (RA) believed immediately without a moment's hesitation, standing as the first Muslim and Mother of the Believers.

questionEn: Who was the first grown free man to embrace Islam without any hesitation?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ remarked that everyone else showed a moment of hesitation except Abu Bakr (RA), who accepted Islam immediately.

questionEn: Who was the first youth/child to embrace Islam while living in the Prophet's ﷺ own household?
explanationEn: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA), then around ten years old, saw the Prophet ﷺ and Khadijah praying and embraced Islam on the spot.

questionEn: Who was the first freedman/servant to accept Islam at the dawn of the Makkan call?
explanationEn: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA), known lovingly inside the Prophet's household, was among the earliest four Muslims alongside Khadijah, Abu Bakr, and Ali.

questionEn: How did Angel Jibril (AS) first teach Prophet Muhammad ﷺ how to perform wudu and Salah?
optionsEn: Jibril struck the earth beside Makkah causing a spring to gush, performed wudu, and led him in prayer
explanationEn: In early Makkah, Jibril (AS) struck the valley ground to bring forth water, demonstrated wudu step by step, and prayed while the Prophet ﷺ followed, who then taught Khadijah (RA).

questionEn: Before the five daily prayers were prescribed during Al-Isra wal-Mi'raj, what regular prayer times did early Muslims observe in Makkah?
optionsEn: Two units (rak'ahs) in the morning and two units in the evening
explanationEn: During the early Makkan phase, the Prophet ﷺ and early Muslims prayed two rak'ahs at dawn and two in the late afternoon, in addition to night prayer.

questionEn: Which early companion brought five of the Ten Promised Paradise into Islam through his quiet, trusted invitations?
explanationEn: Through Abu Bakr's (RA) immediate da'wah, Uthman ibn Affan, al-Zubayr, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, and Talhah ibn Ubaydullah accepted Islam.

questionEn: Approximately how long did the discreet, private phase of calling to Islam in Makkah last before public proclamation?
explanationEn: For the first three years, the Prophet ﷺ invited trusted individuals discreetly while teaching them revelation in private gatherings.

questionEn: Why was Dar al-Arqam chosen as the secret educational center for early Muslims in Makkah?
optionsEn: It was guarded by Roman soldiers
It was next to Dar al-Nadwah
Al-Arqam was young and from Banu Makhzum (rival to Banu Hashim), so Quraysh did not suspect his home near Safa
explanationEn: Situated on the slope of Mount Safa, al-Arqam's home allowed the Prophet ﷺ to teach converts away from Quraysh's eyes.

questionEn: Who was the first person to recite the Qur'an aloud publicly before Quraysh leaders at the Kaaba after the Prophet ﷺ?
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) stood at Maqam Ibrahim and recited Surah Al-Rahman aloud; though beaten by Quraysh, he repeated it the next day with courage.

questionEn: Which verse signaled the Prophet ﷺ to begin calling his closest kinsmen first before addressing all of Makkah?
explanationEn: Allah commanded in Surah Al-Shu'ara (26:214): 'And warn, O Muhammad, your closest kindred,' prompting him to gather Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib.

questionEn: Upon which hill beside the Kaaba did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ climb to proclaim Islam openly to all the clans of Quraysh?
explanationEn: He ascended Mount Safa and called out the clans by name, asking if they would believe him if he warned of an army behind the hill—to which they replied, 'We have only ever known truth from you.'

questionEn: Which uncle of the Prophet ﷺ shouted 'May you perish! Did you gather us only for this?' at Mount Safa, prompting the revelation of Surah Al-Masad?
explanationEn: Abu Lahab publicly cursed the Prophet ﷺ at Safa, upon which Allah revealed Surah Al-Masad (111) condemning Abu Lahab and his wife Umm Jamil.

questionEn: Which Qurayshi verse ordered the Prophet ﷺ to declare the message openly and turn away from the polytheists?
optionsEn: 'Proclaim openly what you are commanded' (Surah Al-Hijr 15:94)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hijr 15:94 ('Fasda' bima tu'mar') marked the transition to open, public preaching throughout Makkah.

questionEn: Why did Abu Lahab's wife, Umm Jamil (Arwa bint Harb), earn the Qur'anic description 'carrier of firewood'?
optionsEn: She built fires inside the Kaaba
She sold timber in Souq Ukaz
She scattered thorny branches along the Prophet's ﷺ path at night and fueled slander
explanationEn: Umm Jamil placed bundles of thorns on the Prophet's ﷺ doorstep and spread malicious gossip against him.

questionEn: Which direction did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ face when performing Salah beside the Kaaba during the Makkan period?
optionsEn: Facing north so both the Kaaba and Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) were aligned before him
explanationEn: While in Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ stood between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone so he faced both the Kaaba and Jerusalem simultaneously.

questionEn: Who was the first person to shed blood in defense of Islam in Makkah when polytheists harassed praying Muslims in a narrow valley?
explanationEn: When idolaters mocked and attacked the early Muslims praying in a Makkan ravine, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) struck one of the attackers with a camel's jawbone.

questionEn: What cruel act did Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt commit while the Prophet ﷺ was in sujud (prostration) beside the Kaaba?
optionsEn: He tore his cloak in half
He threw stones from Mount Safa
He dumped the filthy entrails of a slaughtered camel onto the Prophet's ﷺ back
explanationEn: At Abu Jahl's instigation, Uqbah placed heavy camel entrails upon the Prophet's ﷺ back in prostration until his young daughter Fatimah (RA) came weeping to remove them.

questionEn: Which companion rescued the Prophet ﷺ when Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt tried to strangle him with a twisted cloth near the Kaaba?
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA) rushed forward, pushed Uqbah away, and cried out in the words of Qur'an: 'Would you kill a man merely because he says, My Lord is Allah?'

questionEn: Which Makkan noble was famously nicknamed 'Father of Wisdom' by his clan but earned the title 'Abu Jahl' (Father of Ignorance) for his fierce hostility to Islam?
explanationEn: Amr ibn Hisham of Banu Makhzum was called Abul-Hakam before Islam, but his obstinate rejection of clear truth earned him the title Abu Jahl.

questionEn: What eloquent confession did the pagan scholar al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah privately make after listening to the Prophet ﷺ recite the Qur'an?
optionsEn: That it has a sweetness, beauty, and towering truth unlike poetry or soothsaying
That it sounded like ordinary Bedouin song
That he had written similar verses
That it was copied from Persian stories
explanationEn: Al-Walid admitted the Qur'an's unmatched majesty, yet out of pride he yielded to Abu Jahl and falsely labeled it 'borrowed magic,' as described in Surah Al-Muddaththir.

questionEn: What did Quraysh leaders propose when they visited Abu Talib offering to adopt a replacement son?
optionsEn: They offered to pay Abu Talib's debts
They offered Umarah ibn al-Walid, the handsomest youth of Quraysh, in exchange for handing over Muhammad ﷺ to be killed
They offered to share the keys of the Kaaba
They asked Abu Talib to move to Ta'if
explanationEn: Abu Talib rebuked their absurd offer, saying, 'Would you give me your son to feed while I give you mine to kill? By Allah, that will never be!'

questionEn: What stirring reply did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give Abu Talib when his uncle felt overwhelmed by Quraysh pressure?
optionsEn: 'I will pause preaching for a year'
'Even if they put the sun in my right hand and the moon in my left, I will not abandon this mission until Allah makes it prevail or I perish in it'
'Ask Quraysh for half the trade profits'
explanationEn: With tears in his eyes, the Prophet ﷺ affirmed total commitment to Allah's message, moving Abu Talib to vow lifelong protection.

questionEn: What tempting offer did Utbah ibn Rabi'ah bring to the Prophet ﷺ on behalf of Quraysh to stop his preaching?
optionsEn: Money, kingship, the finest marriage, or treatment for any illness
explanationEn: Utbah offered wealth, sovereignty, or medical cure if he would stop criticizing their idols; in reply, the Prophet ﷺ calmly recited Surah Fussilat (41:1-38).

questionEn: Which Makkan master tortured Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) under the scorching midday sun with a heavy boulder on his chest?
explanationEn: Umayyah ibn Khalaf dragged Bilal onto burning Makkan gravel with a rock on his chest, yet Bilal repeated only 'Ahad! Ahad!' (One! One!).

questionEn: Who purchased Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) from Umayyah ibn Khalaf and set him free for the sake of Allah?
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA) bought Bilal's freedom at a high price (and freed several other persecuted enslaved Muslims including Amir ibn Fuhayrah and Umm Ubays).

questionEn: Who was the very first martyr (Shahidah) in the history of Islam, killed by Abu Jahl in Makkah?
explanationEn: Sumayyah (RA), mother of Ammar ibn Yasir, refused to renounce Islam under brutal torture and was martyred by Abu Jahl's spear.

questionEn: What comforting promise did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ call out as he passed the tortured family of Yasir in Makkah?
optionsEn: 'Patience, O family of Yasir! Your appointed meeting place is Paradise'
'Tomorrow an army will arrive from Yemen'
explanationEn: Unable to halt the torture physically at that stage, the Prophet ﷺ uplifted their hearts with the glad tidings of Jannah.

questionEn: What Qur'anic concession was revealed after Ammar ibn Yasir (RA) uttered words of disbelief under unbearable torture while his heart remained firm in faith?
optionsEn: Permission to fight inside the Kaaba
Exemption for one coerced by force while his heart rests secure in faith (Surah Al-Nahl 16:106)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ wiped Ammar's tears and asked how his heart felt; hearing it was tranquil with Iman, Allah revealed Surah Al-Nahl 16:106.

questionEn: Which persecuted blacksmith companion was pressed onto burning coals in Makkah until the fat of his back extinguished the fire?
explanationEn: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (RA) endured horrific torture by Umm Anmar and later showed his scarred back during Umar's caliphate.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ answer Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (RA) when Khabbab asked him to pray for immediate victory amidst severe Makkan torture?
optionsEn: He reminded him that earlier believers were combed with iron combs and sawed in half yet never abandoned faith, and promised Islam would spread safely from Sanaa to Hadramawt
He told him to stop teaching Qur'an
He commanded an immediate night raid
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ acknowledged their pain while teaching steadfast patience, foretelling complete security for travelers fearing none but Allah.

questionEn: Which distant tribe's companion traveled to Makkah after hearing of the Prophet ﷺ, declared Islam publicly beside the Kaaba, and was beaten until Abbas intervened?
explanationEn: Abu Dharr of Banu Ghifar loudly proclaimed the Shahadah in the Masjid al-Haram; Abbas protected him by reminding Quraysh that their caravans passed Ghifar territory.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise vulnerable Muslims in the fifth year of prophethood to migrate to Abyssinia (Al-Habashah)?
optionsEn: Because Madinah had closed its borders
Because there was a righteous Christian king (Al-Najashi) under whom no one was wronged
explanationEn: Seeking religious freedom from persecution, the Prophet ﷺ directed companions across the Red Sea to the just king Negus (Ashamah al-Najashi).

questionEn: Which daughter of the Prophet ﷺ and her husband Uthman ibn Affan (RA) were among the first emigrants to Abyssinia?
explanationEn: Uthman ibn Affan and Ruqayyah (RA) led the first emigration to Abyssinia; the Prophet ﷺ said Uthman was the first to migrate with his family after Prophet Lut (AS).

questionEn: Which two Qurayshi envoys pursued the Muslim emigrants to Abyssinia bearing leather gifts to bribe the Negus into extraditing them?
optionsEn: Abu Sufyan and Khalid ibn al-Walid
Amr ibn al-As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah
explanationEn: Quraysh dispatched Amr ibn al-As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah with fine Makkan leather gifts for the Negus's bishops and court.

questionEn: Who acted as the eloquent spokesperson for the Muslim refugees before King Negus in Abyssinia?
explanationEn: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (RA), cousin of the Prophet ﷺ, delivered a timeless speech contrasting the darkness of Jahiliyyah with the mercy and justice of Islam.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic passage did Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (RA) recite before King Negus, moving the king and his bishops to tears?
optionsEn: The opening of Surah Maryam (about Prophet Isa and Maryam)
explanationEn: Ja'far recited the opening verses of Surah Maryam (19); Negus wept, drew a line on the ground, and declared that the difference between this and what Isa (AS) brought was not even the width of a stick.

questionEn: What did King Negus refuse to accept from the Qurayshi envoys after hearing Ja'far's speech and Surah Maryam?
optionsEn: He refused to hand over the Muslims even for a mountain of gold, and returned Quraysh's gifts
He exiled the Muslims to Yemen
He asked the Muslims to stay only three days
He demanded a treaty with Abu Talib
explanationEn: Negus shielded the Muslims in full security, returned the envoys' gifts, and later embraced Islam secretly before passing away in Madinah's era, when the Prophet ﷺ prayed Salatul-Gha'ib for him.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Jana'iz); Seerah Ibn Hisham

questionEn: Why did some emigrants in Abyssinia briefly return to Makkah before a second larger migration there?
optionsEn: False rumors reached them that all of Quraysh had embraced Islam
explanationEn: Hearing that Quraysh prostrated when the Prophet ﷺ recited Surah Al-Najm, emigrants thought Makkah had accepted Islam; upon nearing Makkah they learned persecution had intensified, leading to the second Abyssinian migration.

questionEn: Which Surah's final verse caused even the polytheists in Makkah to fall into prostration in awe when the Prophet ﷺ recited it publicly at the Kaaba?
explanationEn: Overwhelmed by the majestic cadence and power of Surah Al-Najm ending in 'So prostrate to Allah and worship Him!' (53:62), everyone present—believers and idolaters alike—fell in prostration.

questionEn: Who was the first prominent warrior of Banu Hashim to embrace Islam openly after hearing that Abu Jahl had insulted the Prophet ﷺ near Safa?
explanationEn: Returning from a hunt and informed by a freedwoman of Abu Jahl's abuse, Hamzah struck Abu Jahl with his bow and declared his Islam openly, becoming a mighty shield for the Muslims.

questionEn: What specific du'a did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ make regarding Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) shortly before Umar accepted Islam?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, strengthen Islam with the more beloved of these two men to You: Abu Jahl or Umar ibn al-Khattab'
'O Allah, let Umar guard Cave Hira'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for Allah to honor Islam through either Umar or Amr ibn Hisham, and Allah answered through Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA).

questionEn: Where was Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) heading with his drawn sword on the day he embraced Islam?
optionsEn: To Dar al-Arqam intending to kill the Prophet ﷺ
explanationEn: Along the way, Nu'aym ibn Abdullah informed Umar that his own sister Fatimah and brother-in-law Sa'id ibn Zayd had already accepted Islam.

questionEn: Which companion was teaching Surah Ta-Ha to Umar's sister Fatimah and her husband Sa'id ibn Zayd when Umar knocked on their door?
explanationEn: Khabbab hid while Fatimah concealed the parchment; after striking them and seeing Fatimah's blood and steadfastness, Umar asked to read the Surah and his heart softened instantly.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic passage touched Umar ibn al-Khattab's (RA) heart so deeply that he asked to be taken immediately to the Prophet ﷺ at Dar al-Arqam?
optionsEn: The opening verses of Surah Ta-Ha (20:1-14)
explanationEn: Reading 'Indeed, I am Allah; there is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance' (20:14), Umar exclaimed how noble those words were and went straight to Dar al-Arqam.

questionEn: What immediate public change occurred for Muslims in Makkah right after Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) embraced Islam?
optionsEn: They built a second mosque near Mina
Abu Jahl resigned from Dar al-Nadwah
They marched in two rows led by Hamzah and Umar to pray openly inside Masjid al-Haram
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud (RA) remarked that Islam remained unable to pray openly at the Kaaba until Umar accepted Islam, earning him the title Al-Faruq.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ bestow the title 'Al-Faruq' upon Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)?
optionsEn: Because he was a skilled navigator
Because he led the first caravan to Syria
Because through him Allah clearly distinguished truth from falsehood
explanationEn: Al-Faruq means 'The Criterion / Distinguisher between truth and falsehood,' reflecting how Umar's conversion and clarity strengthened public truth.

questionEn: Which chieftain of Banu Daws visited Makkah, plugged his ears with cotton at Quraysh's warning, then listened to the Prophet ﷺ and carried Islam back to his entire tribe?
explanationEn: Al-Tufayl reasoned that as a wise poet he could judge for himself, followed the Prophet ﷺ home, heard the Qur'an, accepted Islam, and later brought Banu Daws (including Abu Hurayrah) to Islam.

questionEn: How did Quraysh try to warn visiting Arab pilgrims during Hajj season against listening to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: By stationing men on mountain passes to slander him as a poet, sorcerer, or madman—ironically spreading his name across all Arabia
explanationEn: Under al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah's advice, Quraysh agreed to uniformly label him a 'sorcerer who separates families,' which unintentionally aroused pilgrims' curiosity to seek him out.

questionEn: Which Makkan healer from Yemen, Dhimad al-Azdi, came to 'cure' the Prophet ﷺ of supposed possession and instead embraced Islam on the spot?
optionsEn: After witnessing water flow from his fingers
Upon hearing the Prophet's ﷺ opening khutbah praising Allah, he exclaimed such words surpass poetry and sorcery
explanationEn: Hearing the eloquent opening praise of the Khutbat al-Hajah ('Inna al-hamdu lillah...'), Dhimad asked him to repeat it three times and immediately pledged allegiance to Islam.

questionEn: What compromise did Quraysh leaders propose to the Prophet ﷺ—worshiping Allah for a year if he would worship their idols for a year—prompting the revelation of Surah Al-Kafirun?
optionsEn: Moving the Black Stone to Dar al-Nadwah
A rotational syncretism deal rejected completely by 'To you be your religion, and to me my religion'
explanationEn: Allah revealed Surah Al-Kafirun (109) drawing an uncompromising boundary of pure monotheism (Tawhid) against all polytheistic compromise.

questionEn: What did three Qurayshi elders—Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl, and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq—secretly do three nights in a row near the Prophet's ﷺ home?
optionsEn: Each crept separately in the dark to eavesdrop on his nighttime Qur'an recitation and bumped into one another at dawn
They painted slogans on his wall
They dug a trench outside his door
explanationEn: Captivated by the Qur'an's beauty, all three listened secretly all night three times; though al-Akhnas and Abu Sufyan saw the truth, Abu Jahl's tribal rivalry blocked submission.

questionEn: Who was the first prominent Muslim whose house and property were seized or ransomed when he migrated, later sacrificing his wealth freely in Makkah and Madinah?
explanationEn: When Quraysh tried to block Suhayb al-Rumi from leaving Makkah with his wealth, he told them where his gold was hidden to buy safe passage; the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'Suhayb has profited!'

questionEn: Which handsome, wealthy young Makkan nobleman gave up luxury, endured his mother's boycott, and later became Islam's first ambassador to Madinah?
explanationEn: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) sacrificed silk garments and family privilege for Islam, enduring hunger and tattered clothes with joyful faith.

questionEn: What happened when Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas's (RA) mother vowed to starve herself until he renounced Islam?
optionsEn: Sa'd told her gently that even if she had a hundred souls and each departed, he would never abandon his faith, and Allah revealed kindness to parents without obeying them in shirk
explanationEn: Allah revealed in Surah Luqman (31:15) to accompany parents kindly in worldly affairs while refusing obedience if they strive to associate partners with Allah.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Kitab Fada'il al-Sahabah); Surah Luqman 31:15

questionEn: Which early companion was tortured in his own home by his uncle who wrapped him in a reed mat and blew smoke into his nostrils?
explanationEn: Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam's uncle suspended him in smoke demanding he return to disbelief, yet young Zubayr stood firm: 'I will never disbelieve!'

questionEn: How did Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) and Talhah ibn Ubaydullah (RA) earn the joint nickname 'Al-Qarinayn' (The Two Tied Together) in Makkah?
optionsEn: Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid bound them together with a single rope to torture them for accepting Islam
They co-owned a ship at Jeddah
They rode side by side to Abyssinia
explanationEn: Nawfal, a fierce opponent of Banu Taym, tied Abu Bakr and Talhah together in one rope to humiliate and break them, yet neither wavered.

questionEn: What happened when Uthman ibn Maz'un (RA) renounced the tribal protection of al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah because he felt ashamed to walk safely while poorer Muslims were beaten?
optionsEn: He was struck in the eye by a poet, and when offered renewed protection he refused, saying 'I am content with the protection of Allah'
explanationEn: Uthman ibn Maz'un (RA) lost sight in one eye with joy, declaring his healthy eye yearned to suffer the same for Allah's sake rather than rely on a polytheist's protection.

questionEn: What miraculous support did Abu Bakr (RA) receive from Ibn al-Dughunnah—and why did Abu Bakr eventually give it up?
optionsEn: He lent Abu Bakr a castle in Ta'if
He guarded Abu Bakr's trade ships
Ibn al-Dughunnah offered him protection in Makkah on condition he pray silently indoors, which Abu Bakr returned when Quraysh complained his weeping recitation attracted women and youth
He hid Abu Bakr inside the Kaaba
explanationEn: Abu Bakr built a small prayer place in his courtyard where his tender Qur'an weeping drew Makkan families; refusing to silence his worship, he surrendered Ibn al-Dughunnah's protection and relied solely on Allah.

questionEn: Which group of unseen beings listened attentively to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reciting the Qur'an in the valley of Nakhlah (and earlier near Makkah) and returned as warners to their people?
explanationEn: A group of Jinn heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting Qur'an during Fajr prayer, believed immediately, and returned to warn their community, as recorded in Surahs Al-Ahqaf (46:29) and Al-Jinn (72).

questionEn: What did Abu Jahl plan to do to the Prophet's ﷺ neck while he prayed at the Kaaba, only to retreat in terror waving his hands?
optionsEn: His foot slipped on Zamzam water
He saw a trench of raging fire and winged horrors separating him from the Prophet ﷺ
explanationEn: Abu Jahl swore he would trample the Prophet's ﷺ neck, but recoiled pale with fear, telling Quraysh a fiery trench and dreadful wings stood between them.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Kitab Sifat al-Munafiqin); Surah Al-Alaq 96:9-19

questionEn: Which Surah opens with a direct divine rebuke to the Prophet ﷺ for frowning when a blind seeker—Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA)—interrupted his talk with Qurayshi nobles?
explanationEn: Allah taught in Surah Abasa (80:1-10) that one sincere seeker rushing with awe of Allah outweighs haughty chiefs; thereafter the Prophet ﷺ greeted Ibn Umm Maktum warmly as 'He on whose account my Lord rebuked me!'

questionEn: Which early Makkan female convert was the sister of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and accepted Islam before him alongside her husband Sa'id ibn Zayd?
explanationEn: Fatimah bint al-Khattab bravely protected the Qur'an sheets against her brother's anger, becoming instrumental in Umar's conversion.

questionEn: Who was the first person to bring news of Islam to the Ghifar tribe before Abu Dharr, or how did Abu Dharr first learn of the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Negus wrote a letter to Ghifar
Abu Dharr's brother Unays traveled to Makkah, heard the Prophet ﷺ, and reported his noble character and message back to Abu Dharr
explanationEn: Unays returned from Makkah telling Abu Dharr he met a man who commanded noble morals and spoke speech unlike any poet or soothsayer, prompting Abu Dharr to travel to Makkah himself.

questionEn: Who sheltered Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA) secretly near Zamzam and guided him to meet the Prophet ﷺ without alerting Quraysh?
explanationEn: After Abu Dharr survived on Zamzam water for nearly a month, Ali (RA) recognized him as a stranger, hosted him discreetly, and led him to the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA) right after he accepted Islam in Makkah?
optionsEn: To return to his tribe Ghifar and teach them until he heard the Prophet ﷺ had appeared openly
To remain hidden in Cave Hira
explanationEn: After Abu Dharr boldly proclaimed Islam at the Kaaba and was rescued by Abbas, the Prophet ﷺ sent him back to Banu Ghifar, where half the tribe embraced Islam before Hijrah.

questionEn: What prophecy in Surah Al-Rum (30:1-4) cheered the persecuted Makkan Muslims when pagan Persia defeated Christian Byzantium?
optionsEn: That the Byzantines would reverse the defeat and triumph within a few years (bid'i sinin), coinciding with the Muslims' victory at Badr
That Persia would move the Kaaba
explanationEn: Quraysh rejoiced at Persia's victory as fellow idolaters, so Allah revealed Surah Al-Rum promising Byzantine victory within 3–9 years—confirmed at the same time Muslims celebrated Badr.

questionEn: Which two early converts were enslaved women in Makkah whom Abu Bakr (RA) bought and freed—justifying Surah Al-Layl's praise of one who gives purely seeking Allah's Face?
optionsEn: Lubaynah and al-Nahdiyyah (along with Umm Ubays and Zinnirah)
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA) freed persecuted enslaved women like Zinnirah (whose sight Allah miraculously restored after Abu Jahl mocked her blindness), Lubaynah, al-Nahdiyyah, and Umm Ubays.

questionEn: What happened to Zinnirah al-Rumiyyah (RA) after Abu Bakr (RA) freed her and Quraysh claimed their idols Lat and Uzza had blinded her?
optionsEn: She affirmed Lat and Uzza cannot harm or heal, and Allah restored her eyesight by morning
explanationEn: Zinnirah retorted that their idols did not even know who worshiped them, and Allah miraculously restored her vision the very next day.

questionEn: What nickname did Quraysh mockingly use for the Prophet ﷺ after the deaths of his infant sons, prompting Surah Al-Kawthar?
explanationEn: Al-As ibn Wa'il sneered that Muhammad ﷺ was 'abtar' (cut off without lineage); Allah revealed Surah Al-Kawthar (108), promising eternal abundance and declaring his enemy to be the one truly cut off.

questionEn: Which enemy of the Prophet ﷺ spat toward him or tore up his own daughter's marriage to Ruqayyah, only to be mauled by a lion on a journey to Syria after the Prophet's ﷺ supplication?
explanationEn: Utaybah ibn Abi Lahab insulted the Prophet ﷺ insolently before departing for Syria; the Prophet ﷺ prayed 'O Allah, set one of Your dogs upon him,' and a lion singled him out in the middle of his sleeping caravan.

questionEn: Which subtle form of persuasion did Quraysh try through Abu Jahl's cohort—calling the Qur'an 'Asatir al-Awwalin'—meaning what?
explanationEn: Disbelievers dismissed revelation as 'Asatir al-Awwalin' (tales of the ancients), which the Qur'an refuted by challenging them to produce even a single Surah like it.

questionEn: Why did Quraysh ask the Prophet ﷺ to banish poor companions like Bilal, Suhayb, and Ibn Mas'ud so that wealthy chiefs could sit with him?
optionsEn: Out of tribal arrogance, which Allah strictly forbade in Surah Al-An'am (6:52) and Al-Kahf (18:28)
Because the poor could not read
Because Dar al-Arqam was too small
explanationEn: Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ: 'Do not send away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face'—affirming spiritual equality in Islam.

questionEn: What did Abu Talib write in a famous poem defending Banu Hashim and the Prophet ﷺ during Quraysh hostility?
optionsEn: His famous Lamiyyah poem declaring his clan would never surrender Muhammad ﷺ while any of them lived
explanationEn: Abu Talib composed a powerful ode honoring the Kaaba and declaring Banu Hashim's unwavering defense of the Prophet ﷺ against Quraysh aggression.

questionEn: Who were the five primary Makkan mockers (Mustahzi'un) whom Allah promised in Surah Al-Hijr (15:95) He would suffice the Prophet ﷺ against?
optionsEn: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and al-Harith ibn Qays
Sa'd, Sa'id, Zubayr, Hamzah, and Abbas
Zayd, Bilal, Ammar, Khabbab, and Suhayb
Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, and Talhah
explanationEn: These five relentless mockers each suffered sudden, humiliating deaths soon after Allah reassured His Messenger in Surah Al-Hijr 15:95: 'Indeed, We are sufficient for you against the mockers.'

questionEn: Which early convert from Banu Makhzum was tricked into returning from Abyssinia and then chained in Makkah by his brother Hisham and Abu Jahl?
explanationEn: Abu Jahl lied to Ayyash that his mother vowed neither to comb her hair nor seek shade until she saw him; returning to Makkah, Ayyash was imprisoned until later rescued.

questionEn: How many Muslims roughly took part in the Second Migration to Abyssinia as persecution intensified in Makkah?
explanationEn: Unlike the small first group of ~15, the second emigration to Abyssinia numbered around 83 men and nearly 20 women, including Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and Umm Salamah.

questionEn: Which woman among the Abyssinian emigrants later became a Mother of the Believers and remembered King Negus fondly for his justice?
explanationEn: Umm Salamah (RA) migrated to Abyssinia with her husband Abu Salamah (RA) and famously narrated Ja'far's historic dialogue with Negus.

questionEn: What crucial question did King Negus ask Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (RA) to test whether the Muslims truly honored Prophet Isa (AS)?
optionsEn: 'What do you say regarding Jesus, son of Mary?'
explanationEn: Prompted by Amr ibn al-As who claimed Muslims insulted Isa (AS), Negus asked Ja'far directly; Ja'far affirmed Isa (AS) is Allah's servant, messenger, spirit, and word cast unto pure Maryam.

questionEn: Which prominent Makkan chief, Abu Bakr's own son, initially remained on Quraysh's side in Makkah before accepting Islam years later at Hudaybiyyah?
explanationEn: Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr fought against the Muslims at Badr and Uhud before accepting Islam at Hudaybiyyah and becoming a devoted companion.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic theme overwhelmingly dominated the 13-year Makkan phase of revelation?
optionsEn: Detailed laws of warfare and treaty division
Pure monotheism (Tawhid), the Resurrection and Day of Judgment, moral purification, and patience
explanationEn: Makkan Surahs anchored hearts firmly in Tawhid, accountability in the Hereafter, and steadfast character before legislative rulings descended in Madinah.

questionEn: What did Aishah (RA) explain about why the Qur'an focused on Paradise, Hellfire, and Tawhid in Makkah before prohibiting wine and adultery?
optionsEn: Because nobody could read in Makkah
Because wine did not exist in Makkah
Because if the first command had been 'Do not drink wine,' people would have refused until faith took deep root in their hearts
Because laws were only for Madinah's climate
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) highlighted the divine wisdom of gradual moral transformation: once hearts bowed to Allah in love and awe, obedience to legal prohibitions followed willingly.

questionEn: Which young man from Aws in Yathrib visited Makkah seeking a tribal alliance before the Aqabah pledges, heard the Prophet ﷺ recite the Qur'an, and exclaimed it was better than what he came for?
explanationEn: When Aws youths came to Makkah seeking Quraysh's help against Khazraj, the Prophet ﷺ offered them something far better—Islam—and young Iyas ibn Mu'adh exclaimed, 'By Allah, this is better than what we came for!'

questionEn: What did Quraysh ask the Prophet ﷺ when they demanded miracles like turning Mount Safa into gold or splitting Makkah's mountains?
optionsEn: Jibril informed him that if such demanded signs were sent and rejected, immediate destruction would follow like past nations—so out of mercy he chose patience for his people
He asked Abu Talib to decide
He turned Safa into silver instead
He told them to climb Mount Arafah
explanationEn: Out of profound mercy, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ preferred giving Quraysh and their descendants time to repent and believe rather than risking instant collective destruction.
reference: Musnad Ahmad; Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Surah Al-Isra 17:59)

questionEn: Which two pagan rabbis or scholars in Madinah did Quraysh consult by sending al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt to test the Prophet's ﷺ authenticity?
optionsEn: Jewish scholars in Yathrib, who proposed three questions: the youths of the cave, the traveler to the ends of the earth (Dhul-Qarnayn), and the Ruh (soul)
explanationEn: In response to those three test questions, Allah revealed Surah Al-Kahf (18) detailing Ashab al-Kahf and Dhul-Qarnayn, and Surah Al-Isra (17:85) concerning the Ruh.

questionEn: What did al-Nadr ibn al-Harith try to do in Makkah to distract people whenever Prophet Muhammad ﷺ sat at the Kaaba reciting the Qur'an?
optionsEn: He played loud drums inside Dar al-Nadwah
He distributed free dates at Arafah
He bought Persian books of Rustam and Isfandiyar and told stories to lure listeners away
He blocked the road to Safa
explanationEn: Al-Nadr brought Persian legends from Hirah claiming they rivaled the Qur'an; Surah Luqman (31:6) condemned those who purchase 'idle tales' to mislead people from Allah's path.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when Abu Jahl and Quraysh mockingly insulted him as 'Mudhammam' (the blameworthy) instead of Muhammad?
optionsEn: He answered them with harsh poetry
He forbade anyone from entering the Haram
He smiled and told his companions: 'Do you not see how Allah turns their insults away from me? They curse Mudhammam, whereas I am Muhammad (the praised one)'
explanationEn: With serene dignity and wit, the Prophet ﷺ taught believers not to let malicious slurs disturb their hearts.

questionEn: Where were Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib confined for nearly three years during Quraysh's total social and economic boycott?
optionsEn: Shi'b Abi Talib (the mountain ravine of Abu Talib)
explanationEn: After Umar and Hamzah embraced Islam, Quraysh hung a boycott scroll inside the Kaaba banning marriage and trade with Banu Hashim, isolating them in Shi'b Abi Talib.

questionEn: What did the persecuted believers in Shi'b Abi Talib resort to eating during the severest days of the Makkan boycott?
optionsEn: Leaves of thorny trees and boiled leather hides
explanationEn: Supplies were blocked so strictly that children cried from hunger and companions ate tree leaves and softened leather while remaining steadfast.

questionEn: Which compassionate Makkan—Khadijah's (RA) nephew—secretly smuggled wheat and food into Shi'b Abi Talib on a camel at night?
explanationEn: Hakim ibn Hizam (RA), along with Hisham ibn Amr, risked Quraysh's wrath by secretly driving food-laden camels into the ravine at night.

questionEn: How was the cruel boycott parchment hanging inside the Kaaba miraculously ruined before Quraysh annulled it?
optionsEn: Ali (RA) tore it down at noon
Termites (white ants) ate every word except 'Bismika Allahumma' (In Your Name, O Allah)
A fire burned the Kaaba door
explanationEn: Allah revealed this to His Prophet ﷺ, who told Abu Talib; when Abu Talib challenged Quraysh to check the scroll, they found termites had devoured all clauses except Allah's Name.

questionEn: Which five humane Makkans initiated the campaign inside the Haram to tear up the unjust boycott pact against Banu Hashim?
optionsEn: Waraqah, Bahira, Zayd, Addas, and Negus
Uthman, Ali, Talhah, Zubayr, and Sa'd
Hisham ibn Amr, Zuhayr ibn Abi Umayyah, al-Mut'im ibn Adi, Abu al-Bakhtari, and Zam'ah ibn al-Aswad
Abu Jahl, Uqbah, Utbah, Shaybah, and Umayyah
explanationEn: Hisham ibn Amr rallied four fellow chieftains who denounced starving their own kinsmen at the Kaaba, forcing Abu Jahl to back down as the parchment was found eaten.

questionEn: Why is the tenth year of prophethood famously remembered in Seerah as 'Am al-Huzn' (The Year of Sorrow)?
optionsEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ lost both his protector uncle Abu Talib and his beloved wife Khadijah (RA) within a short span
explanationEn: Shortly after emerging from the grueling three-year boycott, Abu Talib and Khadijah (RA) passed away—removing his external tribal shield and deepest domestic solace.

questionEn: How did Angel Jibril (AS) honor Khadijah (RA) shortly before her passing in Makkah?
optionsEn: He revealed a Surah named after her
He brought her a golden crown
He sent peace (Salam) to her from Allah and promised her a house of hollowed pearl in Paradise free of noise or fatigue
explanationEn: Jibril told the Prophet ﷺ to give Khadijah (RA) Salam from Allah and from himself, and glad tidings of a tranquil palace of pearl (qasab) in Jannah.

questionEn: Which righteous widow from the Abyssinian emigrants did the Prophet ﷺ marry after Khadijah's (RA) passing to care for his household and honor her sacrifice?
explanationEn: Sawdah bint Zam'ah (RA), an early convert whose husband al-Sakran had passed away after returning from Abyssinia, lovingly managed the Prophet's ﷺ home and daughters.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ walk roughly 60–70 km to the mountain city of Ta'if in the tenth year of prophethood?
optionsEn: Seeking support and receptivity to Islam from the tribe of Thaqif after Makkah's doors closed
explanationEn: With Abu Talib gone and Quraysh emboldened, the Prophet ﷺ walked with Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) to Ta'if hoping Banu Thaqif would embrace and shelter the message.

questionEn: Who faithfully accompanied Prophet Muhammad ﷺ on foot during the painful journey to Ta'if and shielded him from stones with his own body?
explanationEn: When the leaders of Thaqif incited mobs to pelt the Prophet ﷺ until his heels bled, Zayd ibn Harithah shielded him and sustained head wounds.

questionEn: Which Christian servant from Nineveh met the bleeding Prophet ﷺ in an orchard outside Ta'if, offered him grapes, and kissed his head and hands upon hearing him say 'Bismillah'?
explanationEn: Addas was moved when the Prophet ﷺ knew Prophet Yunus ibn Matta of Nineveh as 'my brother; he was a prophet and I am a prophet.'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ask Allah for in his famous heartfelt du'a after being stoned out of Ta'if?
optionsEn: For an earthquake to destroy Thaqif
He complained only of his weakness to Allah, declaring that as long as Allah was not displeased with him, he did not care about any hardship
explanationEn: His supplication ('O Allah, to You I complain of my weakness...') remains one of the most moving expressions of complete surrender and sincerity in Islamic history.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when the Angel of the Mountains offered to crush the people of Ta'if between Makkah's two towering mountains (al-Akhshabayn)?
optionsEn: He refused, hoping Allah would bring forth from their descendants people who worship Allah alone
He asked to wait one month
He asked to crush only their chiefs
explanationEn: Even bleeding from their stones, the Mercy to the Worlds prayed for future generations of Ta'if—a hope fulfilled years later when Thaqif embraced Islam.

questionEn: Which noble non-Muslim Makkan chieftain honored tribal chivalry by granting the Prophet ﷺ safe re-entry into Makkah after Ta'if and marching armed with his sons around the Kaaba?
explanationEn: After other chiefs refused, al-Mut'im ibn Adi granted protection; years later after Badr, the Prophet ﷺ said if al-Mut'im had been alive and asked for the captives, he would have released them all for him.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Isra (17:1), between which two sacred mosques did Allah miraculously transport Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in a single night?
explanationEn: Isra refers to the miraculous night journey from Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem.

questionEn: What was the name of the heavenly white steed—larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, whose stride reached as far as the eye could see—that carried the Prophet ﷺ on Al-Isra?
explanationEn: Jibril brought Al-Buraq, which the Prophet ﷺ rode to Jerusalem and tethered at the ring used by the prophets.

questionEn: What extraordinary congregational event took place inside Al-Masjid al-Aqsa during the Night Journey?
optionsEn: He stayed in Jerusalem for a month
He wrote a treaty with Rome
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ led all the previous Prophets of Allah in prayer as their Imam
explanationEn: Leading all earlier prophets in Salah at Al-Masjid al-Aqsa affirmed the unity of prophetic revelation and Muhammad's ﷺ status as Seal of the Prophets.

questionEn: When offered vessels of milk and wine by Angel Jibril (AS) during Al-Isra wal-Mi'raj, which did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ choose, and what did Jibril remark?
optionsEn: He chose milk, and Jibril said: 'You have been guided to the Fitrah (natural purity)'
explanationEn: Choosing pure milk signified that he and his Ummah were guided to al-Fitrah—the pure, natural disposition of monotheism.

questionEn: During Al-Mi'raj (the Ascension through the seven heavens), which prophet did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ meet in the first (lowest) heaven?
