explanationEn: In the first heaven he met Father Adam (AS), who rejoiced over his righteous descendants and wept over those destined for ruin.

questionEn: Which two prophets—maternal cousins—did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ meet together in the second heaven during Al-Mi'raj?
optionsEn: Isa ibn Maryam and Yahya ibn Zakariyya (AS)
explanationEn: In the second heaven he greeted Prophets Isa and Yahya (AS), who welcomed him as 'the righteous brother and righteous prophet.'

questionEn: Which prophet, described as having been given half of all beauty, did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ meet in the third heaven?
explanationEn: In the third heaven he met Prophet Yusuf (AS), whom he described as endowed with half of all worldly beauty.

questionEn: Which prophet did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ meet in the fourth heaven, echoing Surah Maryam's mention that Allah raised him to a high station?
explanationEn: In the fourth heaven he met Prophet Idris (AS), and in the fifth heaven Prophet Harun (AS).

questionEn: Which prophet did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ meet in the sixth heaven, who later advised him to return to Allah and ask to lighten the daily prayers?
explanationEn: In the sixth heaven Musa (AS) wept from joy that a younger prophet's Ummah would enter Paradise in greater numbers, and he wisely counselled the Prophet ﷺ to request prayer reduction.

questionEn: Which prophet did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ meet in the seventh heaven, leaning against Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur?
explanationEn: In the seventh heaven he met his forefather Ibrahim (AS) resting his back against Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, the heavenly sanctuary entered by 70,000 angels daily who never return.

questionEn: What is the name of the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary that Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reached during Al-Mi'raj?
explanationEn: At Sidrat al-Muntaha, beyond which no angel or prophet passes, Allah revealed magnificent mysteries directly to His Messenger ﷺ.

questionEn: How many daily prayers were initially prescribed during Al-Mi'raj before being mercifully lightened to five with the reward of fifty?
explanationEn: Allah initially ordained fifty daily prayers; after repeatedly seeking reduction on Musa's (AS) counsel, Allah decreed five prayers daily carrying the full reward of fifty.

questionEn: What three great gifts were bestowed upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ directly at Sidrat al-Muntaha (per Sahih Muslim)?
optionsEn: The five daily prayers, the final verses of Surah Al-Baqarah (2:285-286), and forgiveness of major sins for whoever dies without associating partners with Allah
Control of the winds, languages of birds, and iron
Exemption from Hajj, fasting, and charity
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud narrated that at Sidrat al-Muntaha the Prophet ﷺ received the five prayers, the concluding verses of Surah Al-Baqarah, and the promise of salvation from eternal Fire for pure monotheists.

questionEn: How did Abu Bakr (RA) earn the eternal title 'Al-Siddiq' (The Steadfast Affirmer of Truth) the morning after Al-Isra wal-Mi'raj?
optionsEn: He drew a map of Jerusalem
He led the caravan back from Syria
He said if Muhammad ﷺ said he traveled to Jerusalem and back in one night, then it is true—just as he believes even greater news of revelation from heaven
He silenced Abu Jahl in court
explanationEn: While skeptics mocked, Abu Bakr's immediate unshakeable conviction ('I believe him in something even more astonishing: revelation descending from heaven morning and evening') earned him Al-Siddiq.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ answer Quraysh when they demanded proof of his Night Journey by describing Bayt al-Maqdis?
optionsEn: Allah raised a visual image of Jerusalem before his eyes so he described its gates and details accurately, and he told them of a Makkan caravan he passed on the road
explanationEn: Those who had traveled to Jerusalem verified his exact description of Al-Masjid al-Aqsa and later saw the returning caravan arrive precisely as he foretold.

questionEn: During the 11th year of prophethood at Mina during Hajj, six men from which tribe of Yathrib met the Prophet ﷺ at al-Aqabah and embraced Islam?
explanationEn: Six men of Khazraj—including As'ad ibn Zurarah and Jabir ibn Abdullah's uncle/companions—recognized him as the final prophet Jewish neighbors in Yathrib had spoken of.

questionEn: How many people from Yathrib (from both Aws and Khazraj) pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ at the First Pledge of Aqabah (12th year of prophethood)?
explanationEn: Twelve men from Yathrib pledged not to associate partners with Allah, steal, commit adultery, kill children, slander, or disobey the Prophet ﷺ in good.

questionEn: Whom did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ send to Yathrib after the First Pledge of Aqabah to teach the Qur'an and Islam—becoming the first ambassador of Islam?
explanationEn: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) stayed with As'ad ibn Zurarah and preached so gently and effectively that almost every household in Yathrib embraced Islam within a year.

questionEn: Which two prominent chieftains of Aws in Madinah embraced Islam through Mus'ab ibn Umayr's (RA) gentle call, transforming their entire clan?
optionsEn: Abu Ayyub and Ubayy ibn Ka'b
Usayd ibn Hudayr and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA)
explanationEn: Usayd came angrily with a spear, listened calmly to Mus'ab's Qur'an recitation, accepted Islam, and sent Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, whose conversion led Banu Abd al-Ashhal to embrace Islam by evening.

questionEn: How many Muslims from Madinah (men and two women) met the Prophet ﷺ secretly by night during Hajj for the Second Pledge of Aqabah?
explanationEn: During the 13th year of prophethood in the middle of the nights of Tashriq at Aqabah, 73 men and 2 women (Nusaibah bint Ka'b and Asma bint Amr) pledged to protect the Prophet ﷺ as their own families.

questionEn: Who accompanied the Prophet ﷺ to the secret Second Pledge of Aqabah—still non-Muslim then, yet fiercely protective of his nephew's safety?
explanationEn: Al-Abbas checked the sincerity and strength of the Ansar's oath to defend the Prophet ﷺ before allowing the commitment to proceed.

questionEn: What did the Ansar ask Prophet Muhammad ﷺ at the Second Pledge of Aqabah—receiving a reassurance that brought tears to their eyes?
optionsEn: They asked if he would leave them for Makkah once victorious; he replied, 'Nay, blood for blood, destruction for destruction—I am of you and you are of me!'
They asked for gold from Syria
They asked him to rule from Ta'if
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ pledged lifelong loyalty to Madinah—a covenant he honored even after conquering Makkah.

questionEn: How many tribal representatives (Nuqaba) did the Prophet ﷺ appoint from among the Ansar at the Second Pledge of Aqabah?
optionsEn: Twelve (nine from Khazraj, three from Aws)
explanationEn: Like the twelve leaders among Bani Isra'il, the Prophet ﷺ selected 12 Nuqaba to coordinate their clans' affairs.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ told his companions he had been shown the land of their migration—a land of date palms between two volcanic lava tracts (Harratayn)—which city was it?
explanationEn: First he thought it might be Yamamah or Hajar, then realized it was Yathrib, nestled between two black basalt lava fields (Harrah).

questionEn: Which companion boldly refused to sneak out of Makkah by night during the Hijrah, announcing at the Kaaba that anyone wanting to lose him should meet him behind the valley?
explanationEn: Umar (RA) performed Tawaf, prayed two rak'ahs at Maqam Ibrahim, and publicly challenged Quraysh before departing in broad daylight with twenty weaker companions.

questionEn: Why did Abu Bakr (RA) remain behind in Makkah when most companions migrated to Madinah?
optionsEn: He wanted to move to Yemen
The Prophet ﷺ told him, 'Do not hasten; perhaps Allah will grant you a companion'
explanationEn: Hoping he might be chosen as that companion, Abu Bakr (RA) carefully fed two fine riding camels for four months in preparation.

questionEn: What evil plot did Quraysh chiefs agree upon inside Dar al-Nadwah on Abu Jahl's suggestion to stop the Prophet ﷺ from migrating?
optionsEn: To select one strong youth from every clan so all would strike him together at night, preventing Banu Hashim from avenging his blood against all tribes
explanationEn: Allah informed His Messenger ﷺ of this plot (Surah Al-Anfal 8:30) and granted permission to migrate.

questionEn: Who slept in Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ bed wrapped in his green Hadrami cloak on the night of Hijrah to deceive the assassins and later return people's trusts?
explanationEn: Ali (RA) willingly risked his life in the Prophet's ﷺ bed and stayed three days in Makkah afterward to return all valuables entrusted to Al-Amin.

questionEn: Which Surah's opening verses did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ recite as he threw a handful of dust and walked unseen past the assassins besieging his house?
explanationEn: Reciting 'And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see' (36:9), he walked safely past every watcher.

questionEn: How did Abu Bakr (RA) react when the Prophet ﷺ arrived at midday to announce Allah had granted permission to migrate and that Abu Bakr would accompany him?
optionsEn: He sent a messenger to Ta'if
He asked for three more weeks
He wept tears of sheer joy, as Aishah (RA) noted she had never seen someone weep out of happiness until that day
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA) immediately offered the better of his two prepared she-camels, though the Prophet ﷺ insisted on paying its fair price.

questionEn: In which direction from Makkah is Cave Thawr located—a deliberate strategy by the Prophet ﷺ to throw off Quraysh trackers?
optionsEn: Due north on the direct Madinah road
South of Makkah, the opposite direction from Madinah
explanationEn: Madinah lies north, so heading south to steep Jabal Thawr and sheltering there for three nights brilliantly thwarted Quraysh's initial northern pursuit.

questionEn: How did Abu Bakr's daughter Asma (RA) earn the honored title 'Dhat al-Nitaqayn' (She of the Two Waistbands) during the Hijrah?
optionsEn: She tore her own waistband in two—using one half to tie the food provisions and the other to tie the water skin for Cave Thawr
explanationEn: Lacking rope to secure their travel provisions, Asma (RA) split her belt in two; the Prophet ﷺ praised her and promised two belts in Paradise.

questionEn: How did Abu Bakr's son Abdullah and freedman Amir ibn Fuhayrah support the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr inside Cave Thawr for three nights?
optionsEn: Abdullah gathered Makkan intelligence by day and reported at night, while Amir grazed sheep over his footprints and brought fresh milk
They dug a tunnel to Jeddah
explanationEn: Together with Asma bringing food, the family ran a remarkably disciplined support network right under Quraysh's nose.

questionEn: What reassuring words recorded in Surah Al-Tawbah (9:40) did the Prophet ﷺ whisper to Abu Bakr when pursuers stood right at the mouth of Cave Thawr?
optionsEn: 'Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us' ('La tahzan inna Allaha ma'ana')
explanationEn: When Abu Bakr whispered that if a pursuer looked down at his feet he would see them, the Prophet ﷺ replied: 'What do you think of two whose third is Allah?'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Manaqib al-Ansar); Surah Al-Tawbah 9:40

questionEn: Who was the skilled, trustworthy non-Muslim guide hired by Abu Bakr and the Prophet ﷺ to lead them along an obscure coastal route from Cave Thawr to Madinah?
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Urayqit was an expert desert navigator whose professional trustworthiness was relied upon to guide them safely along hidden western tracks.

questionEn: What reward did Quraysh announce for anyone who captured or killed Prophet Muhammad ﷺ or Abu Bakr during the Hijrah?
optionsEn: One hundred camels for each of them
explanationEn: Driven by that huge bounty of 100 camels, bounty hunters fanned out across Arabia—including Suraqah ibn Malik.

questionEn: What miraculous protection stopped Suraqah ibn Malik when he tracked down the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hoping to win Quraysh's 100-camel bounty?
optionsEn: His horse's forelegs sank repeatedly into hard desert ground until he realized the Prophet ﷺ was divinely protected and begged for a document of safety
explanationEn: After his horse sank three times and smoke rose from the sand, Suraqah repented, asked Abu Bakr to write a covenant of protection, and misled pursuing scouts away from them.

questionEn: What astonishing prophecy did the Prophet ﷺ give Suraqah ibn Malik on the Hijrah road—which came true decades later under Caliph Umar (RA)?
optionsEn: 'How will you feel, O Suraqah, when you wear the gold bracelets of Khosrow (emperor of Persia)?'
explanationEn: Years later when Muslims conquered Mada'in, Umar (RA) summoned the elderly Suraqah (now a Muslim) and placed Khosrow's jeweled bracelets on his arms in fulfillment of the Prophet's ﷺ words.

questionEn: What blessing occurred at the tent of the Bedouin woman Umm Ma'bad (Atikah bint Khalid) during the Hijrah journey?
optionsEn: A spring erupted under her tent
The Prophet ﷺ stroked the udder of a dry, emaciated ewe left behind from pasture, and milk flowed abundantly for all of them and her household
explanationEn: Afterward Umm Ma'bad gave her husband one of the most eloquent physical and moral descriptions of the Prophet ﷺ preserved in Seerah.

questionEn: During the Hijrah, which tribe's chief Buraydah ibn al-Husayb intercepted the Prophet ﷺ with 80 riders—and ended up embracing Islam alongside his men?
explanationEn: Buraydah of Banu Aslam accepted Islam on the spot, untied his turban to make a makeshift banner on his spear, and escorted the Prophet ﷺ into Madinah's outskirts.

questionEn: Whom did the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr encounter returning from Syria along the Hijrah trail who gifted them clean white garments?
explanationEn: Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam met them with a trade caravan returning from Syria and joyfully presented the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr with fine white clothing.

questionEn: What poignant farewell did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ speak looking back at Makkah as he departed during the Hijrah?
optionsEn: 'I will never look back at you again'
'By Allah, you are the best of Allah's earth and the most beloved of Allah's earth to me; had I not been driven out of you, I would never have left'
explanationEn: This tender expression reveals how deeply the Prophet ﷺ loved Makkah, and Allah soon comforted him in Surah Al-Qasas (28:85) promising his return.

questionEn: In which Islamic month did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ arrive at Quba on the outskirts of Madinah?
explanationEn: He arrived at Quba on Monday, 8th (or 12th) of Rabi' al-Awwal—the very same month and weekday of his blessed birth and later his passing.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Manaqib al-Ansar); Al-Raheeq al-Makhtum

questionEn: Whose home in Quba hosted Prophet Muhammad ﷺ for several days upon his arrival outside Madinah?
explanationEn: At Quba, the Prophet ﷺ stayed with the elderly pious Ansar chief Kulthum ibn al-Hidm (RA), while welcoming visitors at the home of Sa'd ibn Khaythamah.

questionEn: What was the very first mosque built in Islamic history, founded by the Prophet's ﷺ own hands immediately upon arriving at Quba?
explanationEn: Masjid Quba is praised in Surah Al-Tawbah (9:108) as 'a mosque founded on righteousness (taqwa) from the first day'; praying two rak'ahs there equals the reward of an Umrah.

questionEn: Which Muslim who arrived at Quba before the Prophet ﷺ did the Prophet ﷺ wait for there for three days before riding onward into central Madinah?
explanationEn: Ali (RA) walked on foot from Makkah after returning people's deposits, arriving at Quba with blistered, bleeding feet; the Prophet ﷺ embraced him and tended his feet.

questionEn: Where did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ lead his very first Jumu'ah (Friday) prayer and khutbah after departing Quba toward central Madinah?
optionsEn: In Wadi Ranuna, with Banu Salim ibn Awf
explanationEn: Noon on Friday overtook him in the valley of Banu Salim ibn Awf (now Masjid al-Jumu'ah), where he delivered an unforgettable khutbah and led the first Friday prayer.

questionEn: When the Ansar eagerly mistook Abu Bakr (RA) for the Prophet ﷺ while greeting them at the Harrah of Madinah, how did Abu Bakr gently clarify without embarrassing anyone?
optionsEn: He stood up and shaded the Prophet ﷺ from the sun with his cloak, so everyone immediately recognized the Messenger of Allah ﷺ
explanationEn: Abu Bakr's humble gesture of shading the Prophet ﷺ immediately revealed who the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was to those who had never seen him.

questionEn: What were the very first four public pieces of advice Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) heard Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give upon entering Madinah?
optionsEn: 'Spread peace (Salam), feed the hungry, uphold kinship ties, and pray at night while people sleep—and you will enter Paradise in peace'
'Build high walls, store grain, forge armor, and guard the gates'
'Speak only poetry, wear silk, avoid trade, and fast daily'
'Leave Yathrib, travel to Ta'if, pay tribute, and close markets'
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Salam, a learned rabbi of Madinah, saw the truthfulness of the Prophet's ﷺ face and heard those four universal principles, embracing Islam soon after.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell the Ansar clans grabbing his camel's reins in Madinah to let Al-Qaswa walk freely?
optionsEn: Because she knew Abu Talib's road
'Let her go her way, for she is commanded (by Allah)'—preventing jealousy among clans over hosting him
Because he wanted to reach Khaybar
explanationEn: By leaving the choice to Allah's guidance through Al-Qaswa, no Ansar clan felt slighted when the camel finally knelt at the courtyard of Banu al-Najjar.

questionEn: Who owned the open date-drying courtyard (Mirbad) where Al-Qaswa knelt—and did the Prophet ﷺ accept it as a free gift or insist on paying for it?
optionsEn: Abu Ayyub; he took it for free
Abdullah ibn Ubayy; he traded horses for it
Two orphan brothers, Sahl and Suhayl; he insisted on buying it fairly, paid by Abu Bakr (RA)
explanationEn: Though the orphans and Banu al-Najjar offered it freely, the Prophet ﷺ upheld strict justice toward orphans by purchasing the land cleanly for ten gold dinars.

questionEn: Why did Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA) and his wife insist on swapping floors when the Prophet ﷺ stayed on their ground floor?
optionsEn: The ground floor had no windows
They wanted to store dates upstairs
They felt unbearable distress walking over the ceiling directly above the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Revelation
explanationEn: When a water jar broke upstairs, Abu Ayyub and his wife hastily dried it with their own blanket so not a drop would drip onto the Prophet ﷺ, begging him to move upstairs.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Kitab al-Ashribah); Seerah Ibn Hisham

questionEn: Which young Ansar boy was brought by his mother Umm Sulaym to serve Prophet Muhammad ﷺ upon his arrival in Madinah, serving him faithfully for ten years?
explanationEn: Ten-year-old Anas ibn Malik (RA) testified that in ten full years of service, the Prophet ﷺ never once scolded him or asked 'Why did you do that?'

questionEn: Which two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ (Fatimah and Umm Kulthum) and his wife Sawdah (RA) were brought safely from Makkah to Madinah right after he settled?
optionsEn: By Zayd ibn Harithah and Abu Rafi' whom the Prophet ﷺ sent back with camels and funds
explanationEn: Alongside Abu Bakr's son Abdullah escorting Umm Ruman, Aishah, and Asma, Zayd ibn Harithah brought Sawdah, Fatimah, Umm Kulthum, Umm Ayman, and young Usamah safely to Madinah.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ NOT choose to live in Makkah permanently later on, even after Makkah was conquered?
optionsEn: To honor the pledge of loyalty he made to the Ansar at Aqabah: 'Living with you and dying with you'
explanationEn: True to his sacred covenant at the Second Pledge of Aqabah, he returned to Madinah after conquering Makkah and after the Farewell Pilgrimage.

questionEn: What did the young girls of Banu al-Najjar sing joyfully with tambourines (duff) as the Prophet ﷺ entered Madinah?
optionsEn: 'We are neighbors from Banu al-Najjar; how blessed is Muhammad as a neighbor!'
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ smiled tenderly at the children of his maternal ancestors (Banu al-Najjar) and asked, 'Do you love me?'—when they said yes, he replied, 'By Allah, I love you too!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ address the fever and homesickness many Makkan Muhajirun (including Abu Bakr and Bilal) suffered soon after arriving in Madinah?
optionsEn: He sent them back to Makkah
He ordered them to fast forty days
He made du'a: 'O Allah, make Madinah as beloved to us as Makkah or even more beloved, bless its measures, and transfer its fever to al-Juhfah'
explanationEn: Allah answered his heartfelt du'a immediately, transforming Madinah into a blessed, healthy, deeply beloved sanctuary.

questionEn: What was the first thing Quraysh did when they discovered Prophet Muhammad ﷺ had safely slipped away from his besieged house?
optionsEn: They sent trackers to Cave Thawr and offered 100 camels, even beating Asma bint Abi Bakr (RA) when she refused to disclose where her father went
They immediately apologized to Abu Talib
explanationEn: Abu Jahl slapped Asma (RA) so hard her earring flew off, yet she steadfastly kept the secret of Cave Thawr.

questionEn: During the boycott of Shi'b Abi Talib, which companion's marriage to the Prophet's ﷺ daughter Zaynab remained intact in Makkah while she stayed behind until after Badr?
explanationEn: Zaynab remained with Abu al-As in Makkah initially; after Badr, she sent her mother Khadijah's necklace to ransom him, moving the Prophet ﷺ to tears and leading to their later reunion in Islam.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Jihad); Seerah Ibn Hisham

questionEn: Why did the Prophet's ﷺ uncle Abu Talib refrain from declaring the Shahadah on his deathbed despite loving and protecting Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: He was unable to speak since childhood
He had already moved to Ta'if
Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah sat beside him and pressured him not to abandon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib
explanationEn: Though Abu Talib testified in poetry that Muhammad's ﷺ religion was the best of all faiths, fear of Qurayshi tribal shame held him back at the final moment.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse was revealed regarding the Prophet's ﷺ intense grief over Abu Talib's passing without accepting Islam?
optionsEn: 'Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills' (Surah Al-Qasas 28:56)
'Hold fast to the rope of Allah' (3:103)
'Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth' (24:35)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Qasas 28:56 comforted the Prophet ﷺ by clarifying that ultimate guidance of hearts belongs solely to Allah.

questionEn: What special permission did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ obtain for his uncle Abu Talib in the Hereafter out of gratitude for his protection?
optionsEn: Full entry into the highest level of Paradise
He will have the lightest punishment of all inhabitants of the Fire—wearing sandals of fire that still cause his brain to boil, whereas otherwise he would have been in the lowest depths
explanationEn: When al-Abbas asked if Abu Talib benefited at all from protecting him, the Prophet ﷺ informed him of this intercessory mitigation.

questionEn: Which aunt/cousin's home in Makkah did the Prophet ﷺ visit or rest at on the night of Al-Isra wal-Mi'raj according to well-known Seerah reports alongside the Hatim?
optionsEn: The house of Umm Hani (Fakhitah bint Abi Talib)
explanationEn: Narrations mention he slept near the Kaaba (in al-Hatim) or at Umm Hani's home near the Haram before Jibril awakened him for the Night Journey.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Anbiya); Seerah Ibn Hisham

questionEn: When Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reached the outer edge of heaven during Al-Mi'raj, what was Jibril's (AS) true angelic appearance like when the Prophet ﷺ saw him a second time (mentioned in Surah Al-Najm)?
optionsEn: Shaped like a cloud of dust
Having six hundred wings filling the horizon, with pearls and rubies dropping from them
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril in his immense created angelic form twice: once filling the Makkan horizon and a second time near Sidrat al-Muntaha.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Bad' al-Khalq); Surah Al-Najm 53:13-15

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stop asking Allah to reduce the five daily prayers further after Musa (AS) advised him to ask for less than five?
optionsEn: He said: 'I have asked my Lord so much that I feel shy before Him; I am satisfied and I submit'
Five was the minimum possible number in Arabic
explanationEn: Out of profound reverence (haya') before Allah, the Prophet ﷺ accepted the five daily prayers gratefully, and a herald proclaimed: 'I have enacted My obligation and lightened the burden on My servants.'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ comfort his weeping daughter as she washed filth thrown upon his blessed head by Makkan mockers after Abu Talib's passing?
optionsEn: One of the insolent fools of Quraysh threw dirt on his blessed head, and as his daughter wept washing it, he comforted her: 'Do not weep, my daughter, for Allah will protect your father'
explanationEn: After Abu Talib's passing, Quraysh grew bold enough to throw filth on his head in the street; he returned home serene and reassured his weeping daughter.

questionEn: In what valley between Ta'if and Makkah did the Jinn hear the Prophet ﷺ reciting the Qur'an in Fajr prayer on his sorrowful return from Ta'if?
explanationEn: Rejected by human leaders in Ta'if, the Prophet ﷺ stood in night/dawn prayer at Wadi Nakhlah, where Allah sent a company of Jinn from Nasibin who listened and believed—consoling his heart.

questionEn: Which two women accompanied the 73 Ansar men to pledge allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ at the Second Pledge of Aqabah?
optionsEn: Nusaibah bint Ka'b (Umm Umarah) and Asma bint Amr ibn Adi (Umm Mani')
Asma bint Abi Bakr and Sawdah
explanationEn: Both Umm Umarah and Umm Mani' took the pledge alongside the men, with the Prophet ﷺ honoring women's pledges verbally without shaking hands with non-mahram women.

questionEn: Who was the first Ansar leader to stretch out his hand and take the Prophet's ﷺ hand in oath at the Second Pledge of Aqabah?
explanationEn: Elderly chief al-Bara ibn Ma'rur grasped the Prophet's ﷺ hand first, pledging by Allah who sent him with truth that they would defend him just as they defended their own families.

questionEn: How did the Islamic Hijri calendar get its starting year (1 AH), later formalized during Caliph Umar's (RA) reign?
optionsEn: From the birth of the Prophet ﷺ
From the year of the Prophet's ﷺ Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah, marking the birth of the unified Muslim community
explanationEn: When Umar (RA) consulted companions on dating official letters, they chose the Hijrah over his birth or first revelation because the Hijrah separated truth from falsehood and established the Islamic community.

questionEn: Why does the Islamic Hijri year begin with Muharram even though the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah in Rabi' al-Awwal?
optionsEn: Because Muharram was the warmest month
Because Quba was built in Muharram
Because the resolve to migrate began right after the Pledge of Aqabah in Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram is the very next lunar month opening the year
explanationEn: The decision and first departures of Muhajirun began immediately following Dhul-Hijjah's Second Pledge of Aqabah, making Muharram the natural start of the Hijri year.

questionEn: What did Abu Bakr's grandfather Abu Quhafah—who was blind and not yet Muslim—ask Asma (RA) when Abu Bakr took all his liquid wealth on the Hijrah?
optionsEn: He chased Abu Bakr to Cave Thawr
He feared Abu Bakr left them penniless, so Asma cleverly placed smooth pebbles in the wall niche covered with a cloth for her blind grandfather to feel, reassuring him
explanationEn: Asma's quick wit comforted her elderly grandfather without lying about their reliance on Allah, while Abu Bakr took ~5,000–6,000 dirhams to serve the fledgling Madinah community.

questionEn: Which two rivers of Paradise did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ see flowing from the base of Sidrat al-Muntaha during Al-Mi'raj?
optionsEn: Two hidden rivers in Paradise and two manifest rivers on earth (symbolically linked to the Nile and Euphrates)
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim, Jibril explained that two were inward rivers in Paradise and two outward rivers on earth—the Nile and the Euphrates.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ see in Al-Mi'raj when shown the punishment of people who backbite and slander their brothers and sisters?
optionsEn: People with copper fingernails scratching their own faces and chests
explanationEn: Jibril told him those were the ones who 'ate the flesh of people' (backbiting) and attacked their honor—a vivid warning against harming fellow believers with the tongue.

questionEn: Who was the Ansar companion from Madinah who wept with joy when welcoming the Prophet ﷺ after the Hijrah, having earlier led the first small group from Madinah?
optionsEn: As'ad ibn Zurarah (RA) and Abu Salamah (RA) who migrated early
explanationEn: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad (RA) was actually the very first Muhajir to reach Madinah—a full year before the Prophet ﷺ—after Quraysh separated him from his wife Umm Salamah and son.

questionEn: How was Umm Salamah (RA) tragically separated from her husband and baby when trying to migrate to Madinah, before finally reuniting there?
optionsEn: She got lost on a ship
Her clan seized her, her husband's clan pulled away baby Salamah, and she wept daily in al-Abtah for a year until her kin pitied her and returned her son so she migrated with Uthman ibn Talhah
explanationEn: On her lonely journey to Madinah, chivalrous Uthman ibn Talhah (then still pagan) escorted her respectfully all the way to Quba before turning back—later becoming a noble Muslim and keeper of the Kaaba's key.

questionEn: Who was the first person to call the Adhan or lead prayer for the earliest Muhajirun in Quba before the Prophet ﷺ arrived?
optionsEn: Salim, freedman of Abu Hudhayfah (RA), because he had memorized the most Qur'an
explanationEn: Salim (RA), a freedman deeply learned in the Qur'an, led senior companions including Umar and Abu Salamah in prayer at Quba—demonstrating Islam's meritocracy over social class.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ask when he first saw the Ansar climbing palm trees and roofs in Madinah waiting anxiously every morning in the heat until he finally appeared?
optionsEn: He asked them to hide indoors
A Jewish onlooker shouted, 'O Banu Qaylah, here is your fortune that you have been waiting for!' and the whole town rushed out shouting Takbir
explanationEn: Every day after Fajr, Madinah's Muslims waited on the volcanic outskirts until midday heat forced them indoors; on that blessed Monday, a man spotted the white-robed travelers from a watchtower.

questionEn: What happened to Abu Bakr's (RA) freedman Amir ibn Fuhayrah (RA)—who tended sheep near Cave Thawr and accompanied the Hijrah—years later at Bi'r Ma'unah?
optionsEn: He was martyred, and his killer witnessed angels raising his body between heaven and earth, prompting the killer himself to embrace Islam
explanationEn: Jabbar ibn Sulma marveled at Amir crying 'By Allah, I have won!' upon being speared and seeing his corpse lifted skyward—leading Jabbar to seek out Islam.

questionEn: Which verse was revealed praising those Muhajirun who sacrificed home and wealth solely for Allah and His Messenger during the Hijrah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Hashr (59:8): 'For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and properties, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure...'
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hashr 59:8 declares those selfless Muhajirun 'the truthful ones' (Al-Sadiqun), followed in 59:9 by eternal praise for the selfless Ansar.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ say of the Ansar: 'Were it not for the Hijrah, I would have been one of the Ansar'?
optionsEn: To express boundless love and gratitude for their unconditional loyalty and sacrifice
Because he was born in Madinah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ even prayed: 'O Allah, have mercy on the Ansar, the children of the Ansar, and the children of the children of the Ansar!'

questionEn: Which two Ansar tribes in Madinah had fought bitter civil wars (culminating in the Battle of Bu'ath) for generations before Islam united them as brothers?
explanationEn: Five years before Hijrah, Aws and Khazraj bled heavily at Bu'ath, exhausting their elders—which Allah used to soften their hearts toward the unifying message of Islam.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Manaqib al-Ansar); Surah Aal Imran 3:103

questionEn: Which Ansar leader organized the very first Jumu'ah prayer in Madinah at Naqi' al-Khadimat even before the Prophet ﷺ arrived?
optionsEn: As'ad ibn Zurarah (RA) organized the first Jumu'ah prayer in Madinah at Naqi' al-Khadimat before the Prophet's ﷺ arrival
explanationEn: As'ad ibn Zurarah gathered forty men in the territory of Banu Bayadah for the earliest Jumu'ah in Madinah even before the Hijrah was completed.

questionEn: What special rank did the Prophet ﷺ assign to the companions who stayed firm during the Makkan ordeal and migrated before the Conquest of Makkah?
optionsEn: 'Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the Victory; they are greater in degree than those who spent and fought afterward' (Surah Al-Hadid 57:10)
explanationEn: Those who endured persecution, boycotts, and migration when Islam had no worldly power hold an unmatched rank of honor.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ask the people of Makkah when he invited tribes at Mina during Hajj before meeting the Ansar?
optionsEn: Only to shelter him so he could convey the Word of his Lord freely, promising Paradise in return
To crown him king of Yemen
explanationEn: Tribes like Banu Amir demanded political succession after him, which he declined because sovereignty belongs to Allah alone—until the sincere Ansar sought only Allah's pleasure and Paradise.

questionEn: Which companion was betrothed to the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah during the late Makkan period (after Khadijah RA) and migrated with Abu Bakr's family to marry him in Madinah?
explanationEn: Khawlah bint Hakim suggested Sawdah (RA) and Aishah (RA) to comfort the Prophet ﷺ after Khadijah's death; the marriage to Aishah (RA) was consummated later in Madinah, where she became the greatest female scholar of Islam.

questionEn: What was the very first communal institution Prophet Muhammad ﷺ personally helped build upon settling in Madinah?
explanationEn: Before building homes for himself or establishing markets, the Prophet ﷺ worked alongside his companions carrying mud bricks to build Al-Masjid an-Nabawi as the spiritual and civic heart of Madinah.

questionEn: What materials were originally used to construct Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in 1 AH?
optionsEn: Sun-dried mud bricks, palm-trunk pillars, and a roof of palm fronds
explanationEn: Simplicity marked the early mosque: mud-brick walls, date-palm trunks as columns, and palm branches overhead that let rain drip through until later expansions.

questionEn: What joyful verse did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions chant together while hauling heavy bricks to build Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, there is no true life except the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Ansar and the Muhajirah!'
explanationEn: Even while carrying heavy stones side by side with Ammar ibn Yasir, the Prophet ﷺ sang uplifting verses reminding them of Jannah.

questionEn: What was 'Al-Suffah' inside the early Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: A shaded platform at the back of the mosque sheltering poor, unmarried emigrants and full-time students of the Qur'an
explanationEn: Ahl al-Suffah (People of the Bench)—including Abu Hurayrah and Bilal—devoted themselves to learning revelation and worship while the Prophet ﷺ and companions shared food with them.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ solve the economic and social crisis of penniless Makkan emigrants (Muhajirun) arriving in Madinah?
optionsEn: Through Al-Mu'akhat (the Covenant of Brotherhood), pairing each Muhajir with an Ansar brother to share homes, work, and support
By sending them back to Abyssinia
explanationEn: Meeting at Anas ibn Malik's home, the Prophet ﷺ paired ~45 Muhajirun with ~45 Ansar in sacred brotherhood that transcended bloodlines.

questionEn: What iconic reply did Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) give when his Ansar brother Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' (RA) offered to split half of all his wealth with him?
optionsEn: 'May Allah bless you in your family and wealth; simply show me the way to the marketplace'
explanationEn: With dignity and gratitude, Abdur-Rahman went to the market of Banu Qaynuqa, traded butter and dried yogurt, and soon became one of Madinah's wealthiest generous benefactors.

questionEn: Whom did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ take as his own special brother during the pairing of Muhajirun and Ansar in Madinah?
explanationEn: When pairing companions, the Prophet ﷺ took Ali's hand and said, 'You are my brother in this world and the Hereafter.'

questionEn: What historic civic charter (Sahifat al-Madinah) did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ establish in 1 AH uniting Muslims and Madinah's Jewish tribes?
optionsEn: A tax-free trade decree for Makkah
A written constitution guaranteeing mutual defense, religious freedom, shared justice, and civic peace under his arbitration
explanationEn: The Constitution of Madinah recognized Muslims as one Ummah while affirming Jewish tribes' religious autonomy and mutual civic obligations to defend Madinah against aggression.

questionEn: How was the Islamic call to prayer (Adhan) introduced in Madinah after companions debated bells, horns, and fires?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA) saw an angel in a true dream teaching the exact words of the Adhan, confirmed independently by Umar (RA), and the Prophet ﷺ instructed Bilal to proclaim it
Abu Bakr copied it from Syria
explanationEn: Recognizing Abdullah ibn Zayd's dream as truth from Allah, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Teach it to Bilal, for he has a sweeter and stronger voice than yours.'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Salah); Jami' al-Tirmidhi

questionEn: Who was the very first Mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer) in Islam, appointed by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Madinah?
explanationEn: Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) became the Prophet's primary caller to prayer, later joined by the blind companion Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA) during Ramadan.

questionEn: For roughly how many months after arriving in Madinah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and the Muslims pray facing Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) before the Qiblah changed?
explanationEn: For 16 or 17 months in Madinah, Muslims faced Jerusalem while the Prophet ﷺ longed and gazed heavenward hoping Allah would turn them toward the Kaaba.

questionEn: In which Islamic month and year was the Qiblah permanently changed from Jerusalem to the Sacred Kaaba in Makkah?
explanationEn: In mid-Sha'ban (or Rajab) of 2 AH, Allah revealed Surah Al-Baqarah (2:144): 'So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram!'

questionEn: Why is Masjid al-Qiblatayn in Madinah famously named 'The Mosque of the Two Qiblahs'?
optionsEn: A congregation there received news mid-prayer that the Qiblah had changed to the Kaaba, so they pivoted 180 degrees mid-Salah
Both Makkah and Jerusalem are visible from its roof
explanationEn: While praying Asr (or Dhuhr) facing north toward Jerusalem in Banu Salamah's mosque, a messenger announced the verse changing the Qiblah, and the entire congregation turned smoothly toward Makkah.

questionEn: Which major pillars of worship—fasting Ramadan, Zakat al-Fitr, and the two Eid prayers—were ordained in Madinah in 2 AH?
optionsEn: Fasting the month of Ramadan, Zakat al-Fitr, and the Eid prayers
explanationEn: In Sha'ban of 2 AH, fasting Ramadan became obligatory, followed by Zakat al-Fitr and the first Eid al-Fitr celebration in Shawwal 2 AH.

questionEn: What well in Madinah did Uthman ibn Affan (RA) buy from a landowner at great expense and dedicate as a free public endowment (waqf) for Muslims?
explanationEn: When Muslims struggled to buy drinking water, the Prophet ﷺ promised Paradise to whoever bought Bi'r Rumah and made it free for all; Uthman (RA) bought half and then the entire well.

questionEn: Which wealthy hypocrite chief in Madinah was about to be crowned king of Yathrib before the Prophet ﷺ arrived, sparking his lifelong resentment?
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Ubayy outwardy professed Islam after Badr while secretly leading the hypocrites (Munafiqun) to undermine the Muslim community.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ initially lead small expeditions to intercept Quraysh caravans heading to Syria in 1–2 AH?
optionsEn: Quraysh had confiscated Muslim homes and wealth in Makkah and remained in an active state of war against Madinah
To steal camel herds for sport
explanationEn: Allah granted permission in Surah Al-Hajj (22:39) to those who were wronged and expelled unjustly from their homes to defend their rights and deter Quraysh aggression.

questionEn: How many Muslims marched out with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Ramadan 2 AH intending originally to intercept Abu Sufyan's caravan—before facing Quraysh's full army at Badr?
explanationEn: Only 313 Muslims—with just 2 horses and 70 camels shared in turns—marched toward Badr, whereas Abu Jahl mobilized ~1,000 heavily armed Quraysh soldiers.

questionEn: Why did Uthman ibn Affan (RA) remain behind in Madinah during the Battle of Badr while still receiving a full share of honor and reward?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ ordered him to stay and nurse his sick wife Ruqayyah (the Prophet's ﷺ daughter), who passed away right as news of Badr victory arrived
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ assured Uthman (RA) he would receive the same reward and share as one who fought at Badr.

questionEn: Before the Battle of Badr began, which Ansar leader reassured the Prophet ﷺ in consultation that the Ansar would follow him even if he marched into the sea?
explanationEn: Because Aqabah's pledge was for defending Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ consulted the Ansar; Sa'd ibn Mu'adh pledged total loyalty wherever he led them, echoing al-Miqdad's vow for the Muhajirun.

questionEn: What did al-Miqdad ibn Amr (RA) famously declare before Badr, contrasting his companions' loyalty with the Bani Isra'il's refusal to follow Musa (AS)?
optionsEn: 'We will never say as Musa's people said: Go you and your Lord and fight! Rather we will fight on your right, your left, in front of you, and behind you!'
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ face lit up with joy upon hearing al-Miqdad's (RA) fearless words of devotion.

questionEn: Which companion suggested a smart tactical adjustment at Badr: moving forward to camp at the nearest water well to Quraysh and blocking the wells behind them?
explanationEn: Al-Hubab respectfully asked whether the first campsite was divine revelation or war strategy; learning it was strategy, he proposed controlling the water cistern, and the Prophet ﷺ immediately adopted his counsel.

questionEn: What two natural blessings did Allah send upon the Muslims the night before the Battle of Badr, mentioned in Surah Al-Anfal (8:11)?
optionsEn: Deep, tranquil slumber removing fear, and gentle rain that purified them, firmed the loose sand underfoot, and turned the enemy's clay ground muddy
explanationEn: Even while severely outnumbered, the believers slept peacefully while Allah strengthened their footing and hearts with rain.

questionEn: Who proposed building a shaded command shelter ('Arish) on a hill overlooking the battlefield of Badr for Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
explanationEn: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh suggested the shelter with swift mounts ready as a safeguard while Abu Bakr stayed beside the Prophet ﷺ inside it, praying fervently.

questionEn: What intense du'a did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ make in his shelter before Badr until his cloak slipped off his shoulders and Abu Bakr gently placed it back?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, if this small band perishes today, You will not be worshiped upon the earth!'
'O Allah, grant us the gold of Damascus'
explanationEn: Abu Bakr embraced him from behind saying, 'Enough, O Messenger of Allah, Allah will fulfill His promise to you!'—and Allah revealed Surah Al-Anfal 8:9 promising 1,000 angels.

questionEn: On which exact date in Ramadan 2 AH did the decisive Battle of Badr—called 'Yawm al-Furqan' (The Day of the Criterion)—take place?
explanationEn: On Friday, 17th of Ramadan 2 AH, Allah separated truth from falsehood decisively at Badr.

questionEn: Which three Qurayshi champions stepped out for single combat at the start of Badr and were defeated by Hamzah, Ali, and Ubaydah ibn al-Harith (RA)?
optionsEn: Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, and al-Walid ibn Utbah
explanationEn: After three young Ansar stepped out and Quraysh demanded peers from their own tribe, the Prophet ﷺ sent Ubaydah, Hamzah, and Ali, who swiftly defeated Quraysh's champions.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Jihad); Seerah Ibn Hisham

questionEn: Which two young Ansar boys—Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh, sons of Afra—eagerly asked Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) at Badr to point out Abu Jahl so they could strike him?
optionsEn: Two teenage Ansar brothers determined to stop the one who insulted the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah
explanationEn: Both boys charged fearlessly through enemy ranks and felled Abu Jahl before Abdullah ibn Mas'ud finished him off.

questionEn: How many Qurayshi soldiers were killed and how many were taken captive at the Battle of Badr?
explanationEn: Despite being outnumbered more than 3-to-1, only 14 Muslims were martyred while 70 Qurayshi leaders/fighters fell and 70 were captured.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ instruct the companions to treat the 70 Qurayshi prisoners captured at Badr?
optionsEn: 'Treat the prisoners well'—companions gave them bread while eating only dates themselves
Exile them to the desert without water
explanationEn: Prisoners like Abu Aziz reported being given the best food (bread) by their captors in Madinah out of obedience to the Prophet's ﷺ command.

questionEn: What remarkable educational ransom did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ offer literate Badr captives who could not afford monetary ransom?
optionsEn: Teaching ten Muslim children of Madinah how to read and write in exchange for their freedom
explanationEn: Highlighting Islam's immense value on literacy and education, Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) was among those who learned writing through this initiative.

questionEn: What moved Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to tears when ransoms for the prisoners of Badr arrived from Makkah?
optionsEn: His daughter Zaynab sent the onyx necklace her late mother Khadijah (RA) had gifted her on her wedding day to ransom her husband Abu al-As
explanationEn: Deeply touched by the memory of Khadijah (RA), the Prophet ﷺ asked the companions' permission to release Abu al-As freely and return Zaynab's necklace, on condition Abu al-As send Zaynab to Madinah.

questionEn: Which two senior companions differed in consultation over the fate of the Badr prisoners—and whose view did the Prophet ﷺ lean toward out of mercy?
optionsEn: Ali advised exile; Uthman advised silence
Abu Bakr advised accepting ransom hoping Allah might guide them later; Umar advised execution of hostile leaders; the Prophet ﷺ inclined toward Abu Bakr's mercy
explanationEn: Comparing Abu Bakr to Prophet Ibrahim/Isa in mercy and Umar to Nuh/Musa in firmness, the Prophet ﷺ chose mercy, though Qur'an (8:67-68) reminded believers about weakening fierce enemies before taking captives.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ have to straighten the row of soldiers at Badr with an arrow—leading Sawad ibn Ghaziyyah (RA) to ask for retaliation and kiss the Prophet's ﷺ uncovered torso?
optionsEn: When the Prophet ﷺ lightly poked Sawad's protruding stomach to align the rank, Sawad playfully asked for equal retribution, then embraced and kissed his torso hoping his last earthly touch would be the Prophet's ﷺ skin
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ immediately lifted his shirt showing absolute equality under the law—even in the middle of battle prep—rewarding Sawad's heartfelt love.

questionEn: Which two Makkans secretly plotted near the Kaaba after Badr to assassinate the Prophet ﷺ—only for Umayr ibn Wahb to embrace Islam when the Prophet ﷺ revealed their secret conversation?
optionsEn: Umayr ibn Wahb and Safwan ibn Umayyah
explanationEn: Umayr slipped into Madinah with a poisoned sword pretending to ransom his son; when the Prophet ﷺ quoted the exact private pact made with Safwan beside the Hatim, Umayr proclaimed the Shahadah immediately.

questionEn: Which Jewish tribe in Madinah broke their peace treaty right after Badr by publicly assaulting a Muslim woman in their marketplace and killing a Muslim defender?
explanationEn: After a goldsmith pinned a Muslim woman's garment to humiliate her and the tribe killed the Muslim who defended her, Banu Qaynuqa barricaded themselves in violation of the Constitution and were expelled.

questionEn: Why was the brief skirmish in 2 AH when Abu Sufyan raided Madinah's outskirts and fled hurriedly named 'Ghazwat al-Sawiq'?
optionsEn: Because fleeing Quraysh raiders dumped sacks of sawiq (parched barley meal) to lighten their camels' load
Because it happened at a bakery
explanationEn: Abu Sufyan had vowed not to wash his hair until avenging Badr; he burned two palm trees at night, killed two farmers, and fled dropping bags of sawiq as Muslims pursued him.

questionEn: During the expedition of Dhat al-Riqa' (or Dhul-Amarr), what happened when an enemy Bedouin named Ghawrath stood over the sleeping Prophet ﷺ with his drawn sword crying 'Who will save you from me now?'
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ calmly answered 'Allah!'—causing the sword to drop from the man's trembling hand, and the Prophet ﷺ pardoned him
explanationEn: When the man dropped the sword, the Prophet ﷺ picked it up and asked, 'Now who will protect you from me?'—then forgave him completely, inspiring the man's awe.

questionEn: How many soldiers did Quraysh bring from Makkah to avenge Badr at the Battle of Uhud in Shawwal 3 AH?
optionsEn: 3,000 fighters (compared to ~700 Muslims after hypocrites deserted)
explanationEn: Quraysh marched with 3,000 men; 1,000 Muslims left Madinah, of whom 300 hypocrites led by Abdullah ibn Ubayy deserted midway, leaving 700 steadfast believers.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ demonstrate consultation (Shura) before the Battle of Uhud even though he initially favored defending inside Madinah?
optionsEn: When younger enthusiastic companions urged fighting outside at Uhud, he yielded to the majority, put on his armor, and refused to reverse the decision once committed
explanationEn: When companions felt bad and offered to follow his initial view, he taught leadership resolve: 'It is not fitting for a prophet, once he puts on his armor, to take it off until Allah decides between him and his enemies.'

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ send young boys like Samurah ibn Jundub and Rafi' ibn Khadij back during troop inspection before Uhud—and why did he permit Rafi' and Samurah later?
optionsEn: Because of their young age (~14-15), until Rafi' proved skilled at archery and Samurah proved he could wrestle Rafi' down!
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ forbade underage children from combat, allowing 15-year-old Rafi' for archery skill and Samurah after he demonstrated equal physical readiness.

questionEn: Who led the 50 archers whom Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stationed on Jabal al-Rumat (the Archers' Hill) at Uhud with strict orders never to leave their post?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ commanded them strictly: 'Even if you see birds snatching our flesh, do not leave your post unless I send for you; and even if you see us victorious, do not leave!'

questionEn: To whom did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ famously award his sword at Uhud after asking 'Who will take this sword with its full right?'
explanationEn: When Abu Dujanah asked what its right was, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'To strike the enemy with it until it bends.' Abu Dujanah tied his red headband of courage and fought fearlessly.

questionEn: What critical mistake by most of the archers on Jabal al-Rumat turned initial Muslim victory at Uhud into a severe setback?
optionsEn: Thinking the battle was won as Quraysh retreated, ~40 archers left their strategic hill for spoils despite Abdullah ibn Jubayr's warnings, allowing Khalid ibn al-Walid's cavalry to strike from behind
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Jubayr and about ten loyal archers stood firm until martyred, while Khalid ibn al-Walid swept around the undefended pass and encircled the Muslims.

questionEn: Which beloved uncle of the Prophet ﷺ—honored as 'Sayyid al-Shuhada' (Master of Martyrs)—was martyred by Wahshi's javelin during the Battle of Uhud?
explanationEn: Wahshi ibn Harb ambushed Hamzah (RA) with a spear from afar for promised freedom; the Prophet ﷺ wept deeply upon seeing Hamzah's mutilated body.

questionEn: Which brave standard-bearer of Islam at Uhud lost both his right and left hands gripping the Muslim banner before being martyred—who had earlier been Islam's first ambassador to Madinah?
explanationEn: Mus'ab bore a resemblance to the Prophet ﷺ, so when Ibn Qami'ah killed him he shouted falsely that Muhammad ﷺ was slain; at burial, Mus'ab had only a short cloak unable to cover both head and feet.

questionEn: Who was the Ansar companion martyred at Uhud whom the Prophet ﷺ saw being washed by angels because he rushed straight to battle from his wedding night without taking ghusl?
explanationEn: Hearing the call to Uhud on his wedding morning, Hanzalah hurried out immediately to defend Islam and earned the eternal honor 'Washed by the Angels.'

questionEn: Which elderly disabled companion with a severe limp insisted on fighting at Uhud against his sons' pleas, declaring 'I hope to tread in Paradise with this limp of mine'?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ honored his sincere plea, and after Amr fell as a martyr at Uhud, the Prophet ﷺ said he saw him walking completely whole in Paradise.

questionEn: Which companion shielded the Prophet's ﷺ face at Uhud with his own hand until his fingers were paralyzed and he bore over seventy wounds?
explanationEn: Talhah intercepted arrows and carried the wounded Prophet ﷺ up the rocks of Uhud; Abu Bakr (RA) called Uhud 'Talhah's day,' and the Prophet ﷺ called him 'a living martyr walking on earth.'

questionEn: Which heroic female companion fought with sword and shield right beside the Prophet ﷺ at Uhud, receiving a deep shoulder wound while defending him?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ remarked: 'Wherever I turned to the right or left at Uhud, I saw Umm Umarah fighting in front of me!'

questionEn: Which two Ansar companions—Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Abu Dujanah—stood beside the Prophet ﷺ, or which arrow-master received the Prophet's ﷺ unmatched praise 'May my father and mother be ransomed for you, shoot!' at Uhud?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ emptied his own quiver before Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) saying 'Shoot, may my father and mother be ransomed for you'—an honor given to no one else.

questionEn: What injuries did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ personally sustain at Uhud when surrounded by enemies?
optionsEn: His lower front tooth was chipped, his lip cut, his forehead wounded, and two iron rings of his helmet drove into his cheek
explanationEn: Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah (RA) extracted the two embedded helmet links with his own teeth, losing two of his own front teeth in the process, while Fatimah (RA) washed the blood and burned a reed mat to stop the bleeding.

questionEn: Which companion first recognized the wounded Prophet ﷺ amidst the chaos of Uhud after rumors spread that he had been killed?
explanationEn: Ka'b ibn Malik recognized the Prophet's ﷺ shining eyes beneath his helmet and shouted joyously that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was alive, though the Prophet ﷺ motioned him to keep quiet so enemies wouldn't swarm them.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pray while wounded on the day of Uhud—and what did he do with the companions who prayed behind him?
optionsEn: He led Dhuhr prayer sitting due to his wounds, and the companions prayed sitting behind him
explanationEn: Demonstrating the priority of Salah even amid extreme crisis and injury, he led congregation seated, and they followed his posture.

questionEn: When Abu Sufyan taunted from the hillside after Uhud, shouting 'Glory to Hubal!' and claiming the day repaid Badr, what reply did the Prophet ﷺ instruct Umar (RA) to shout back?
optionsEn: 'Allah is Most High and Most Majestic! We are not equal: our dead are in Paradise and your dead are in the Fire!'
explanationEn: Even battered and outnumbered, the Prophet ﷺ taught believers never to compromise the honor of Tawhid or confuse an earthly setback with spiritual defeat.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ march out the very next morning after Uhud to Hamra al-Asad despite the believers' heavy wounds?
optionsEn: To deter Quraysh from turning back to attack Madinah and show unbroken Muslim morale (praised in Surah Aal Imran 3:172)
explanationEn: Only those who had fought at Uhud were permitted to join; hearing that Muslims were marching out with high resolve, Abu Sufyan panicked and retreated back to Makkah.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Maghazi); Surah Aal Imran 3:172

questionEn: Which Ansar hero's body at Uhud had over eighty sword, spear, and arrow wounds after he cried out, 'I smell the fragrance of Paradise from beyond Uhud!'?
explanationEn: Having missed Badr, Anas ibn al-Nadr vowed to show Allah what he would do at the next battle; only his sister could identify his mangled body by his fingertip, fulfilling Surah Al-Ahzab 33:23.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forbid immediately after Uhud when his grief over Hamzah's mutilation initially moved him to vow harsh retaliation?
optionsEn: Allah revealed Surah Al-Nahl (16:126-127) urging patience over equal retaliation, so the Prophet ﷺ forgave, exercised patience, and strictly forbade mutilating enemy corpses
explanationEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ restrained natural grief through divine guidance, establishing strict Islamic ethics banning mutilation of the dead in war.

questionEn: How were the 70 martyrs of Uhud buried at the foot of Mount Uhud?
optionsEn: In their blood-stained battle clothes without washing or funeral prayer at that time, often two or three sharing one grave with the one knowing more Qur'an placed first
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ honored the martyrs of Uhud by burying them right where they fell—teaching pilgrims visiting Uhud today to greet those noble companions with Salam.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic Surah devotes roughly sixty verses (3:121–180) to analyzing the spiritual and moral lessons of the Battle of Uhud?
explanationEn: While Surah Al-Anfal centers on Badr, Surah Aal Imran gently heals the believers' hearts after Uhud, highlighting obedience, unity, and trusting Allah even after defeat.

questionEn: Which Ansar woman famously lost her father, brother, and husband at Uhud—yet felt relief only when she saw Prophet Muhammad ﷺ alive, crying 'Every calamity after you is small!'?
optionsEn: A woman of Banu Dinar (also attributed in Seerah to Sumayra bint Qays)
explanationEn: Informed sequentially of her husband's, brother's, and father's martyrdom, she kept asking only 'How is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?' until she saw him safe with her own eyes.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ explain about Mount Uhud years later when looking at it while returning with his companions?
optionsEn: 'This is Uhud—a mountain that loves us and that we love'
explanationEn: Despite the deep grief he suffered there, the Prophet ﷺ turned sorrow into enduring affection for Madinah's sacred mountain.

questionEn: What happened to the Muslim companion Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man (RA) when an arrow struck his eye out of its socket while defending the Prophet ﷺ at Uhud?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ gently pushed the eye back into place with his blessed hand, and it became his healthier and sharper eye
explanationEn: This miracle of healing at Uhud became widely known across Madinah through Qatadah's descendants.

questionEn: Who was the companion sent by the Prophet ﷺ during the chaos of Uhud to check on Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', finding him taking his final breaths with 70 wounds?
optionsEn: Muhammad ibn Maslamah or Ubayy ibn Ka'b / Zayd ibn Thabit (narrated of Zayd)
explanationEn: Dying Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' sent his dying salam to the Prophet ﷺ and a warning to the Ansar: 'You will have no excuse before Allah if the Messenger of Allah is harmed while a single eye among you blinks!'

questionEn: In what year did the Prophet ﷺ marry Hafsah bint Umar (RA) after her husband Khunays ibn Hudhafah passed away from wounds sustained in early battles?
explanationEn: After Uthman and Abu Bakr gently declined Umar's offer (knowing the Prophet ﷺ had mentioned Hafsah), the Prophet ﷺ honored Umar (RA) by marrying Hafsah (RA) in 3 AH.

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers was affectionately known as 'Umm al-Masakin' (Mother of the Poor) for her immense charity, whom the Prophet ﷺ married in 4 AH after her husband died at Uhud?
explanationEn: Zaynab bint Khuzaymah (RA) lived only about two to eight months after marrying the Prophet ﷺ before passing away, leaving a shining legacy of feeding the needy.

questionEn: Which famous grandson of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born to Fatimah (RA) and Ali (RA) in Ramadan of 3 AH?
explanationEn: Al-Hasan (RA) was born in 3 AH and Al-Husayn (RA) in 4 AH; the Prophet ﷺ called them 'the two leaders of the youth of Paradise' and his 'two sweet basil flowers in this world.'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ do when his daughter Fatimah (RA) gave birth to Hasan and Husayn (RA) regarding their naming and Aqiqah?
optionsEn: He gave them the blessed names Hasan and Husayn (rather than 'Harb'), whispered in their ears, shaved their heads, and gave silver equal to the hair's weight in charity
He named them Harb and Murrah
explanationEn: Replacing the harsh pre-Islamic name 'Harb' (War) with 'Hasan' (Beauty/Goodness) reflects the Prophet's ﷺ preference for uplifting, hopeful names.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Adahi); Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: Who was the first newborn baby born among the Muhajirun in Madinah after the Hijrah, whom the Prophet ﷺ blessed with Tahnik (rubbing a chewed date in his mouth)?
explanationEn: His birth (to Asma bint Abi Bakr and Zubayr) shattered a false rumor that magic had made the emigrants barren, filling Madinah with cries of Takbir.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ establish a separate Muslim marketplace in Madinah early after Hijrah?
optionsEn: To move all caravans to Ta'if
To ensure fair trade free of usury (riba), cheating, and unfair taxation, telling them 'This is your market; let it not be diminished nor taxed'
explanationEn: Creating an ethical marketplace helped break predatory monopolies and protected honest merchants.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ personally institute in 1 AH to organize civic defense and know exact population numbers in Madinah?
optionsEn: He built a brick wall around Quba
He conducted a census asking companions to write down the names of everyone who professed Islam—numbering around 1,500 then
explanationEn: Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman narrated that the Prophet ﷺ ordered a written count of Muslims, totaling ~1,500 men and women.

questionEn: Which two tribes of Madinah were originally reconciled inside the Prophet's ﷺ Mosque when verses of Surah Aal Imran (3:103) reminded them how Allah turned their old enmity into brotherhood?
optionsEn: Aws and Khazraj, after Shas ibn Qays tried to revive pre-Islamic war poetry between them
explanationEn: When an instigator recited old Bu'ath war poems nearly sparking a swordfight, the Prophet ﷺ rushed out and reminded them of Allah's blessing of brotherhood, causing them to drop weapons and embrace in tears.
reference: Seerah Ibn Hisham; Surah Aal Imran 3:103

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when Abu Bakr's daughter Aishah (RA) and other Muhajirun suffered fever in Madinah and Bilal recited longing poetry about Makkah?
optionsEn: He prayed that Allah make Madinah even dearer to them than Makkah and bless Madinah's climate and food measures (Sa' and Mudd)
He built a hospital in Quba
He ordered them back to Makkah
explanationEn: His empathetic du'a healed both their bodies and their homesickness, turning Madinah into the spiritual refuge of all believers.

questionEn: Which Ansar companion—after losing his sight or remaining devoted to learning—was the blind Mu'adhdhin alongside Bilal (RA) in Madinah?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ loved and trusted Ibn Umm Maktum (RA) so deeply that he appointed him deputy governor of Madinah over a dozen times when traveling on expeditions.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ask the Ansar to donate—even a single date or palm branch—for the poor Ahl al-Suffah living in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Bunches of dates hung on a rope between two pillars in the mosque so Ahl al-Suffah could eat whenever hungry
explanationEn: Companions regularly hung bunches of fresh dates in the mosque and invited Ahl al-Suffah home in small groups every evening after Isha.

questionEn: What happened when the Prophet ﷺ leaned against a dry date-palm trunk while delivering sermons in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi before a wooden minbar (pulpit) was built?
optionsEn: When he later stepped onto the new three-step wooden minbar, the palm trunk sobbed aloud like a grieving camel until he descended and stroked it gently
explanationEn: Overwhelmed with longing for the Prophet's ﷺ touch and the dhikr it used to hear, the inanimate trunk wept until the Prophet ﷺ comforted it—reminding believers to long even more for closeness to him.

questionEn: Who was the first companion to whom the Prophet ﷺ gave his first battle banner in Madinah (before Badr) to patrol along the coast?
explanationEn: In Ramadan 1 AH, Hamzah (RA) led 30 Muhajirun riders toward Sayf al-Bahr, where Majdi ibn Amr al-Juhani mediated peacefully between them and Abu Jahl's 300 guards.

questionEn: Which Muslim archer shot the very first arrow in the path of Allah during Ubaydah ibn al-Harith's early patrol at Rabigh in 1 AH?
explanationEn: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) proudly recounted that he was the first Arab to shoot an arrow in Allah's path, even when companions ate tree leaves from hunger.

questionEn: What incident occurred during Abdullah ibn Jahsh's (RA) scouting mission to Nakhlah just before Badr, prompting Surah Al-Baqarah (2:217)?
optionsEn: A small Qurayshi caravan was attacked at the end of Rajab without knowing whether the Sacred Month had ended, and Allah clarified that Quraysh's persecution and blocking the Sacred Mosque is far graver
They built a mosque at Nakhlah
explanationEn: When Quraysh hypocritically accused Muslims of violating Rajab, Allah revealed 2:217 exposing Quraysh's far worse crimes of driving believers out of Makkah and barring them from Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: Who was the Qurayshi captive taken at Nakhlah before Badr who immediately accepted Islam when he witnessed the Muslims' nobility, refusing to return with his clan?
explanationEn: Al-Hakam ibn Kaysan remained in Madinah as a sincere Muslim and later achieved martyrdom at Bi'r Ma'unah.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ say before Badr that Allah had promised him one of two groups—either the trade caravan or the Makkan army—and why did Quraysh refuse to turn back even after Abu Sufyan's caravan escaped?
optionsEn: Abu Jahl arrogantly insisted on marching to Badr to party, drink wine, and boast before all Arabs, leading Quraysh to their doom
Abu Sufyan ordered them to attack
Their horses lost the road back
explanationEn: Even after al-Akhnas and Banu Zuhrah wisely turned back when the caravan reached safety, Abu Jahl's pride dragged 1,000 Quraysh warriors into disaster at Badr.

questionEn: Which uncle of the Prophet ﷺ was forced into Quraysh's army at Badr, captured by an Ansar, and later embraced Islam openly—having been secretly friendly to Muslims in Makkah?
explanationEn: Before Badr, the Prophet ﷺ specifically instructed companions not to kill Banu Hashim members like al-Abbas who were compelled to march out.

questionEn: Which former Makkan persecutor of Bilal (RA) was spotted on the battlefield of Badr by Bilal, who cried out 'The head of disbelief, Umayyah ibn Khalaf! May I not survive if he survives!'?
explanationEn: Though Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf tried to take Umayyah as a captive, Bilal rallied the Ansar and justice caught up with the merciless torturer on the battlefield of Badr.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to the slain Qurayshi leaders buried in the dry well (Qalib) of Badr three days after the battle?
optionsEn: He forbade passing Badr ever again
He called them by name asking if they had now found their Lord's promise true, telling astonished companions: 'You do not hear what I say better than they do, though they cannot reply'
He buried his own sword there
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Umar (RA) asked how he spoke to lifeless bodies, and the Prophet ﷺ affirmed that their souls heard his solemn confirmation of Allah's truth.

questionEn: What happened when Abu Lahab—who had stayed behind in Makkah—heard the news of Quraysh's crushing defeat at Badr?
optionsEn: He led a second army to Uhud
Shamed and furious, he beat Abu Rafi', was struck by Umm al-Fadl, and died seven days later of a contagious malignant pustule (al-Adasah) abandoned even by his sons
explanationEn: So foul was his sudden disease that his sons feared approaching him, pushing him into a grave from afar with poles and burying him under stones.

questionEn: What special privilege did Allah grant the warriors who fought at Badr ('Ahl Badr'), as narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari regarding Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ said Allah looked upon the People of Badr and declared: 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you'
explanationEn: Because of their unmatched sincerity when Islam stood on a knife-edge, Ahl Badr earned a unique promise of divine forgiveness and honor—later honored by Jibril asking the Prophet ﷺ how he regarded Ahl Badr.

questionEn: Which two messengers carried the joyous news of the Badr victory back to Madinah—arriving just as Ruqayyah (RA) was being laid to rest?
optionsEn: Zayd ibn Harithah (to the upper city) and Abdullah ibn Rawahah (to the lower city)
explanationEn: Zayd rode the Prophet's ﷺ camel al-Qaswa into Madinah announcing the triumph, mingling public relief with personal grief over Ruqayyah's passing.

questionEn: Who was the Jewish poet of Madinah who traveled to Makkah after Badr to incite Quraysh into launching the revenge attack of Uhud, violating the Constitution of Madinah?
explanationEn: Ka'b wept in Makkah, composed inflammatory verses urging war, and insulted Muslim women in Madinah until Muhammad ibn Maslamah executed him for treason.

questionEn: Who was the noble Jewish scholar from Banu Tha'labah who fought alongside Muslims at Uhud, bequeathed his seven orchards to the Prophet ﷺ for Madinah's poor, and was praised as 'the best of the Jews'?
explanationEn: Mukhayriq told his people that supporting Muhammad ﷺ on that Saturday was a duty; he fell martyred at Uhud, and his seven orchards became the Prophet's ﷺ first charitable endowments (sadaqah) in Madinah.

questionEn: Who sent a sealed secret letter to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ just days before Uhud warning him that Quraysh had mobilized 3,000 soldiers?
optionsEn: His uncle Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib from Makkah
explanationEn: Al-Abbas hired a fast Ghifari courier to ride 10 days' journey in 3 days, enabling the Prophet ﷺ to prepare Madinah before Quraysh arrived.

questionEn: What symbolic dream did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ see shortly before the Battle of Uhud—and how did he interpret it?
optionsEn: Cows being slaughtered, a notch in the tip of his sword, and placing his hand in a sturdy coat of armor—representing martyrs from his companions, harm to a family member, and Madinah's safety
explanationEn: Though the dream pointed to staying in Madinah's 'sturdy armor,' the Prophet ﷺ respected majority Shura to march to Uhud; the notch foretold Hamzah's martyrdom.

questionEn: Which Muslim commander initially defeated Quraysh's standard-bearers one after another at Uhud before the archers left their post?
optionsEn: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA), Hamzah (RA), and al-Zubayr (RA)
explanationEn: All nine standard-bearers of Banu Abd al-Dar were struck down by Muslim champions until the Makkan army broke and fled—before the flank vulnerability reversed the tide.

questionEn: Which Qurayshi warrior, later to become the legendary Muslim general 'Sayfullah,' led the cavalry flank attack at Uhud when the Muslim archers left Jabal al-Rumat?
explanationEn: Noticeable for his keen military eye, Khalid spotted the empty pass behind the Muslims and swung his cavalry around, catching the scattered Muslims off guard.

questionEn: Which Ansar companion pledged with six others to form a living human shield around the Prophet ﷺ at Uhud, fighting off waves of attackers until all seven fell or fainted?
optionsEn: Ziyad ibn al-Sakan (and companions like Abu Dujanah and Talhah)
explanationEn: As the last survivor of that small Ansar group fell bleeding, the Prophet ﷺ asked to bring Ziyad close, and Ziyad passed away with his cheek resting on the Prophet's ﷺ blessed foot.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about Umm Sulaym and Aishah (RA) whom Anas saw bustling briskly on the battlefield of Uhud?
optionsEn: They guarded the camels in Madinah
They rolled up their garments and carried heavy leather waterskins on their backs to quench the wounded soldiers' thirst
explanationEn: Muslim women played vital medical and logistical roles at Uhud, tending the wounded and supplying water under arrow fire.

questionEn: What severe warning did Allah reveal in Surah Aal Imran (3:144) right after rumors of the Prophet's ﷺ death at Uhud shook some companions?
optionsEn: 'Muhammad is not but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed on before him. So if he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels?'
explanationEn: Years later when the Prophet ﷺ actually passed away, Abu Bakr (RA) recited this exact verse (3:144) to steady the stunned Muslim community.

questionEn: What harsh treatment befell the Prophet's ﷺ personal enemy Ubayy ibn Khalaf when he charged toward the wounded Prophet ﷺ at Uhud swearing to kill him?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ took a spear from al-Harith ibn al-Simmah and struck Ubayy slightly on the neck—giving him a tiny scratch from which Ubayy screamed 'Muhammad has killed me!' and died en route to Makkah
explanationEn: Years earlier in Makkah, Ubayy boasted he was fattening a horse to kill the Prophet ﷺ, who replied 'Nay, I will kill you, in sha' Allah!'—making Ubayy the only man the Prophet ﷺ ever fatally struck in his entire life.

questionEn: What did Hind bint Utbah do at Uhud in bitter vengeance for her father and relatives killed at Badr—and how did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ still forgive her years later?
optionsEn: She mutilated Hamzah's body and chewed his liver; yet at the Conquest of Makkah she embraced Islam and the Prophet ﷺ pardoned her completely
explanationEn: Remarkably, both Hind bint Utbah and Wahshi ibn Harb (who killed Hamzah) later embraced Islam and were pardoned by the Prophet ﷺ—demonstrating Islam's unmatched power of forgiveness.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ wrap Hamzah (RA) and Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) in such humble shrouds at Uhud that companions wept decades later remembering it?
optionsEn: Mus'ab's single cloak only covered his head leaving his feet bare, or his feet leaving his head bare—so the Prophet ﷺ covered his head with the cloak and his feet with idhkhir grass
explanationEn: Decades later when Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) was served rich food while fasting, he wept recalling that Mus'ab—a far better man—didn't even have a full shroud, fearing earthly luxury might exhaust their reward.

questionEn: What heartwarming reassurance did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) after his father Abdullah ibn Haram was martyred at Uhud leaving behind young daughters and debt?
optionsEn: That debts were canceled by force
That Allah spoke directly to Abdullah without a veil or translator, asking him what he wished—and Abdullah wished only to return to earth and be martyred again for Allah!
explanationEn: Upon hearing Jabir's father's wish, Allah revealed Surah Aal Imran (3:169): 'And never think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.'
reference: Jami' al-Tirmidhi (Kitab al-Tafsir); Surah Aal Imran 3:169

questionEn: Which tragic betrayal in 4 AH involved 70 devout Qur'an memorizers (Qurra') sent by the Prophet ﷺ to teach Islam in Najd, only to be ambushed at a well?
explanationEn: Requested by Abu Bara Amir ibn Malik for Najd, 70 scholar-companions (including Amir ibn Fuhayrah and Anas's uncle Haram ibn Milhan) were treacherously surrounded by Amir ibn al-Tufayl and massacred.

questionEn: What did the martyred companion Haram ibn Milhan (RA) cry out at Bi'r Ma'unah as a spear pierced his back and came out his chest—so inspiring his killer that the killer later embraced Islam?
optionsEn: 'Fuztu wa-Rabbil-Ka'bah!' ('I have won, by the Lord of the Kaaba!')
explanationEn: Baffled by how a dying man could claim victory, Jabbar ibn Sulma investigated Islam and later embraced the faith wholeheartedly.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond spiritually for an entire month in Fajr prayer after the treacherous massacre of the 70 Qur'an scholars at Bi'r Ma'unah?
optionsEn: He stood in Qunut al-Nazilah (supplication in calamity) during Fajr prayer for 30 days praying against the treacherous tribes of Ri'l, Dhakwan, and Usayyah
He closed Masjid an-Nabawi for a month
explanationEn: Anas (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ never grieved as intensely over anything as he did for those 70 Qur'an teachers, reciting Qunut until Allah revealed a comforting message about their entry into Paradise.

questionEn: In the parallel betrayal of Al-Raji' (4 AH), which two captured Muslim teachers were sold to Makkans and executed, famously praying two rak'ahs before martyrdom?
optionsEn: Khubayb ibn Adi (RA) and Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah (RA)
explanationEn: Khubayb (RA) asked to pray two brief rak'ahs before execution so they would not think he feared death—establishing the Sunnah of praying two rak'ahs before martyrdom.

questionEn: What did Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah (RA) reply when Abu Sufyan asked him just before execution in Makkah whether he wished Muhammad ﷺ were in his place while he sat safe at home?
optionsEn: 'By Allah, I would not wish even a thorn to prick Muhammad ﷺ where he is right now in exchange for my being safely with my family!'
explanationEn: Abu Sufyan marveled aloud: 'I have never seen anyone love another person the way Muhammad's companions love Muhammad!'

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ lay siege to Banu Nadir in 4 AH, leading to their exile from Madinah (chronicled in Surah Al-Hashr)?
optionsEn: When he visited them peacefully seeking treaty-obligated blood-money aid, they plotted to drop a heavy millstone on his head from a rooftop
explanationEn: Informed by Angel Jibril of their assassination plot, the Prophet ﷺ stood up calmly, returned to Madinah, and besieged Banu Nadir after they broke their covenant.
