questionEn: Which Surah—originally referred to by Ibn Abbas (RA) as 'Surah Bani Nadir'—describes the bloodless victory over Banu Nadir and distribution of Fay' wealth to the poor Muhajirun?
explanationEn: Because Banu Nadir surrendered without fighting, their lands became Fay' (wealth gained without combat), which the Prophet ﷺ distributed carefully to elevate the poor Muhajirun.

questionEn: Why was the expedition of Dhat al-Riqa' (4/5 AH) given the name 'The Expedition of Patches'?
optionsEn: Because the companions' feet bled over sharp rocky ground until their nails fell off and they wrapped rags/patches around their feet
explanationEn: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) described six men sharing a single camel in turns, tying rags around bruised feet—and asked his listener not to spread it widely out of modesty.

questionEn: Which unique prayer format did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ first perform and teach the Ummah during the Expedition of Dhat al-Riqa'?
optionsEn: Salat al-Khawf (The Prayer of Fear, praying in alternating shifts while facing potential enemy ambush)
explanationEn: Demonstrating that Salah is never abandoned even in active war zones, one group stood guard while the Prophet ﷺ led the other group, then rotated.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ march to Badr a second time in Sha'ban 4 AH ('Badr al-Maw'id')—returning victorious without a single battle?
optionsEn: To honor the appointment Abu Sufyan had challenged him to at the end of Uhud; Quraysh turned back halfway due to drought and fear
explanationEn: Showing total reliability and courage, the Prophet ﷺ camped at Badr for eight days while Muslims traded peacefully and won immense prestige across Arabia.

questionEn: How many allied coalition soldiers (Al-Ahzab) marched on Madinah in Shawwal 5 AH during the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq)?
explanationEn: Incited by exiled leaders of Banu Nadir, a massive confederacy of 10,000 fighters converged on Madinah's ~3,000 defenders.

questionEn: Which Persian companion famously proposed digging a defensive trench (Khandaq) along Madinah's exposed northern flank—a tactic unfamiliar to Arab warfare?
explanationEn: Salman (RA) shared how Persians dug trenches when besieged; the Prophet ﷺ embraced the idea and divided the 5.5 km northern border into ten-yard sections for groups of ten companions.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ personally share the physical hunger and labor of digging the Trench alongside his companions?
optionsEn: He swung the pickaxe, carried earth until his chest was covered in dust, and tied a stone over his stomach against hunger—just as companions tied one
explanationEn: When Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) saw the Prophet ﷺ with a stone bound against his starving stomach, he hurried home to prepare a modest meal of one goat kid and barley—which Allah multiplied to feed all 1,000 diggers!

questionEn: What three grand future conquests did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ prophesy when three sparks flew as he shattered a huge stubborn rock in the Trench with his pickaxe?
optionsEn: The palaces of Syria (Byzantium), Persia (Mada'in), and Yemen (Sanaa)
explanationEn: While hypocrites mocked starving men promising empires, every single spark's prophecy materialized within a generation!

questionEn: During the Battle of the Trench, which famed Qurayshi horseman leaped across a narrow gap in the trench and challenged the Muslims—only to be slain in a duel by Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)?
explanationEn: Amr was considered equal to a thousand horsemen; Ali (RA) offered him Islam or retreat first, then defeated him decisively, shattering Quraysh's morale.

questionEn: Which tribe inside Madinah treacherously broke their defense pact at the height of the Battle of the Trench, threatening Muslim women and children from the rear?
explanationEn: Persuaded by Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Banu Qurayzah tore up their alliance at the most perilous hour, creating the terror described in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:10): 'Eyes grew wild and hearts reached the throats.'

questionEn: Which newly converted companion from Ghatafan—whose conversion was unknown to both Quraysh and Banu Qurayzah—brilliantly sowed mutual distrust between the besiegers during Khandaq?
explanationEn: When Nu'aym offered to fight, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'You are just one man, so go and sow discord among them if you can, for war is strategy (khad'ah)'—and Nu'aym's diplomacy paralyzed the coalition!

questionEn: Which companion was chosen by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ on a freezing, pitch-black night at Khandaq to slip silently into the enemy camp and bring intelligence?
explanationEn: Although trembling from cold and hunger, the Prophet's ﷺ comforting touch warmed Hudhayfah completely; he witnessed a fierce freezing wind (Rih al-Saba) overturn Quraysh's pots and tents, forcing the Ahzab to flee.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ announce right after the Battle of the Trench ended, declaring the strategic turning point in the war with Quraysh?
optionsEn: 'Now we shall march against them, and they will never march against us; we will advance toward them!'
explanationEn: Khandaq was Quraysh's final offensive against Madinah; from that night onward, the initiative shifted decisively to Islam.

questionEn: Whom did Banu Qurayzah themselves choose to arbitrate their fate after their treason during Khandaq—who judged them according to their own Torah law (Deuteronomy 20)?
optionsEn: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA), chief of Aws and their longtime ally
explanationEn: Banu Qurayzah trusted their former ally Sa'd ibn Mu'adh to judge; wounded from Khandaq, Sa'd ruled that active combatants be executed and non-combatants spared—which the Prophet ﷺ confirmed matched Allah's decree from above seven heavens.

questionEn: What extraordinary honor occurred when Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA) passed away shortly after the Banu Qurayzah verdict from his Khandaq wound?
optionsEn: The Throne of the Most Merciful (Arsh al-Rahman) shook at his passing, and 70,000 angels attended his funeral
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ walked swiftly in his funeral procession, explaining that 70,000 angels who had never descended to earth before came down to honor Sa'd.

questionEn: During the Battle of the Trench, why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pray Asr after sunset one day—later inspiring the verse 'Guard strictly the prayers, especially the Middle Prayer'?
optionsEn: There was no water in Madinah
Continuous enemy assaults kept the Muslims pinned down fighting until sunset, prompting the Prophet ﷺ to pray Dhuhr/Asr consecutively afterward
explanationEn: Showing how intensely the battle raged, the Prophet ﷺ prayed missed prayers in order upon relief, establishing the rule for making up prayers delayed by extreme combat.

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ marry in 5 AH after her divorce from Zayd ibn Harithah, permanently abolishing pre-Islamic legal adoption erasing true lineage?
explanationEn: Revealed in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:37), Allah Himself ordained this marriage to teach that adopted sons are not biological sons, ending a deep-rooted pre-Islamic taboo.

questionEn: Which captive daughter of Banu al-Mustaliq's chief did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ marry in 5/6 AH after paying her contract of freedom—leading the Muslims to free over 100 families of her tribe out of respect?
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) noted: 'I know of no woman who brought greater blessing to her people than Juwayriyah'—for her entire tribe embraced Islam seeing the Muslims' nobility.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Itq); Seerah Ibn Hisham

questionEn: What painful trial known as 'Hadith al-Ifk' (The Slander) occurred on the return from the Banu al-Mustaliq expedition?
optionsEn: Money was stolen from the treasury
Hypocrites led by Abdullah ibn Ubayy spread false slander against Aishah (RA) after her camel litter departed without her while she searched for a lost necklace
explanationEn: For an agonizing month Aishah (RA) and the Prophet ﷺ endured cruel rumors until Allah Himself revealed ten verses in Surah Al-Nur (24:11-20) declaring her absolute innocence.

questionEn: Which verse in Surah Al-Nur rebuked Abu Bakr (RA) when he briefly swore to stop supporting his poor relative Mistah ibn Uthathah who had echoed the slander against Aishah (RA)?
optionsEn: 'Let them pardon and overlook. Would you not love that Allah should forgive you?' (Surah Al-Nur 24:22)
'Hold fast to the rope of Allah' (3:103)
explanationEn: Hearing 24:22, Abu Bakr (RA) immediately cried, 'Yes, by Allah, I love that Allah should forgive me!' and resumed supporting Mistah forever.

questionEn: How many companions set out with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Dhul-Qa'dah 6 AH wearing Ihram and bringing sacrificial camels solely to perform a peaceful Umrah?
explanationEn: Carrying only sheathed travelers' swords and marking 70 sacrificial camels, ~1,400 unarmed pilgrims marched toward Makkah seeking only to worship at Allah's Sacred House.

questionEn: Where did the Prophet's ﷺ camel Al-Qaswa unexpectedly kneel outside Makkah during the Umrah march of 6 AH—and how did he interpret it?
optionsEn: At Al-Hudaybiyyah; he said 'She has not grown stubborn—rather, the One who restrained the Elephant (from Makkah) has restrained her!'
explanationEn: Recognizing Allah's decree, he pledged to accept any peaceful proposal from Quraysh that honored Allah's sacred sanctuaries.

questionEn: What miracle occurred at Al-Hudaybiyyah when 1,400 companions ran out of water beside a dry well?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ drew an arrow from his quiver and placed it in the well—or placed his hand in a basin—and fresh water gushed up abundantly for everyone and every animal
explanationEn: Al-Bara ibn Azib and Jabir (RA) narrated how water welled up powerfully until every single pilgrim and animal drank and filled their vessels.

questionEn: Why was the famous pledge under the acacia tree at Hudaybiyyah ('Bay'at al-Ridwan') originally taken by the 1,400 companions?
optionsEn: Rumors spread that Quraysh had murdered the Prophet's ﷺ envoy Uthman ibn Affan (RA), so the companions pledged to stand firm unto death
explanationEn: Allah declared His eternal pleasure with those who pledged under the tree (Surah Al-Fath 48:18), and the Prophet ﷺ placed his own left hand over his right hand on behalf of absent Uthman (RA)!

questionEn: Which Qurayshi diplomat sent to Hudaybiyyah returned astounded by the companions' reverence for the Prophet ﷺ, saying 'I have visited Chosroes, Caesar, and Negus, yet never seen a leader loved like Muhammad'?
explanationEn: Urwah witnessed companions catching his ablution water and lowering their voices before him—a reverence that later moved Urwah himself to embrace Islam.

questionEn: Who represented Quraysh in negotiating and signing the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah—prompting the Prophet ﷺ to remark cheerfully 'Your affair has been made easy (Suhayl)'?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ loved good omens, reading Suhayl's name ('Easy') as a hopeful sign of peaceful agreement.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ show extraordinary diplomatic humility when Suhayl ibn Amr objected to writing 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim' and 'Muhammad Messenger of Allah' in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?
optionsEn: He ordered Umar to write it
He agreed to write 'Bismika Allahumma' and 'Muhammad ibn Abdullah'—and when Ali (RA) hesitated to erase 'Messenger of Allah,' the Prophet ﷺ erased it with his own hand
explanationEn: Prioritizing substantive peace and long-term da'wah over formal titles, the Prophet ﷺ knew he remained Allah's Messenger regardless of ink on parchment.

questionEn: What were the core terms agreed upon in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (6 AH)?
optionsEn: A 10-year truce, Muslims return this year and perform a 3-day Umrah next year, tribes may ally freely, and Makkan converts without guardians' permission are returned while Madinah defectors are not
explanationEn: Though the unequal repatriation clause initially pained companions like Umar (RA), it turned out to be a brilliant strategic triumph that removed hostilities and sparked mass conversions.

questionEn: What happened moments before the ink dried at Hudaybiyyah when Suhayl's own persecuted Muslim son Abu Jandal stumbled into camp in chains seeking asylum?
optionsEn: Honoring the newly agreed treaty strictly, the Prophet ﷺ returned Abu Jandal to Suhayl, reassuring him: 'Be patient, for Allah will grant you and the oppressed a way out'
He hid Abu Jandal in a tent
explanationEn: Maintaining absolute integrity to his pledged word even at agonizing cost taught the world Islamic fidelity to treaties—and soon Abu Basir and Abu Jandal formed an independent coastal camp that forced Quraysh to beg the Prophet ﷺ to cancel that very clause!

questionEn: Whose wise practical advice saved the companions from despair at Hudaybiyyah when they hesitated three times to sacrifice their animals and shave their heads?
optionsEn: Umm Salamah (RA), who advised the Prophet ﷺ to go out silently, sacrifice his own camel, and call his barber—whereupon everyone immediately followed him
explanationEn: Umm Salamah's (RA) perceptive counsel demonstrated the Prophet's ﷺ deep respect for his wife's political and spiritual wisdom.

questionEn: Which Surah was revealed on the journey back from Hudaybiyyah declaring the truce 'Fathan Mubina' (a manifest victory)?
explanationEn: Calling Hudaybiyyah 'a clear victory' astonished companions who thought they had compromised—until two years of peace saw more people enter Islam than in the previous nineteen years combined!

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ have a silver signet ring engraved with 'Muhammad Rasul Allah' made after returning from Hudaybiyyah?
optionsEn: To wear on his left thumb
Because companions informed him that foreign kings and emperors would not accept unsealed diplomatic letters
explanationEn: Preparing to send letters calling kings to Islam, he engraved the ring in three stacked lines—'Allah' at top, 'Rasul' in middle, 'Muhammad' at bottom—so no letter lacked sovereign authority.

questionEn: Which Byzantine Emperor received the Prophet's ﷺ letter via Dihyah al-Kalbi (RA) in Syria and questioned Abu Sufyan closely to verify Muhammad's ﷺ prophethood?
explanationEn: Heraclius tested Abu Sufyan on the Prophet's ﷺ lineage, truthfulness, followers, and loyalty, concluding: 'If what you say is true, he will soon possess the very ground beneath my two feet!'

questionEn: What arrogant mistake did the Persian Emperor Khosrow II (Kisra) commit upon receiving Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ letter—and what did the Prophet ﷺ foretell?
optionsEn: Khosrow tore the letter into shreds, and the Prophet ﷺ prayed: 'May Allah tear his kingdom into shreds!'—which unfolded swiftly through Persia's collapse
explanationEn: Contrastingly, when Khosrow ordered Yemen's governor Badhan to arrest the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ informed Badhan's envoys that Khosrow had just been assassinated by his own son that very night—leading Badhan and Yemen to accept Islam!

questionEn: How did Al-Muqawqis, ruler of Egypt (Alexandria), respond to the Prophet's ﷺ diplomatic letter delivered by Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah (RA)?
optionsEn: He received it respectfully, placed it in an ivory casket, and sent gifts including Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah, her sister Sirin, and the white mule Duldul
explanationEn: Though worldly rule kept al-Muqawqis from openly declaring Islam, he acknowledged a prophet was awaited and honored the envoy with courtesy.

questionEn: Who was the ruler of Bahrain (Hajar) who embraced Islam wholeheartedly along with his people after receiving the Prophet's ﷺ letter through al-Ala ibn al-Hadrami?
explanationEn: Al-Mundhir wrote back accepting Islam warmly and asking how to handle Zoroastrian and Jewish residents, receiving wise guidance on religious tolerance and jizyah.

questionEn: Which two rulers of Oman embraced Islam when Amr ibn al-As (RA) delivered the Prophet's ﷺ letter inviting them to the faith?
optionsEn: Jayfar and Abd, sons of al-Julanda
explanationEn: Oman's people embraced Islam peacefully without war, sending zakat and welcoming Muslim educators.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ march to the fortified oasis of Khaybar in Muharram 7 AH right after Hudaybiyyah?
optionsEn: Khaybar had become the headquarters of exiled Banu Nadir chiefs who organized the Trench coalition and continued plotting alliances against Madinah
explanationEn: With Quraysh neutralized by the 10-year truce, only the 1,400 faithful companions of Bay'at al-Ridwan were permitted to join the Khaybar campaign, neutralizing the northern threat.

questionEn: What famous announcement did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ make at night before the decisive conquest of Khaybar's stubborn fortress?
optionsEn: 'Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love, at whose hands Allah will grant victory!'
explanationEn: Every companion hoped to be chosen; the next morning the Prophet ﷺ summoned Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA), cured his painful eye infection with his saliva and du'a, and handed him the banner.

questionEn: What core instruction did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give Ali (RA) as he handed him the banner at Khaybar?
optionsEn: 'Proceed calmly until you halt in their courtyard, then invite them to Islam—for by Allah, if Allah guides even one person through you, it is better for you than red camels!'
explanationEn: Even amid siege warfare, the Prophet ﷺ prioritized peaceful invitation and human guidance above all material spoils.

questionEn: Which fierce fortress champion of Khaybar did Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) defeat in single combat before storming Fort al-Qamus?
explanationEn: Marhab boasted in verse of his might; Ali (RA) struck him down cleanly, opening the gates of Khaybar's strongest citadel.

questionEn: What touching reunion took place right after the victory of Khaybar, moving the Prophet ﷺ to say 'I do not know which brings me greater joy: the conquest of Khaybar or the return of Ja'far'?
optionsEn: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (RA) and the remaining emigrants from Abyssinia arrived safely in Khaybar
explanationEn: After more than a decade in Abyssinia, Ja'far (RA) and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) arrived just as Khaybar fell, and the Prophet ﷺ kissed Ja'far between the eyes.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ arrange land stewardship at Khaybar after its inhabitants surrendered?
optionsEn: He sold the land to Quraysh
He let the Jewish farmers stay and cultivate the fertile orchards in exchange for half the annual harvest
explanationEn: Because they were expert farmers and Madinah lacked agricultural labor, this fair sharecropping arrangement benefited both communities peacefully.

questionEn: What grave peril did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ survive at Khaybar when a hostile woman named Zaynab bint al-Harith served him a roasted shoulder of mutton laced with deadly poison?
optionsEn: After taking one chew, the meat spoke miraculously warning him 'I am poisoned,' so he spat it out—though Bishr ibn al-Bara swallowed some and passed away
He refused to eat meat entirely
explanationEn: The lingering effect of that poison caused recurring pain up to the Prophet's ﷺ final illness years later, earning him the spiritual rank of martyrdom alongside prophethood.

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers—noble descendant of Prophet Harun (AS) and daughter of Huyayy ibn Akhtab—did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ free and honorably marry after Khaybar?
explanationEn: When Safiyyah (RA) chose Allah and His Messenger over returning to her defeated kin, the Prophet ﷺ freed her and made her emancipation her dowry, later defending her proudly against anyone who mocked her Jewish heritage.

questionEn: Which Abyssinian-hosted daughter of Abu Sufyan did the Prophet ﷺ marry via King Negus's proxy (around 7 AH) while her father was still Madinah's enemy?
explanationEn: When her former husband Ubaydullah apostatized in Abyssinia, Umm Habibah held firm to Islam alone; the Prophet ﷺ honored her devotion by marrying her, with Negus paying her dowry of 400 dinars.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ execute a shepherd named Mid'am—or announce that a servant named Mid'am was in Hellfire despite dying alongside Muslims at Khaybar?
optionsEn: Because Mid'am had secretly stolen a single woolen cloak (shamla) from the public spoils before distribution (Ghulul)
explanationEn: This sobering moment taught the entire army absolute honesty regarding public funds—leading another companion to promptly return even two shoelaces he had taken!

questionEn: What spiritual prohibitions were formally announced by the Prophet ﷺ during the Khaybar campaign?
optionsEn: The prohibition of temporary marriage (Mut'ah) and eating domestic donkey meat (as well as fanged predators and taloned birds)
explanationEn: Ali (RA) narrated clearly in Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim that at Khaybar the Prophet ﷺ prohibited temporary marriage and domestic donkey meat.

questionEn: What joyful pilgrimage did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and ~2,000 Muslims finally perform in Dhul-Qa'dah 7 AH under the terms of Hudaybiyyah?
explanationEn: Returning to Makkah peacefully after seven years of exile, Quraysh vacated the valley to watch from Mount Qu'ayqi'an while Muslims performed Tawaf briskly (Ramal) to show strength.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ instruct the companions to perform 'Ramal' (brisk walking) during the first three circuits of Tawaf during Umrat al-Qada?
optionsEn: To refute Quraysh's mocking rumor that Madinah's fever had weakened the Muslims
explanationEn: Covering their right shoulders (Idtiba') and jogging briskly for the first three rounds, Muslims showed vibrant health—leaving behind a lasting Sunnah for men in Tawaf al-Qudum/Umrah.

questionEn: Who led the Prophet's ﷺ camel Al-Qaswa into Makkah during Umrat al-Qada reciting fiery inspiring poetry, prompting Umar (RA) to caution him inside the Haram?
explanationEn: When Umar rebuked Ibn Rawahah for reciting poetry in the Sacred Mosque, the Prophet ﷺ gently intervened: 'Leave him, O Umar, for his words are swifter upon them than arrows!'

questionEn: Who was the very last Mother of the Believers whom Prophet Muhammad ﷺ married, at Sarif right as he concluded Umrat al-Qada in 7 AH?
explanationEn: Sister-in-law of al-Abbas (and aunt of Ibn Abbas and Khalid ibn al-Walid), Maymunah (RA) was invited to celebrate her wedding feast in Makkah, though Quraysh forced the Muslims out after three days—so the wedding took place at Sarif, where she was also later buried.

questionEn: Which three future pillars of Islam—including Quraysh's top military strategist—rode voluntarily to Madinah to accept Islam right after Umrat al-Qada in early 8 AH?
optionsEn: Khalid ibn al-Walid, Amr ibn al-As, and Uthman ibn Talhah (RA)
explanationEn: Recognizing that every path before truth was clear, Khalid, Amr, and Uthman (guardian of the Kaaba's key) met along the road to Madinah; seeing them, the Prophet ﷺ rejoiced: 'Makkah has thrown to us the finest pieces of her liver!'

questionEn: What heartwarming custody dispute occurred at the end of Umrat al-Qada when Hamzah's young daughter Umamah ran calling 'Uncle, uncle!' after the Muslims leaving Makkah?
optionsEn: Ali, Ja'far, and Zayd each claimed the honor of raising her, and the Prophet ﷺ ruled in favor of Ja'far because his wife Asma bint Umays was her maternal aunt ('The maternal aunt holds the status of a mother')
explanationEn: To comfort all three competing companions tenderly, the Prophet ﷺ praised each one personally: telling Ali 'You are from me and I am from you,' Ja'far 'You resemble my appearance and character,' and Zayd 'You are our brother and freedman.'

questionEn: Which companion—known as 'Abu Basir'—escaped Quraysh custody after being returned under Hudaybiyyah and set up a coastal camp at Al-Is until Quraysh begged the Prophet ﷺ to waive the return clause?
explanationEn: Joined by Abu Jandal and ~70 Makkan escapes outside Madinah's treaty jurisdiction, their threat to Syrian caravans compelled Quraysh to ask the Prophet ﷺ to accept Makkan converts into Madinah freely!

questionEn: What did Allah reveal in Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:10) when believing women like Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah migrated alone to Madinah after Hudaybiyyah?
optionsEn: To examine the sincerity of their faith and NOT return believing women to polytheists, while compensating their disbelieving husbands for their dowries
explanationEn: Because Hudaybiyyah's Arabic text mentioned 'rajul' (men) returning, Allah protected refugee believing women from forced return into religious persecution.

questionEn: Where did Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) call the Adhan in Makkah during Umrat al-Qada in 7 AH while watching Quraysh elders looked on?
optionsEn: During Umrat al-Qada, Bilal called the Adhan for Dhuhr from inside/beside the Kaaba courtyard, enraging watching Quraysh chiefs on the hills above
explanationEn: Hearing the formerly enslaved Bilal proclaim 'Allahu Akbar' across Makkah echoed the total transformation of human dignity brought by Islam.

questionEn: Which verse of Surah Al-Ahzab (33:33) was revealed purifying Ahl al-Bayt (the Prophet's ﷺ household), after which the Prophet ﷺ gathered Fatimah, Ali, Hasan, and Husayn under his cloak?
optionsEn: 'Allah only wishes to remove impurity from you, O People of the Household, and to purify you thoroughly'
'Indeed We sent you as a mercy'
explanationEn: In Hadith al-Kisa' (Sahih Muslim), he draped his black woolen cloak over Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn and prayed: 'O Allah, these are the People of my House; remove impurity from them and purify them thoroughly.'
reference: Sahih Muslim (Kitab Fada'il al-Sahabah); Surah Al-Ahzab 33:33

questionEn: Which expedition in 5/6 AH saw Prophet Muhammad ﷺ travel northward to Dumat al-Jandal near the Syrian border to secure northern trade routes?
explanationEn: Marching with 1,000 companions against highway-raiding tribes near Dumat al-Jandal, the raiders fled at his approach, establishing northern deterrence.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the people of Al-Madinah when hypocritical whisperers spread division between Muhajirun and Ansar at the water well of Al-Muraysi'?
optionsEn: He sided with one clan over the other
He condemned tribal fanaticism saying: 'Leave it (tribalism), for it is foul and rotten!'
explanationEn: When Abdullah ibn Ubayy threatened that the 'honorable' would expel the 'meaner' upon returning to Madinah, Allah revealed Surah Al-Munafiqun (63:8), and Umar's restraint plus the Prophet's ﷺ wisdom prevented bloodshed—even Ibn Ubayy's own devout Muslim son defended the Prophet's ﷺ honor!

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when Abdullah ibn Ubayy's sincere Muslim son offered to execute his own father if ordered, after the hypocrite insulted the Muhajirun?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ strictly forbade it: 'Rather, we will treat him kindly and keep good company with him as long as he remains among us!'
explanationEn: By protecting family ties and showing magnanimity even to a known hypocrite, the Prophet ﷺ caused Abdullah ibn Ubayy's own tribe to rebuke him whenever he stirred trouble thereafter.

questionEn: What long march did the Prophet ﷺ lead immediately after Al-Muraysi' to keep companions focused and exhausted hypocrites' gossip during the Return?
optionsEn: He divided the army into ten camps
He halted at Quba for a month
He marched the army continuously through the afternoon, night, and next morning until everyone slept deeply at the halt
explanationEn: Wise leadership redirected restless energy away from rumor-mongering before returning safely to Madinah.

questionEn: Which devout Muhajir cousin of the Prophet ﷺ—husband of Zaynab bint Jahsh before her divorce—received the unique distinction of being the ONLY companion mentioned explicitly by name in the Qur'an?
optionsEn: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:37)
explanationEn: To compensate Zayd for losing the title 'son of Muhammad' when adoption-erasing lineage was abolished, Allah honored Zayd permanently by naming him in Surah Al-Ahzab 33:37.

questionEn: Which tribe of Yemen/Hijaz came to Khaybar alongside Ja'far (RA)—specifically Abu Musa al-Ash'ari's tribe—whom the Prophet ﷺ praised saying 'You have the softest hearts and most tender feelings'?
explanationEn: Looking toward Yemen, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The people of Yemen have come to you; they are the softest of hearts and gentlest of souls. Faith is Yemeni and wisdom is Yemeni!'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ notice about the Ash'ari companions' exemplary community spirit during travel and famine?
optionsEn: When provisions ran low, they pooled all remaining food onto a single cloth and divided it equally among everyone—so the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'They are from me and I am from them!'
They fasted for ten days straight
explanationEn: This selfless mutual aid in times of scarcity remains a timeless prophetic model for pilgrims and travelers.

questionEn: What important diplomatic envoy did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ send to Shurahbil ibn Amr al-Ghassani in Bosra/Mu'tah—whose murder sparked the Battle of Mu'tah?
explanationEn: Killing an ambassador was a severe violation of universal diplomatic immunity; al-Harith was the only envoy of the Prophet ﷺ ever murdered.

questionEn: Which companion of the Prophet ﷺ took his letter to the Persian Emperor Khosrow II—after first delivering it to the governor of Bahrain?
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Hudhafah fearlessly stood before the mighty Persian Emperor and delivered the call to Islam.

questionEn: When Prophet Muhammad ﷺ sent Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri (RA) to King Negus in Abyssinia around 6–7 AH, what request did his letter also include?
optionsEn: To formalize his marriage to Umm Habibah (RA) and help facilitate the return of the remaining emigrants to Madinah
explanationEn: Negus joyfully arranged the marriage ceremony, provided two ships for Ja'far and the emigrants to sail home, and sent gifts of honor.

questionEn: What happened when the Prophet ﷺ ordered the cutting down of some date palms belonging to Banu Nadir during their 4 AH siege—prompting Surah Al-Hashr (59:5)?
optionsEn: Allah confirmed that cutting or sparing those palms was done by Allah's leave to break the rebels' resistance
explanationEn: Because Banu Nadir boasted behind thick groves and fortresses, clearing a strategic portion pressured them into bloodless surrender within two weeks.

questionEn: Which two Jewish tribes/settlements in the north—Fadak and Wadi al-Qura—submitted peacefully to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ shortly after Khaybar's fall in 7 AH?
explanationEn: Fadak surrendered without combat (becoming prophetic Fay' supporting travelers and the needy), while Tayma agreed to pay Jizyah for full protection.

questionEn: What happened during the Battle of Khaybar when a poor Abyssinian shepherd tending the fort's sheep came to the Prophet ﷺ, asked about Islam, accepted it, and asked what to do with the sheep entrusted to him?
optionsEn: He set them loose in the desert

The Prophet ﷺ ordered him to return every sheep to the fort first—showing strict trustworthiness even in war—before the shepherd fought and attained martyrdom without ever having prayed a single Salah
The Prophet ﷺ kept the sheep
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ later smiled seeing his body, saying Allah honored this sincere man who 'did little work yet earned immense reward!'

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forbid mut'ah (temporary) marriage and instruct companions strictly on rules of purity, family, and spoils during 5–7 AH?
optionsEn: Because Madinah had too many weddings
To elevate marriage into a lasting sacred bond (mithaqan ghaliza) and safeguard justice and social integrity
explanationEn: Gradual Qur'anic and prophetic legislation shaped a disciplined, compassionate society grounded in responsibility.

questionEn: Which companion—famous for his poetic defense of the Prophet ﷺ—was told by the Prophet ﷺ: 'Attack Quraysh with your poetry, for Jibril is with you!'?
explanationEn: A special platform/pulpit was even placed in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi for Hassan ibn Thabit (RA) to defend the Prophet ﷺ and Islam eloquently against hostile poets.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to comfort a companion who arrived worried that Khaybar's booty had been split before his return, even though Allah rewarded those who attended Hudaybiyyah?
optionsEn: He reserved Khaybar exclusively for the 1,400 heroes of Hudaybiyyah, while warmly welcoming Ja'far's Abyssinian group into the shares by agreement of the companions
He sent them back to Abyssinia
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ balanced justice for the Hudaybiyyah veterans with generous inclusion of the newly arrived emigrants from Abyssinia and Banu Daws (like Abu Hurayrah).

questionEn: Which future prolific narrator of over 5,300 hadiths migrated from Yemen (Banu Daws) and met the Prophet ﷺ right at Khaybar in 7 AH?
explanationEn: Living among Ahl al-Suffah and remaining constantly at the Prophet's ﷺ side for the final four years, Abu Hurayrah (RA) preserved thousands of prophetic teachings after the Prophet ﷺ spread his cloak and prayed for his memory.

questionEn: What special kindness did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ show when Abu Hurayrah's (RA) mother initially resisted Islam and spoke harshly against him?
optionsEn: He sent Umar to warn her
He wrote her a stern letter
He told Abu Hurayrah never to visit her
The Prophet ﷺ immediately raised his hands and made du'a: 'O Allah, guide the mother of Abu Hurayrah!'—and by the time Abu Hurayrah walked home, she embraced Islam!
explanationEn: Abu Hurayrah hurried back weeping tears of joy to report Allah's immediate answer to the Prophet's ﷺ du'a.

questionEn: What treaty-building journey did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ send Shuja ibn Wahb (RA) on in 6–7 AH with a diplomatic letter?
optionsEn: To al-Harith ibn Abi Shamir al-Ghassani, governor of Damascus/Ghassan
explanationEn: Though al-Harith initially threatened war against Madinah, Caesar Heraclius restrained him while preparing for imperial campaigns.

questionEn: Why did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) later fast, give charity, free slaves, and pray abundantly out of remorse for how he questioned the Prophet ﷺ at Hudaybiyyah?
optionsEn: Because he broke his camel's leg
Because he had impatiently asked 'Are we not on the truth and our enemies on falsehood? Why then accept humiliation in our religion?'—not yet seeing Allah's grand plan
explanationEn: Umar (RA) gratefully acknowledged his error once Surah Al-Fath came down, saying afterward he continually did good deeds hoping to atone for his impatience that day.

questionEn: What question did Umar (RA) put to Abu Bakr (RA) at Hudaybiyyah—and how did Abu Bakr's reply mirror the Prophet's ﷺ own words?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr agreed to go back immediately
Abu Bakr replied word-for-word without having heard the Prophet ﷺ: 'He is indeed Allah's Messenger, he will never disobey his Lord, and Allah is his Helper—so hold fast to his stirrup!'
explanationEn: Abu Bakr's uncanny harmony of heart with the Prophet ﷺ at moments of crisis showcased his supreme spiritual insight (Siddiqiyyah).

questionEn: During the Battle of the Trench, which companion's tent inside the mosque did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ order set up to nurse the wounded Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA) so he could visit him closely?
optionsEn: The medical tent of Rufaydah al-Aslamiyyah (RA), Islam's pioneering female nurse/field medic
explanationEn: Rufaydah al-Aslamiyyah (RA) cared for wounded soldiers in a dedicated medical tent inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi—pioneering organized nursing in Islamic history.

questionEn: How did the Prophet's ﷺ aunt Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib (RA) protect the women and children inside Hassan ibn Thabit's fortress during the Battle of the Trench?
optionsEn: She rode out to fight Khalid
When an enemy scout climbed to spy on the undefended women's fort, Safiyyah bravely struck him down with a tent pole to stop him from alerting Banu Qurayzah
explanationEn: When Hassan hesitated, Safiyyah acted decisively with courage, ensuring Banu Qurayzah stayed deterred from attacking the families' stronghold.

questionEn: Which Qurayshi noble tried to bribe the Ghatafan tribe with half of Madinah's date harvest to withdraw from the Trench coalition—and why did the Prophet ﷺ cancel the draft treaty?
optionsEn: He consulted the Ansar chiefs Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Sa'd ibn Ubadah, who proudly declared: 'By Allah, we will give them nothing but the sword!'—delighting the Prophet ﷺ
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ tested the Ansar's morale out of mercy for their hardship; seeing their fierce faith, he tore up the unsealed draft immediately.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when Aishah (RA) wept in her parents' home during the Month of the Slander (Ifk) and finally heard the verses of her innocence?
optionsEn: Her mother told her to thank the Prophet ﷺ, and Aishah replied with profound Tawhid: 'By Allah, I will not thank anyone except Allah, Who revealed my innocence!'
She stayed silent for a year
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ smiled tenderly at her pure devotion to Allah alone, while punishing the slanderers who spread falsehood without four witnesses as decreed in Surah Al-Nur.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reply to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari's wife when Abu Ayyub asked her how she reacted to the false rumor during the Incident of Ifk?
optionsEn: She asked Abu Ayyub if he would ever do such a deed; when he said no, she answered: 'By Allah, Aishah is better than me, and Safwan is better than you!'
explanationEn: Allah praised that exact pure mindset in Surah Al-Nur (24:12): 'Why, when you heard it, did not the believing men and believing women think good of one another and say, This is an obvious falsehood?'

questionEn: Which commander led the 8 AH expedition to Dhat al-Salasil before Mu'tah and later requested backup force led by Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah (RA)?
explanationEn: Amr ibn al-As led the expedition to Dhat al-Salasil; when Abu Bakr and Umar arrived in Abu Ubaydah's backup force, Amr retained overall command and wisely led them using dry ablution (Tayammum) in extreme freezing cold—which the Prophet ﷺ smiled and approved!
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Taharah); Sahih al-Bukhari

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ smile approvingly when Amr ibn al-As (RA) explained he performed Tayammum instead of Ghusl on a freezing night during Dhat al-Salasil?
optionsEn: Because Amr cited Allah's verse 'Do not kill yourselves; indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you' (4:29), demonstrating sound Islamic jurisprudence prioritizing preserving life
explanationEn: The Prophet's ﷺ approving smile taught the Ummah that Islam is a faith of wisdom and ease, never harming oneself needlessly.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Taharah); Surah Al-Nisa 4:29

questionEn: What humorous yet profound lesson happened on the 'Expedition of the Sea Coast' (Sariyyat Sayf al-Bahr / Expedition of Khabat) led by Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah (RA)?
optionsEn: Starving on a single date a day, Allah cast up a giant whale ('Anbar) on shore that fed 300 companions for a month—and when they brought dried meat back, the Prophet ﷺ ate some too!
explanationEn: After checking whether eating sea creatures found washed ashore was lawful, the Prophet ﷺ confirmed: 'It is a provision Allah brought forth for you—have you any left to feed us?'

questionEn: Which verse was revealed during the period of Khaybar/Hudaybiyyah emphasizing how Muslims should speak about earlier prophets and people of the Book when exchanging knowledge?
optionsEn: 'Say: We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us...' and confirming Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the mercy-bringing witness confirming earlier truth
explanationEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught companions neither to blindly affirm nor reject unverified reports from previous scriptures, judging everything by the Qur'an's criterion.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ react when a companion returning from an expedition killed an enemy soldier who had uttered 'La ilaha illallah' out of fear of the sword?
optionsEn: He rebuked Usamah ibn Zayd repeatedly: 'Did you split open his heart to see whether he said it sincerely or out of fear?!'—until Usamah wished he had only embraced Islam that day!
explanationEn: This unforgettable prophetic reprimand established an ironclad Islamic rule: outward profession of the Shahadah renders a person's life sacred and inviolable.

questionEn: Which tribal chief of Najd—Thumamah ibn Uthal—was captured and tied to a pillar in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, only to embrace Islam immediately when released unconditionally?
optionsEn: Thumamah ibn Uthal (chief of Banu Hanifah)
explanationEn: Watching the companions' noble worship and character for three days inside the mosque melted Thumamah's heart; freed without ransom, he bathed, declared the Shahadah, and performed the very first public Muslim Umrah shouting the Talbiyah in Makkah!

questionEn: What did Thumamah ibn Uthal do upon reaching Makkah for Umrah right after embracing Islam in Madinah?
optionsEn: He cut off Yamamah's wheat shipments to hostile Quraysh until Quraysh begged the Prophet ﷺ to lift it—and the compassionate Prophet ﷺ wrote to Thumamah to resume Makkah's food supply!
explanationEn: Even against bitter enemies who had boycotted Muslims into starvation in Shi'b Abi Talib, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ refused to starve the civilians of Makkah.

questionEn: During the 7 AH Khaybar campaign, why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid eating domestic donkey meat right as pots were already boiling in the camp?
optionsEn: To teach instant, joyful obedience to Allah's prohibition—the companions overturned every boiling pot immediately without hesitation
explanationEn: Just as Muslims poured out jars of wine into Madinah's streets the instant alcohol was prohibited, the companions overturned boiling pots the moment the herald cried Allah's command.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell Abu Bakr and Umar (RA) when he saw the companions sleeping past Fajr once on the return journey from Khaybar—after Bilal fell asleep while keeping watch?
optionsEn: 'Allah took your souls when He willed and returned them when He willed'—then calmly moved from that valley, called Adhan, and led Fajr in congregation!
He ordered them to skip Fajr that day
explanationEn: His gentle, serene handling of an accidental oversleeping taught the permanent legal rule: whoever sleeps through or forgets a prayer prays it as soon as they wake or remember, without guilt.

questionEn: What unique honor did the Prophet ﷺ grant Uthman ibn Talhah (RA) when he returned to Madinah to accept Islam in early 8 AH?
optionsEn: He made him commander of Khaybar
He reassured him gently, laying the groundwork to permanently entrust the Key of the Kaaba to his family (Banu Shaybah) after the Conquest of Makkah
explanationEn: Uthman ibn Talhah had once barred the Prophet ﷺ from entering the Kaaba in Makkah; the Prophet ﷺ calmly foretold a day when that very key would be in his hand—which he fulfilled nobly at the Conquest!

questionEn: Which three commanders did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ sequentially appoint before the Battle of Mu'tah (8 AH) against a massive Byzantine-Ghassanid army?
optionsEn: Zayd ibn Harithah, then Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, then Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA)
Abu Bakr, then Umar, then Uthman
explanationEn: All three beloved commanders attained martyrdom sequentially at Mu'tah while holding the banner—and the Prophet ﷺ announced their martyrdom live from Madinah's pulpit with tears streaming down his face.

questionEn: What immortal title did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ confer upon Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA) after Khalid skillfully rallied the outnumbered 3,000 Muslims at Mu'tah and brought them safely back to Madinah?
explanationEn: Nine swords shattered in Khalid's hand as he rotated regiments to deceive the huge Roman force and execute a brilliant tactical withdrawal; the Prophet ﷺ announced: 'Then a Sword from the Swords of Allah took the banner until Allah granted them victory!'

questionEn: Which hero of Mu'tah fought onward after losing both arms gripping the banner to his chest, earning the honor 'Dhul-Janahayn' (He of Two Wings in Paradise)?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ told his weeping family that Allah replaced Ja'far's two lost hands with two radiant wings with which he flies wherever he wishes in Paradise.

questionEn: What treacherous breach by Quraysh shattered the 10-year Treaty of Hudaybiyyah in 8 AH, leading directly to the Conquest of Makkah?
optionsEn: Quraysh secretly armed Banu Bakr to massacre Banu Khuza'ah—who were under the Prophet's ﷺ treaty protection—even inside the Sacred Sanctuary of Makkah
explanationEn: Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i rode swiftly to Madinah reciting poignant verses begging the Prophet's ﷺ help; the Prophet ﷺ vowed: 'You shall be aided, O Amr ibn Salim!'

questionEn: When Abu Sufyan hurried to Madinah in panic trying to renew the broken Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, whose daughter refused to let him even sit on the Prophet's ﷺ bedding?
optionsEn: His own daughter, Umm Habibah (RA), saying 'It is the bedding of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and you are an impure polytheist!'
explanationEn: Every senior companion declined to intercede for Abu Sufyan after Quraysh's blood-stained betrayal, so he returned empty-handed to Makkah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pray before marching secretly toward Makkah in Ramadan 8 AH so Quraysh would be caught completely off guard without bloodshed?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, take away the spies and scouts from Quraysh until we come upon them suddenly in their own land!'
explanationEn: Total secrecy prevented Quraysh from mobilizing resistance, turning the Conquest of Makkah into a virtually bloodless liberation.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forgive Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah (RA) after intercepting a secret letter Hatib sent warning Quraysh of the impending march?
optionsEn: It was a code in Persian
Hatib explained he acted solely to protect his unprotected family in Makkah without doubting Islam—and the Prophet ﷺ reminded Umar (RA) that Hatib had fought at Badr!
explanationEn: Revealing Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:1), Allah cautioned believers against taking allies out of misplaced sentiment while the Prophet ﷺ honored Hatib's Badr sincerity.

questionEn: How large was the Muslim army that marched with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ into Makkah in Ramadan 8 AH—after lighting ten thousand campfires on Marr al-Zahran?
explanationEn: Ten thousand campfires lit up the night horizon overlooking Makkah, demonstrating overwhelming peaceful strength that convinced Quraysh surrender was futile.

questionEn: What compassionate warning did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ issue to a companion's puppy-nursing dog discovered right along the marching route to Makkah?
optionsEn: He halted the march for a week
He ordered the dogs chased away
He stationed a guard named Ju'ayl ibn Suraqah beside the mother dog and her puppies so the entire 10,000-man army would march around without disturbing them
explanationEn: Even while leading 10,000 warriors toward the decisive conquest of Makkah, the Mercy to the Worlds paused to protect a nursing dog and her newborn pups!

questionEn: When Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA) exclaimed 'Today is the day of fierce battle (Yawm al-Malhamah)!' upon entering Makkah, how did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ immediately correct him?
optionsEn: 'Rather, today is the day of mercy (Yawm al-Marhamah)—today Allah will honor the Kaaba!'—and transferred the banner to Sa'd's son Qays
explanationEn: Refusing vengeance, the Prophet ﷺ declared general safety inside the Haram, inside Abu Sufyan's house, and inside every person's closed home.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Maghazi); Seerah Ibn Hisham

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ carry himself physically upon riding Al-Qaswa into liberated Makkah on 20 Ramadan 8 AH?
optionsEn: Bowing his head so low in humility and gratitude to Allah that his beard nearly touched the saddle of his camel, reciting Surah Al-Fath
explanationEn: Far from earthly conquerors' arrogance, he entered Makkah trembling with humility, recognizing victory belonged solely to Allah.

questionEn: What verse did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ recite as he pointed with his staff at the 360 idols arrayed around the Kaaba, causing them to topple one by one?
optionsEn: 'The truth has come, and falsehood has perished; indeed falsehood is ever bound to vanish' (Surah Al-Isra 17:81)
'Read in the name of your Lord' (96:1)
'In the Name of Allah, Most Merciful' (1:1)
explanationEn: He purified Allah's Sacred House from every idol and pagan painting inside—returning the Kaaba to the pure Abrahamic monotheism for which it was built.

questionEn: What historic judgment did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ deliver to the trembling people of Makkah gathered around the Kaaba after the Conquest?
optionsEn: 'Go, for you are the free ones (al-Tulaqa')—no blame upon you this day; may Allah forgive you!' (echoing Prophet Yusuf's words)
explanationEn: Quoting Prophet Yusuf's (AS) words to his brothers (Surah 12:92), he granted sweeping amnesty to those who had boycotted, tortured, and waged wars against him for twenty years!

questionEn: Whom did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ command to climb onto the very roof of the Sacred Kaaba to call the Adhan on the Day of Conquest?
explanationEn: In the heart of Makkah where he had once been dragged over burning gravel, Bilal (RA) stood atop the Kaaba proclaiming the greatness of Allah.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ honor the Qur'anic verse 'Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due' (4:58) inside the Kaaba on Conquest Day?
optionsEn: Even though Ali (RA) asked for the Kaaba's key, the Prophet ﷺ returned the key permanently to Uthman ibn Talhah and his family Banu Shaybah
He kept the key in Madinah
He gave the key to Abu Bakr
explanationEn: Banu Shaybah remain the hereditary custodians of the Kaaba's key to this very day—a living, unbroken 1,400-year fulfillment of prophetic trustworthiness!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pray inside the Kaaba on the Day of Conquest, as narrated by Bilal (RA) who entered with him and Usamah ibn Zayd?
optionsEn: He stood facing the far wall between two pillars, made Takbir in the corners, and prayed two rak'ahs inside the Sacred House
He locked the door for a year
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) eagerly asked Bilal which spot inside the Kaaba the Prophet ﷺ prayed in so he could follow his exact footsteps.

questionEn: On which hill in Makkah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ sit after the Conquest to accept the pledge of allegiance (Bay'ah) from the newly Muslim men and women of Makkah?
explanationEn: On the very same Mount Safa where Abu Lahab had mocked him 17 years earlier, thousands of Makkans climbed up to pledge allegiance to Allah and His Messenger.

questionEn: Why did the Ansar momentarily worry after the Conquest of Makkah when they saw the Prophet ﷺ raising his hands in long du'a on Mount Safa?
optionsEn: They feared he might choose to remain in his beloved birthplace Makkah—until he firmly reassured them: 'I am Allah's servant and Messenger; my life is with you and my death is with you!'
explanationEn: Hearing his unshakeable promise to return home with them to Madinah moved the Ansar deeply to tears.

questionEn: Which fierce Makkan opponent—son of Abu Jahl—fled to Yemen by sea after the Conquest, only to return and embrace Islam when his wife Umm Hakim secured the Prophet's ﷺ pardon for him?
explanationEn: Before Ikrimah arrived, the Prophet ﷺ forbade companions from insulting his father Abu Jahl in his presence ('Harming the dead hurts the living without reaching the dead'), and Ikrimah became a devoted martyr at Yarmouk!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ do when Fudalah ibn Umayr approached him during Tawaf right after the Conquest intending to assassinate him?
optionsEn: He called Fudalah by name, asked 'What were you whispering to yourself?' and gently placed his blessed hand on Fudalah's chest—transforming Fudalah's hatred into instant love and faith!
explanationEn: Fudalah testified: 'Before he lifted his hand off my chest, no creature on earth was dearer to me than him!'

questionEn: Which two major pagan tribes of Ta'if and the surrounding hills marched 20,000 warriors against the Muslims in Shawwal 8 AH—leading to the Battle of Hunayn?
explanationEn: Alarmed by Islam's triumph in Makkah, Malik ibn Awf rallied Hawazin and Thaqif with their families and herds behind them in the narrow valley of Hunayn.

questionEn: What spiritual lesson does Surah Al-Tawbah (9:25) teach from the opening ambush at the Battle of Hunayn when the 12,000-strong Muslim force initially scattered?
optionsEn: Pride in large numbers ('We will not be defeated today due to few numbers') availed them nothing until they turned in reliance to Allah
explanationEn: Ten thousand Madinah veterans plus 2,000 newly Muslim Makkans marveled at their own numbers—until Hawazin archers ambushed them in the dawn gorge, proving victory comes solely from Allah.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ turn panic into resounding triumph at Hunayn while nearly everyone else fled?
optionsEn: Riding forward alone on his white mule Duldul calling 'I am the Prophet, no lie! I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib!', he had al-Abbas's booming voice rally the Muhajirun and Ansar back around him
He sent a letter to Ta'if
explanationEn: Surrounded only by a handful like Abbas, Ali, and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, the Prophet's ﷺ unmatched courage rallied the believers and Allah sent down tranquility (Sakinah) and unseen angels.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ grant huge gifts of 100 camels to newly converted Makkan chiefs (Al-Mu'allafatu Qulubuhum) after Hunayn while giving the Ansar none of the spoils—and how did he console the Ansar?
optionsEn: He planned to stay in Ta'if

He explained he gave fleeting worldly camels to win new hearts, then asked the Ansar: 'Are you not pleased that other people take sheep and camels back while you take the Messenger of Allah ﷺ home with you?'
explanationEn: Hearing his tender words, the Ansar wept until their beards were soaked, crying: 'We are pleased with the Messenger of Allah as our share and portion!'

questionEn: Which Umrah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ enter Ihram for from Ji'ranah right after distributing the Hunayn spoils in Dhul-Qa'dah 8 AH?
explanationEn: Entering Ihram from Ji'ranah at night, he quietly performed Umrah in Makkah before returning swiftly to Madinah—leaving Ji'ranah as a historic site associated with his Prophetic Umrah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ do when a delegation from defeated Hawazin came to Ji'ranah after accepting Islam and begged for the return of their 6,000 captured wives and children?
optionsEn: He gave up his own and Banu Abd al-Muttalib's share immediately, inspiring the Muhajirun and Ansar to freely release all 6,000 captives too!
explanationEn: Even those like Uyaynah ibn Hisn who initially hesitated were compensated with six camels per captive later—resulting in unprecedented mass reconciliation.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond during the Siege of Ta'if (8 AH) when companions asked him to curse Thaqif so their fortress would fall?
optionsEn: Instead of cursing, he raised his hands and prayed: 'O Allah, guide Thaqif and bring them to us!'—and within a year Thaqif came voluntarily to Madinah to accept Islam!
explanationEn: Matching his refusal to crush Ta'if ten years earlier, his persistent du'a brought the entire city peacefully into Islam.

questionEn: Which poet—who had mocked the Prophet ﷺ in verse for years—walked boldly into Masjid an-Nabawi in 9 AH, recited the famous 'Banat Su'ad' ode praising the Prophet ﷺ, and received the Prophet's ﷺ own striped cloak (Burdah)?
explanationEn: Known forever as 'Qasidat al-Burdah,' Ka'b's poem praised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as 'a drawn sword from Allah's swords of light,' moving the Prophet ﷺ to drape his own mantle over Ka'b's shoulders.

questionEn: Which baby boy was born to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah (RA) in 8 AH, bringing great joy before passing away in infancy at ~16–18 months?
explanationEn: Holding his dying toddler Ibrahim gently in tears, the Prophet ﷺ taught believers balanced grief: 'The eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, yet we say only what pleases our Lord—truly, O Ibrahim, we are deeply saddened by your departure.'

questionEn: When a solar eclipse coincided with the death of the Prophet's ﷺ infant son Ibrahim and people whispered the sun eclipsed out of grief for Ibrahim, how did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ immediately correct that superstition?
optionsEn: 'The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of Allah; they do not eclipse for anyone's death or life—so when you see them, hasten to prayer!'
explanationEn: At the very peak of personal bereavement, the Prophet ﷺ refused to exploit coincidence for personal glory, anchoring believers in pure rational monotheism.

questionEn: Why was the Expedition of Tabuk in Rajab 9 AH called 'Jaysh al-Usrah' (The Army of Hardship)?
optionsEn: Because they lost their camels at Quba
Because of scorching summer heat, ripe date-harvest temptation, extreme drought, and an exhausting 700-km march north toward the Byzantine frontier
explanationEn: Unlike other campaigns kept secret, the Prophet ﷺ announced the distant destination openly so the 30,000-strong army could prepare thoroughly.

questionEn: How did Uthman ibn Affan (RA), Abu Bakr (RA), and Umar (RA) famously compete in charitable giving to outfit the needy Army of Hardship for Tabuk?
optionsEn: Uthman equipped a third of the army with ~300–900 camels and 1,000 gold dinars; Umar brought half his wealth; Abu Bakr brought ALL his wealth leaving only Allah and His Messenger for his family!
explanationEn: Pouring 1,000 gold dinars into the Prophet's ﷺ lap, Uthman moved the Prophet ﷺ to exclaim: 'Nothing Uthman does after today can ever harm him!'

questionEn: What did Allah reveal in Surah Al-Tawbah (9:92) about the seven poor companions ('Al-Bakka'un' — The Weepers) who begged for mounts to join Tabuk and wept when none remained?
optionsEn: They returned with eyes overflowing with tears of sorrow that they had nothing to spend—and Allah freed them from all blame!
explanationEn: Their sincere tears proved that true devotion is measured by the heart's longing, earning them the full reward of those who marched.

questionEn: What profound answer did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) when Ali felt sad being left behind to look after Madinah and the Prophet's ﷺ family during Tabuk?
optionsEn: 'Are you not pleased to be to me as Harun (Aaron) was to Musa (Moses), except that there is no prophet after me?'
explanationEn: This elevated comparison honored Ali's trustworthiness while unambiguously affirming Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as the Final Prophet.

questionEn: Which devout companion deliberately stayed behind from Tabuk out of mere procrastination—and then told the total truth instead of lying excuses—enduring a 50-day social boycott until Allah revealed his forgiveness in Surah Al-Tawbah?
optionsEn: Ka'b ibn Malik (RA), alongside Murarah ibn al-Rabi' and Hilal ibn Umayyah (RA)
explanationEn: Though the king of Ghassan wrote inviting lonely Ka'b to defect, Ka'b burned the letter; after 50 agonizing days of complete isolation, Allah revealed Surah Al-Tawbah (9:118) accepting their repentance and praising truthfulness.

questionEn: What hypocritical rival mosque built near Quba by Abu Amir al-Rahib's faction to divide believers did Allah order the Prophet ﷺ never to stand in and to demolish upon returning from Tabuk?
optionsEn: Masjid al-Dirar (The Mosque of Harm and Division)
explanationEn: Masjid al-Dirar was disguised as a place of worship while serving as a secret espionage outpost; Allah exposed it in Surah Al-Tawbah (9:107-108) while praising nearby Masjid Quba.

questionEn: Why is the 9th year after Hijrah famously known in Islamic history as 'Am al-Wufud' (The Year of Delegations)?
optionsEn: Because over 70 tribal delegations from every corner of the Arabian Peninsula streamed into Madinah voluntarily to declare Islam and learn its teachings
explanationEn: Following the Conquest of Makkah and Tabuk, tribes across Yemen, Najd, Bahrain, Oman, and northern Arabia entered Allah's religion in multitudes—fulfilling Surah Al-Nasr (110).

questionEn: Which senior companion did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ appoint as Amir al-Hajj to lead the Muslim Hajj in Dhul-Hijjah 9 AH, accompanied by Ali (RA) announcing Surah Al-Tawbah's decrees?
explanationEn: Under Abu Bakr's leadership, Ali (RA) proclaimed at Mina that after this final transitional year, no polytheist would perform Hajj and no one would make Tawaf naked—restoring the Sacred House's dignity permanently.

questionEn: Which two wise, gentle companions did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ send as governors and judges to Yemen around 9–10 AH with the advice: 'Make things easy, do not make them difficult; give glad tidings, do not repel people'?
optionsEn: Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ also famously interviewed Mu'adh (RA) on how he would judge cases (Qur'an, then Sunnah, then careful scholarly reasoning/ijtihad) and praised his clarity.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Maghazi); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: When Banu Abd al-Qays delegation arrived from eastern Arabia and rushed off their camels to kiss the Prophet's ﷺ hands and feet, which quiet chief stayed back to wash, dress cleanly, and greet him calmly?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ praised al-Ashajj with timeless words: 'Indeed you possess two qualities that Allah loves: forbearance (hilm) and deliberateness/gentleness (anah)!'

questionEn: Which rough-spoken Bedouin from Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr marched into Al-Masjid an-Nabawi demanding straight answers from the Prophet ﷺ—'By Allah, I will ask you harshly!'—and left embracing Islam?
explanationEn: After grilling the Prophet ﷺ directly on whether Allah truly commanded the five prayers, Zakat, Ramadan, and Hajj, Dimam swore 'I will neither add to them nor subtract from them!'—and the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'He will enter Paradise if he keeps his word!'

questionEn: Which Christian delegation from southern Arabia visited Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in 9–10 AH, was graciously permitted by the Prophet ﷺ to pray inside his mosque facing east, and concluded a peaceful protective covenant?
explanationEn: Showing extraordinary hospitality and civic tolerance, the Prophet ﷺ lodged the Najran delegation honorably and guaranteed their churches and religious freedom under covenant.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to Adi ibn Hatim (son of the famed generous Hatim al-Ta'i) that melted Adi's doubts about Islam?
optionsEn: He argued with him all week
He spread his own leather cushion for Adi to sit while sitting on the bare floor himself, and foretold a time when a lone woman would travel safely from Hirah to Makkah fearing none but Allah
He ordered him to move to Yemen
explanationEn: Witnessing both the Prophet's ﷺ unmatched humility and later watching two of his three prophecies come true in his own lifetime, Adi became a steadfast Muslim.

questionEn: Roughly how many pilgrims accompanied Prophet Muhammad ﷺ when he departed Madinah in Dhul-Qa'dah 10 AH for his first and only Hajj—the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat al-Wada)?
explanationEn: From Madinah and across Arabia, over 100,000 believers converged around the Prophet ﷺ to learn every step of Hajj directly from him.

questionEn: From which Miqat near Madinah did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ enter Ihram for the Farewell Pilgrimage after anointing himself with perfume and praying?
explanationEn: At Dhul-Hulayfah (modern Abyar Ali), just outside Madinah, he entered Ihram (combining Hajj and Umrah as Qiran, while instructing companions without sacrificial animals to perform Tamattu').

questionEn: What timeless command did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ repeat throughout the Farewell Pilgrimage so pilgrims across all generations would follow his exact rites?
optionsEn: 'Take your pilgrimage rituals from me (Khudhu 'anni manasikakum), for perhaps I may not perform Hajj again after this year!'
explanationEn: Every detail Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) recorded in Sahih Muslim—from Talbiyah to Arafah to Mina—forms the blueprint of Umrah and Hajj today.

questionEn: In his monumental Farewell Sermon (Khutbat al-Wada) on 9 Dhul-Hijjah 10 AH at Arafah, what fundamental declaration did the Prophet ﷺ proclaim regarding human equality?
optionsEn: 'An Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor a white person over a black person, except by piety (Taqwa) and righteous deeds!'
explanationEn: Shattering racial, tribal, and class arrogance before over 100,000 people, he reminded humanity that all descend from Adam, and Adam was created from dust.

questionEn: What strict moral and social principles did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ emphasize during his Farewell Sermon at Arafah and Mina?
optionsEn: The absolute sanctity of human life, property, and honor; abolishing pre-Islamic usury (riba) and blood feuds; and treating women with kindness and fulfilled rights
explanationEn: He famously began abolishing usury with his own uncle Abbas's claims and abolished pre-Islamic blood vengeance with his own kinsman's claim—modeling leadership by personal example.

questionEn: Which two monumental anchors did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warn the Ummah to hold fast to during the Farewell Pilgrimage (and at Ghadir Khumm) so they would never go astray?
optionsEn: The Book of Allah (the Qur'an) and his Sunnah (and in Sahih Muslim at Ghadir Khumm, Allah's Book and mindfulness of Ahl al-Bayt)
explanationEn: In his Farewell Sermon he anchored the Ummah permanently in the Qur'an and Prophetic Sunnah, while later at Ghadir Khumm he also reminded believers of the Book of Allah and kind care for his family (Ahl al-Bayt).
reference: Sahih Muslim (Kitab al-Hajj & Kitab Fada'il al-Sahabah); Muwatta Malik

questionEn: Which verse was revealed at Arafah on the Friday evening of the Farewell Pilgrimage, causing Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) to weep realizing the Prophet's ﷺ earthly mission was nearly complete?
optionsEn: 'This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion' (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:3)
'Read in the name of your Lord' (96:1)
'Indeed We have given you a clear victory' (48:1)
explanationEn: When a Jewish scholar told Umar (RA) they would have made that day an Eid, Umar affirmed it came down on two Eids together: Friday and the Day of Arafah—while silently sensing that perfection precedes departure.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ conclude his Farewell Sermon at Arafah, calling upon heaven and earth to bear witness?
optionsEn: Asking 'Have I conveyed the message?'—and when 100,000+ roared 'Yes!', he pointed his index finger toward the sky and back to the people saying three times: 'O Allah, bear witness!'
explanationEn: He also charged every listener: 'Let those present convey this to those who are absent—for perhaps one to whom it is conveyed will understand it even better than one who heard it directly.'

questionEn: Which companion helped shave Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ blessed head at Mina on 10 Dhul-Hijjah during the Farewell Pilgrimage, after the Prophet ﷺ sacrificed 63 camels with his own hand (one for each year of his life)?
optionsEn: Ma'mar ibn Abdullah (RA)—while Khalid ibn al-Walid eagerly asked for a lock of hair from his forelock for blessing
explanationEn: Sacrificing 63 camels himself and letting Ali (RA) sacrifice the remaining 37 (to reach 100) silently mirrored his 63 years of blessed life; Abu Talhah (RA) then distributed locks of his hair among the companions.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say during the Farewell Pilgrimage at the Stoning of the Jamarat when a man asked in panic because he had shaved before sacrificing or sacrificed before stoning?
optionsEn: 'Do it (now), there is no blame!'—repeating 'La haraj' (no hardship) to every pilgrim who altered the sequence unknowingly
explanationEn: Exemplifying prophetic gentleness and ease in pilgrimage rituals, he never turned away a sincere pilgrim on account of sequence confusion during the crowds of Eid.

questionEn: Which Surah revealed toward the end of the Prophet's ﷺ life—praising Allah when people entered Islam in crowds—was understood by Ibn Abbas (RA) and Umar (RA) as a subtle announcement of the Prophet's ﷺ approaching departure?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Nasr (110:1-3): 'When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest...'
explanationEn: Commanding him to glorify Allah and seek forgiveness once the mission's victory arrived signaled that his earthly work was crowned and his meeting with his Lord was near.

questionEn: What unusual nightly actions did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ perform right before his final illness in Safar/Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH?
optionsEn: He visited the martyrs of Uhud to pray for them as if bidding farewell to the living and the dead, and went to Jannat al-Baqi at night asking Allah's forgiveness for its residents
explanationEn: Before returning from his last journey, he also completed a 20-day Ramadan I'tikaf (instead of his usual 10) and reviewed the entire Qur'an twice with Jibril (AS) that final Ramadan!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Maghazi & Kitab Fada'il al-Qur'an)

questionEn: Who was the 18-year-old son of Zayd ibn Harithah whom the Prophet ﷺ appointed commander of his very last military expedition to northern Syria in 11 AH—honoring Zayd's martyrdom at Mu'tah?
explanationEn: When some grumbled that young Usamah was placed over senior Muhajirun, the Prophet ﷺ rebuked them from the pulpit: 'He is worthy of command just as his father Zayd was worthy, and he is among the dearest of people to me!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ cryptically hint at his imminent passing during one of his last public sermons in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi—making Abu Bakr (RA) burst into tears immediately?
optionsEn: 'Allah offered a servant the choice between the splendor of this world and what is with Allah—and that servant chose what is with Allah!'
explanationEn: While others wondered which servant he meant, Abu Bakr (RA) understood instantly that the servant was the Prophet ﷺ himself, weeping: 'May our fathers and mothers be ransomed for you!'

questionEn: Which wife's apartment beside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ask his other wives' gracious permission to stay in during his final illness?
explanationEn: Supported by Ali and al-Abbas (RA) with his feet tracing the ground, he entered Aishah's room where Allah united his final days and his burial spot.

questionEn: Whom did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ firmly appoint to lead the Muslims in congregational Salah during the final days when fever prevented him from standing?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA)—insisting 'Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer!' even when Aishah noted Abu Bakr weeps easily
explanationEn: Abu Bakr (RA) led 17 consecutive prayers while the Prophet ﷺ lived; once when Umar briefly stepped in due to Abu Bakr's temporary absence, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah and the believers refuse anyone except Abu Bakr!'

questionEn: What touching scene unfolded at Fajr on the very last Monday morning of the Prophet's ﷺ life when he lifted the curtain of Aishah's room?
optionsEn: Seeing the believers aligned neatly in prayer behind Abu Bakr (RA), his face beamed with a radiant smile of joy—nearly making companions break prayer from sheer delight!
explanationEn: He gestured for them to complete their prayer and lowered the curtain—the last time most companions ever beheld his blessed face alive.

questionEn: What urgent final warning did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ repeat during his final illness regarding the graves of prophets and righteous people?
optionsEn: 'Build tall marble towers over my grave'
'May Allah curse (or condemn) those who take the graves of their prophets as places of worship (masajid)'—warning against turning his own grave into an idolized shrine
explanationEn: Even on his deathbed, he fiercely guarded pure Tawhid so Muslims would always worship Allah alone while loving and sending Salawat upon him.

questionEn: What were among the very last repeated counsels Prophet Muhammad ﷺ breathed to his Ummah as his soul prepared to depart?
optionsEn: 'The Prayer, the Prayer (Al-Salah, Al-Salah), and fear Allah regarding those under your care/authority!'
explanationEn: His parting words summed up the two pillars of human life: our vertical connection with Allah (Salah) and our horizontal mercy toward the vulnerable.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Adab); Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ demonstrate utter detachment from worldly wealth even in his final hours of illness?
optionsEn: He wrote a will dividing gold palaces
He stored coins beneath his bed
Remembering 6 or 7 gold dinars left in Aishah's keeping, he insisted they be distributed immediately in charity so he would not meet Allah with them unspent
explanationEn: At his passing, his iron armor was actually pawned to a neighbor for thirty sa's of barley to feed his household—having given away everything else for Allah's sake!

questionEn: What final tender act did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ perform moments before passing away while resting in Aishah's (RA) lap?
optionsEn: Seeing Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr holding a fresh siwak (tooth-stick), Aishah softened it by chewing it for him, and the Prophet ﷺ brushed his teeth thoroughly before raising his hand and whispering: 'In the Highest Company (Fil-Rafiq al-A'la)'
He wrote a letter to Rome
He rode Al-Qaswa one last time
explanationEn: With his head resting between Aishah's chest and chin, he chose the Highest Companion—passing away on Monday, 12 Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH at age 63.

questionEn: What immortal declaration did Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) deliver inside Masjid an-Nabawi to calm the stunned companions (including Umar RA) upon the Prophet's ﷺ passing?
optionsEn: 'Whoever worshiped Muhammad—Muhammad has died; and whoever worships Allah—indeed Allah is Ever-Living and never dies!' followed by Surah Aal Imran 3:144
explanationEn: Hearing Surah Aal Imran 3:144 from Abu Bakr's lips, Umar's knees gave way as he realized the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had truly passed on.

questionEn: How did the companions resolve where to bury Prophet Muhammad ﷺ after his passing?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr (RA) recalled hearing the Prophet ﷺ say: 'Every prophet is buried right where he passes away'—so Abu Talhah dug his grave beneath the very spot of his bed in Aishah's room
explanationEn: Because Aishah's room bordered Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, his Sacred Chamber (al-Hujrah al-Nabawiyyah) stands beside al-Rawdah al-Sharifah today, visited with peace and Salawat by millions of pilgrims.

questionEn: How was the funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah) performed for Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Without a single Imam leading—groups of men, then women, then children entered Aishah's room sequentially and prayed individually over his blessed body
explanationEn: Because no human could stand as an Imam over the Prophet ﷺ, the entire community entered in small waves across Tuesday to offer prayers of love and peace.

questionEn: Which two senior companions were later buried beside Prophet Muhammad ﷺ inside Aishah's chamber?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) and Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)
explanationEn: United in life and mission, his two closest ministers lie beside him in death—and pilgrims greet the Prophet ﷺ, then Abu Bakr, then Umar with Salam when visiting Al-Masjid an-Nabawi.

questionEn: What did the Prophet's ﷺ beloved daughter Fatimah (RA) weepingly say to Anas (RA) right after her father's burial?
optionsEn: 'O Anas, how could your souls bear to throw earth over the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?!'
explanationEn: Anas (RA) himself noted that the day the Prophet ﷺ entered Madinah everything shone with light, and the day he passed away everything felt dark—and Fatimah (RA) rejoined her beloved father just six months later, just as he had gently whispered to her during his illness!

questionEn: Why did Fatimah (RA) first weep and then laugh when Prophet Muhammad ﷺ whispered two secrets into her ear during his final illness?
optionsEn: First he whispered he would pass away from this illness so she wept; then he whispered she would be the very first of his family to join him (and chief of the women of Paradise), so she smiled!
explanationEn: Fatimah (RA) faithfully kept that secret until after the Prophet's ﷺ passing, passing away six months later in Ramadan 11 AH.

questionEn: Which famous non-Muslim general of Makkah—father-in-law of the Prophet ﷺ through Umm Habibah—finally accepted Islam on the eve of the Conquest of Makkah after speaking with al-Abbas?
explanationEn: Viewing the 10,000-man Muslim camp alongside Abbas and seeing the Prophet's ﷺ mercy, Abu Sufyan accepted Islam and the Prophet ﷺ honored him by making his home a place of safety on Conquest Day.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ do when Abu Sufyan's cousin—Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, who had bitterly satirized him in poetry for years—came seeking forgiveness outside Makkah?
optionsEn: Inspired by Ali's advice to quote Yusuf's brothers ('We certainly prefer you, and indeed we have been sinners'), the Prophet ﷺ forgave him instantly with Surah Yusuf 12:92!
explanationEn: Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith became so devoted afterward that he stood gripping the Prophet's ﷺ stirrup fearlessly at Hunayn.

questionEn: What happened at the Battle of Hunayn when a Hawazin sniper named Shaybah ibn Uthman crept behind the Prophet ﷺ intending to avenge his father killed at Uhud?
optionsEn: As Shaybah drew near, a blazing flame of awe filled his vision, the Prophet ﷺ turned gently and placed his hand on Shaybah's chest praying 'O Allah, guide Shaybah!'—and Shaybah instantly embraced Islam!
explanationEn: Minutes later, Shaybah fought heroically beside the Prophet ﷺ against Hawazin—and later served faithfully as custodian of the Kaaba.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ demonstrate supreme honesty during the Siege of Ta'if when enslaved servants escaped from Ta'if's fort to join the Muslim camp?
optionsEn: He declared them 'Freedmen of Allah' (Utaqa' Allah) and refused to return them even when Thaqif later surrendered and asked for them back!
explanationEn: One of those freedmen, Abu Bakrah (Nufay'), climbed down on a pulley (bakrah) from Ta'if's wall and became a respected scholar-companion.

questionEn: When Thaqif's delegation finally visited Madinah in 9 AH to embrace Islam, what two absurd requests did they make—one of which the Prophet ﷺ accepted temporarily and one of which he firmly refused?
optionsEn: He agreed to leave al-Lat standing

He firmly refused leaving their idol al-Lat standing for three years (sending al-Mughirah and Abu Sufyan to smash it immediately), and refused exempting them from Salah—for 'there is no good in a religion without prayer!'
explanationEn: He gently deferred charity/military duties momentarily until faith took root, yet never compromised pure monotheism (shirk) or the daily Salah!
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Imarah); Seerah Ibn Hisham

questionEn: What miraculous supply of water occurred during the arduous Tabuk march when the 30,000-man army nearly perished of thirst in Wadi al-Hijr?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for rain (Istisqa), and immediately a lone cloud gathered above the camp and poured rain until every water skin was full while the desert around stayed dry!
explanationEn: Even a hypocrite who mocked 'How can a cloud come in this scorching sky?' trembled in awe when it stopped directly above them—until the rain passed and he reverted to skepticism!
