questionEn: While passing through Al-Hijr (Mada'in Salih, ancient land of Thamud) en route to Tabuk, what spiritual instruction did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give his companions?
optionsEn: 'Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves unless weeping, lest what befell them befall you!'—and he hastened past with his cloak covering his face
Stop and build a market there
explanationEn: He taught pilgrims and travelers to treat historic sites of divine punishment with sober reflection and humility, never as casual tourist spectacles.

questionEn: What diplomatic success did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ achieve during the 20-day stay at Tabuk even though the Byzantine army retreated without fighting?
optionsEn: Christian and local rulers of Aylah (Yuhannah ibn Ru'bah), Jarba, Adhruh, and Dumat al-Jandal (Ukaydir) signed peace and protection treaties with Madinah
explanationEn: Establishing peaceful borders across northern Arabia transformed Islam into the undisputed, respected power of the Peninsula.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ do when his beloved daughter Zaynab's husband—or when his camel al-Qaswa went missing during Tabuk and a hypocrite mocked 'Muhammad claims revelation yet doesn't know where his camel is!'?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ replied humbly: 'By Allah, I know only what Allah teaches me—and Allah has just informed me she is in this valley, her halter caught on a tree!'—where they found her immediately!
explanationEn: He clearly distinguished prophetic revelation (knowledge granted by Allah) from personal omniscience, shaming the scoffer with instant proof.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ do at the funeral of Abdullah ibn Ubayy (the head of Madinah's hypocrites) out of kindness to his devout Muslim son—before Allah revealed Surah Al-Tawbah (9:84)?
optionsEn: He gave his own shirt for Ibn Ubayy's shroud and prayed his Janazah out of compassion for his believing son—until Allah revealed 9:84 forbidding praying over confirmed hypocrites
explanationEn: Even for his lifelong political saboteur, the Prophet's ﷺ unmatched personal mercy sought hope until Allah Himself set the final boundary.

questionEn: What was the Prophet's ﷺ reaction when false prophet Musaylimah 'the Liar' of Yamamah wrote an arrogant letter demanding 'Half the earth is for us and half for Quraysh'?
optionsEn: He wrote back calmly: 'In the Name of Allah: From Muhammad, Messenger of Allah, to Musaylimah the Liar—indeed the earth belongs to Allah; He inherits it to whomever He wills of His servants, and the good end is for the righteous!'
explanationEn: He also spared Musaylimah's two arrogant envoys saying 'Were it not that envoys are never killed, I would have executed you both!'—upholding diplomatic immunity strictly.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Jihad); Al-Raheeq al-Makhtum

questionEn: What touching moment occurred during the Conquest of Makkah when Abu Bakr (RA) brought his blind, white-haired elderly father Abu Quhafah to accept Islam?
optionsEn: He told Abu Quhafah to travel to Madinah
The Prophet ﷺ gently rebuked Abu Bakr out of kindness: 'Why did you not leave the old man in his house so I could come to him myself?'
explanationEn: As Abu Bakr wept joyfully seeing his aged father take the Shahadah, he said he loved that the Prophet's ﷺ uncle Abu Talib had also accepted Islam because he knew how dearly that would have pleased the Prophet ﷺ!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to the woman of Makkah from Banu Makhzum who committed theft after the Conquest when Usamah ibn Zayd (RA) tried to intercede for an exemption?
optionsEn: 'Do you intercede concerning one of Allah's prescribed boundaries? By Allah, if Fatimah daughter of Muhammad were to steal, I would cut off her hand!'
explanationEn: He explained that earlier nations perished precisely because they let powerful elites go free while punishing the weak—anchoring impartial rule of law in Islam.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ abolish pre-Islamic 'Nasi'' (intercalary calendar manipulation) during his Farewell Sermon at Mina/Arafah?
optionsEn: To restore the pure 12-lunar-month year instituted when Allah created the heavens and the earth, ending pagan tampering with Sacred Months
To copy the Roman solar calendar
explanationEn: Declaring 'Time has rotated back to its original alignment on the day Allah created the heavens and earth,' he safeguarded the pure lunar timing of Ramadan and Hajj forever.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Bad' al-Khalq); Surah Al-Tawbah 9:37

questionEn: During the Farewell Pilgrimage, what did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gently do when a young woman from Khath'am asked whether she could perform Hajj on behalf of her aged father who could barely sit on a mount?
optionsEn: He affirmed 'Yes, perform Hajj on his behalf!'—while patiently turning his young cousin al-Fadl ibn Abbas's face aside so the youth wouldn't stare at her!
explanationEn: This beautiful moment combined legal clarity (allowing Hajj al-Badal for incapacitated elders) with gentle, non-judgmental protection of modesty.

questionEn: Where did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ deliver his famous reminder during the return from the Farewell Pilgrimage regarding holding fast to Allah's Book and caring for his family (Ahl al-Bayt)?
optionsEn: At Ghadir Khumm (a watering place between Makkah and Madinah, near al-Juhfah)
explanationEn: Recorded by Zayd ibn Arqam in Sahih Muslim, he urged believers to hold firmly to the Qur'an—'Allah's rope extending from heaven to earth'—and reminded them three times: 'I remind you of Allah concerning my household!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe the spiritual bond between himself and future believers who never saw him, during his visit to Jannat al-Baqi shortly before passing?
optionsEn: Calling us 'our brothers' (Ikhwanuna), explaining: 'Those are my companions, while my brothers are those who will come after me and believe in me without seeing me!'
explanationEn: Yearning deeply to meet his future followers at his Hawd (Cistern) on Judgment Day, the Prophet ﷺ sent his love across centuries to every sincere believer today.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say during his final illness when his companions wept worrying who would wash and shroud him?
optionsEn: He told them not to shroud him
He calmly assured them not to worry, explaining that his family (Ali, al-Abbas, al-Fadl, Qutham, and Usamah/Shuqran) would wash him, and instructed them on the three white Yemeni cotton shrouds
He asked to be washed in Zamzam only
He asked to be buried in Quba
explanationEn: Even facing imminent death, his serene composure comforted his family and outlined dignified burial etiquette for all Muslims.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah; Sahih Muslim (Kitab al-Jana'iz)

questionEn: During the Prophet's ﷺ final illness, why did Umar (RA) initially stop him from calling for parchment to write a testament, and what three verbal legacies did the Prophet ﷺ still leave?
optionsEn: Seeing the Prophet ﷺ overcome with severe fever pain, Umar said 'Allah's Book is sufficient for us!'—and the Prophet ﷺ orally instructed: expel polytheist hostilities from the Peninsula, honor foreign delegations warmly, and (a third remembered as holding fast to Qur'an/prayer)
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated these three final oral counsels as the Prophet ﷺ ensured Madinah's security, hospitality to visitors, and spiritual fidelity.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ specifically instruct regarding Abu Bakr's (RA) private door opening directly into Masjid an-Nabawi during his last sermon?
optionsEn: 'Close every private door opening into the mosque except the door of Abu Bakr—for I know no one better to me in companionship than Abu Bakr!'
explanationEn: This explicit public honor reinforced Abu Bakr's uniquely close bond right before the leadership of the Ummah passed to him.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ handle the false prophet al-Aswad al-Ansi who seized parts of Yemen during the Prophet's ﷺ final months in 11 AH?
optionsEn: He signed a treaty sharing Yemen
Believers in Yemen led by Fayruz al-Daylami neutralized al-Aswad, and revelation informed the Prophet ﷺ of his death in Madinah the very night it happened!
explanationEn: Before messengers even arrived from Sanaa weeks later, the Prophet ﷺ comforted Madinah announcing that al-Aswad al-Ansi had been slain by a righteous household.

questionEn: What comforting statement did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ utter when he saw Fatimah (RA) weeping beside his bed as he suffered intense fever pain?
optionsEn: 'There will be no more suffering for your father after this day!'
explanationEn: Enduring double the fever of an ordinary person so his reward would be doubled and to console sufferers everywhere, he looked forward eagerly to peaceful reunion with Allah.

questionEn: Which faithful companion—his freedman Thawban—used to grow pale merely from thinking he wouldn't see the Prophet ﷺ in the Hereafter if placed in a lower rank of Paradise, prompting which comforting revelation?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Nisa (4:69): 'Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger—those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor: the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs, and the righteous!'
explanationEn: Matching his famous hadith 'A person will be with those whom he loves,' this verse guarantees believers reunion with the beloved Prophet ﷺ in Jannah.

questionEn: How did Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) respond emotionally after the Prophet's ﷺ passing when attempting to call the Adhan in Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: When he reached 'Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasul Allah,' tears choked his voice so deeply he could not continue, and he eventually moved to Syria so he wouldn't break down daily
explanationEn: Years later when Caliph Umar (RA) visited Jerusalem/Syria and begged Bilal to call one last Adhan, the entire army burst into sobs remembering the blessed days of Madinah.

questionEn: Who was the wise young Ansar companion—Zayd ibn Thabit (RA)—whom Abu Bakr (RA) soon entrusted with compiling the scattered written Qur'an sheets after the Prophet's ﷺ passing?
optionsEn: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA), the Prophet's ﷺ primary revelation scribe who had also attended the final review
explanationEn: Trained as a youth on the Prophet's ﷺ direct order to even master Hebrew/Syriac script in weeks, Zayd's meticulous integrity preserved the Mushaf verbatim.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare about property left behind by prophets when Fatimah (RA) later inquired about his modest land in Fadak and Khaybar?
optionsEn: 'We prophets do not leave material inheritance; whatever we leave behind is public charity (Sadaqah)'
explanationEn: True prophets leave behind knowledge, guidance, and spiritual light as their real inheritance—not personal dynasties or estates.

questionEn: How many years in total did Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ prophetic mission last from the first revelation in Cave Hira until his passing in Madinah?
optionsEn: 23 years (13 years in Makkah and 10 years in Madinah)
explanationEn: Receiving prophethood at age 40 and passing away at age 63, those 23 years reshaped human history forever.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ honor his cousin Umm Hani's (RA) grant of safety to two of her non-Muslim in-laws on the Day of the Conquest of Makkah?
optionsEn: When Ali (RA) sought to execute them, the Prophet ﷺ firmly upheld her pledge saying: 'We give shelter to whomever you have sheltered, O Umm Hani!'
explanationEn: Even during conquest, a believing woman's word of asylum was respected as binding state law, and she served him water to break his voluntary fast after he prayed eight rak'ahs of Victory (Salat al-Fath) at her home.

questionEn: How many rak'ahs of gratitude did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ perform inside Umm Hani's home right after the Conquest of Makkah—establishing Salat al-Duha / Salat al-Fath?
optionsEn: Eight rak'ahs (prayed swiftly yet completely, in pairs)
explanationEn: Umm Hani (RA) narrated she never saw him pray a lighter yet more complete eight-rak'ah prayer than that morning of victory in Makkah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare at Makkah on the second day after the Conquest regarding the eternal sanctity of Makkah?
optionsEn: 'Indeed, Allah made Makkah sacred the day He created the heavens and earth—its game is not to be chased, its thorny trees not cut, and its lost property not picked up except to announce it!'
explanationEn: Explaining that fighting was only briefly permitted for a single hour on Conquest Day, he reaffirmed Makkah's perpetual peace and ecological sanctity for every pilgrim forever.

questionEn: How did Aishah (RA) concisely summarize Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ moral character when asked about it by companions?
optionsEn: 'His character was the Qur'an (Kana khuluquhu al-Qur'an)'
explanationEn: Every ethical ideal, command, and mercy taught in the Qur'an was visibly embodied in the Prophet's ﷺ daily words and actions.

questionEn: According to Abu Hurayrah (RA), how was Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ face described by companions who beheld him?
optionsEn: As radiant as though the sun moved across his face, and he smiled more frequently than anyone else
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn al-Harith (RA) testified: 'I have never seen anyone who smiled more than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!'

questionEn: How did Anas ibn Malik (RA) describe the softness and natural fragrance of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ palm and sweat?
optionsEn: His hands were rough like stone
He never touched silk or brocade softer than the Prophet's ﷺ palm, nor smelled musk or ambergris sweeter than his natural scent
explanationEn: Companions even knew when the Prophet ﷺ had walked down a Madinah lane by the lingering sweet fragrance left in the air.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ walk when moving through Madinah, according to Abu Hurayrah and Ali (RA)?
optionsEn: With vigorous, purposeful poise, leaning slightly forward as though descending a slope
explanationEn: He walked briskly without arrogance, turning his entire body attentively whenever someone addressed him.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ speak when teaching his companions so that every listener could absorb and remember his words?
optionsEn: He spoke clearly, unhurriedly, and distinctly—sometimes repeating key points three times—so a listener could even count his words
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) noted that unlike rushed chatter, the Prophet's ﷺ speech was measured, eloquent, and lucid.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ modesty (Haya') compare to others, as narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA)?
optionsEn: He was more bashful and modest than a veiled maiden in her private quarters—and when he disliked something, it showed gently on his face without harsh words
explanationEn: Whenever addressing a community flaw, he rarely named or humiliated an individual, saying instead: 'What is the matter with some people who say such-and-such?'

questionEn: How did Ibn Abbas (RA) describe the Prophet's ﷺ unmatched generosity, especially during the month of Ramadan?
optionsEn: He gave only once a year
He was the most generous of all people, and even more generous than the fast-blowing wind carrying rain when Jibril met him every night in Ramadan
explanationEn: Asked for anything he possessed, the Prophet ﷺ never once said 'No'—even giving away a whole valley of sheep between two mountains to a stunned newcomer!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Bad' al-Wahy); Sahih Muslim

questionEn: When a needy traveler arrived in Madinah and the Prophet ﷺ had nothing left in his own home to give, what did he sometimes do out of generosity?
optionsEn: He borrowed on his own credit or asked a companion to host the guest so the needy person would never leave empty-handed
He told them to come next month
explanationEn: Once when Bilal ran out of supplies, the Prophet ﷺ borrowed food to honor guests until Allah sent provision to settle the debt.

questionEn: What did Aishah (RA) say Prophet Muhammad ﷺ regularly did inside his own home rather than acting like a king served by his wives?
optionsEn: He mended his own sandals, patched his own clothes, milked his goat, and served his family until the call to prayer sounded
explanationEn: His domestic humility sets the highest example for every husband and leader: 'The best of you is the one who is best to his family, and I am the best of you to my family.'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ react when a rough Bedouin yanked his thick-bordered Najrani cloak so violently from behind that it left red welts on his neck, demanding wealth?
optionsEn: He turned around, smiled gently, and ordered that the man be given generous provisions!
explanationEn: Anas (RA) watched in amazement as the Prophet ﷺ answered rough rudeness with warmth and boundless grace.

questionEn: What did Aishah (RA) testify about whether Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ever took personal revenge for an insult or injury against himself?
optionsEn: He never once avenged himself for any personal wrong—only upholding Allah's sacred limits when Allah's laws were violated
He held grudges for a year
explanationEn: Nor did he ever strike a woman, a child, or a servant with his hand in his entire life.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ treat children—such as his grandsons Hasan and Husayn (RA) and his granddaughter Umamah—even while leading prayer or sitting in the mosque?
optionsEn: He carried Umamah on his shoulder during Salah, setting her down in prostration and picking her up upon rising, and prolonged sujud when Hasan or Husayn climbed on his back!
He forbade children from entering the mosque
explanationEn: When companions feared something happened because his sujud lasted long, he explained: 'My grandson rode on my back and I disliked rushing him until he finished playing!'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to al-Aqra ibn Habis when al-Aqra boasted he had ten children and had never kissed any of them, amazed to see the Prophet ﷺ kissing little Hasan (RA)?
optionsEn: 'Whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy'—and 'What can I do if Allah has stripped mercy from your heart?'
explanationEn: Affectionate tenderness toward children is a sign of a living, merciful heart in Islam.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ frequently shorten a congregational prayer he had initially intended to lengthen?
optionsEn: Upon hearing a baby cry, out of compassion for the mother's distress so she wouldn't worry while praying behind him
explanationEn: Listening even to a child's cry while standing in worship before Allah shows how deeply maternal anxiety mattered to him.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ comfort Anas's little brother Abu Umayr when the toddler's pet sparrow (nughayr) died?
optionsEn: He told him boys shouldn't cry
He sat kindly with the child and gently cheered him up asking: 'O Abu Umayr, what happened to the little nughayr?'
explanationEn: Despite carrying the weight of an entire nation, the Prophet ﷺ validated a little boy's grief over a tiny pet bird.

questionEn: What special honor did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise for anyone who lovingly sponsors and raises an orphan?
optionsEn: Holding his index and middle fingers slightly apart, he said: 'I and the caretaker of an orphan will be like this in Paradise!'
explanationEn: Himself an orphan raised by relatives, he elevated caring for orphans into one of the fastest paths to his personal closeness in Jannah.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ express the immense spiritual reward of serving widows and the poor in daily life?
optionsEn: 'The one who strives to help a widow or a needy person is like a warrior in Allah's path—or like one who prays all night without tiring and fasts all day without breaking!'
explanationEn: Compassion in civic service equals continuous night worship and fasting in Allah's sight.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ treat an elderly, poor woman who used to sweep Al-Masjid an-Nabawi when she passed away during the night and companions buried her without waking him?
optionsEn: He felt deeply hurt they hadn't informed him, walked straight to her grave, and prayed Salatul-Janazah over her himself!
explanationEn: Every humble believer serving Allah's house held priceless dignity in the Prophet's ﷺ eyes.

questionEn: What happened when an emaciated, weeping camel in an Ansar's orchard walked up to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and rested its head beside him?
optionsEn: He tied it to a palm tree
The Prophet ﷺ wiped its tears behind its ears and reprimanded its owner: 'Do you not fear Allah regarding this beast He put in your care? It complained to me that you starve it and overwork it!'
explanationEn: Islam's environmental and animal ethics flow directly from his mercy—even warning that a woman entered Hellfire solely for starving a trapped cat, while another was forgiven for giving water to a panting dog!
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Jihad); Sahih al-Bukhari

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ order when his companions took two tiny chicks from a mother bird's nest during a journey, causing the mother bird to flutter frantically above them?
optionsEn: 'Who has distressed this bird by taking her chicks? Return her chicks to her immediately!'
explanationEn: Seeing the grief of even a tiny mother bird moved the Prophet ﷺ to restore her young instantly.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach conservation of water even while performing ablution (wudu)?
optionsEn: Passing Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas using extra water, he asked 'Why this extravagance?'—and when Sa'd asked if wasting exists in wudu, he replied: 'Yes, even if you are beside a flowing river!'
explanationEn: Using only a mudd (~half-liter) for wudu and a sa' for ghusl modeled mindful environmental stewardship long before modern conservation.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah (Kitab al-Taharah); Sahih al-Bukhari

questionEn: What ecological encouragement did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give about planting trees even when a believer sees the signs of the End of the World?
optionsEn: 'If the Final Hour comes while one of you has a palm shoot in his hand, if he can plant it before the Hour arrives, let him plant it!'
explanationEn: Even at the end of time, planting for future life and charity (sadaqah jariyah) remains a sacred act of worship.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when a Bedouin urinated inside a corner of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi and companions jumped up shouting to stop him?
optionsEn: He banned Bedouins from the mosque

'Leave him alone and do not interrupt him!'—then had a bucket of water poured over the spot and gently taught the man: 'These mosques are not for filth, but for remembrance of Allah, Salah, and Qur'an'
explanationEn: Amazed by the Prophet's ﷺ patience compared to the companions' anger, that Bedouin prayed: 'O Allah, have mercy on me and Muhammad, and no one else!'—to which the Prophet ﷺ chuckled gently: 'You have narrowed something vast!'

questionEn: What was Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ sense of humor like with his family and companions?
optionsEn: Warm, playful, and affectionate—yet he never uttered anything except the literal truth, even when joking
explanationEn: For instance, he teased an elderly woman saying 'No old woman enters Paradise'—then smiled and recited that Allah recreates all women of Paradise as youthful peers in beauty!

questionEn: What gentle joke did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ play on the loyal Bedouin companion Zahir ibn Hiram (RA) in the marketplace of Madinah?
optionsEn: Sneaking up behind Zahir, the Prophet ﷺ hugged him and playfully called out 'Who will buy this slave?'—and when Zahir sighed 'You will find me worthless,' he replied: 'In Allah's sight, you are precious!'
explanationEn: Through playful warmth, the Prophet ﷺ lifted the self-worth of a humble villager who felt overlooked in society.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ react when he found a companion eating food he disliked?
optionsEn: He never once criticized any food in his life; if he liked it, he ate it, and if he disliked it, he simply left it silently
explanationEn: Refined gratitude meant never hurting the feelings of anyone who prepared or served a meal.

questionEn: Did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ever eat reclining lazily on cushions like arrogant monarchs—and how did he explain his posture?
optionsEn: No; he sat modestly on the floor or kneeled humbly, saying: 'I eat as a servant eats and I sit as a servant sits'
explanationEn: He also never ate off raised luxury tables (khiwan), instead sharing simple dishes placed on a leather mat on the floor.

questionEn: What was Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ routine regarding meals in his household, as Aishah (RA) sadly yet proudly recalled years later?
optionsEn: Months passed without a cooking fire ever being lit in his wives' homes—they survived simply on dates and water ('the two black ones')
explanationEn: Although wealth from Arabia poured into Madinah in his later years, he gave it all away to the needy before sunset, living in voluntary simplicity so his family never ate wheat bread for three consecutive days.

questionEn: What was Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ bed made of when Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) visited him and wept seeing rough woven palm-fiber mat marks imprinted on the Prophet's ﷺ side?
optionsEn: A rough leather mat stuffed with date-palm fibers (lif), while Persian and Byzantine kings slept on silk
explanationEn: When Umar wept seeing the imprint on his side, the Prophet ﷺ comforted him: 'Are you not pleased, O Umar, that for them is this world and for us is the Hereafter?'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ behave whenever entering his home—a sunnah of cleanliness and intimacy?
optionsEn: The very first thing he did upon entering home was brush his teeth with a siwak (miswak) and greet his family warmly with Salam
explanationEn: Using the siwak before entering home, before prayer, and upon waking reflected his remarkable personal hygiene and consideration for others.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ treat people when shaking their hands in greeting?
optionsEn: He only shook hands with chiefs
He gave a quick nod from afar
He was never the first to pull his hand away until the other person released his hand first, and never turned his face away until the speaker finished
explanationEn: Every person who sat with him felt as though they were the most honored individual in the entire gathering.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about greeting children and marginalized people as he walked through Madinah's streets?
optionsEn: He always initiated Salam warmly to children playing in the street, enslaved workers, and poor widows—even walking hand-in-hand with a female servant across Madinah to settle her need!
He waited to be greeted first
explanationEn: Anas (RA) narrated that even an ordinary servant girl in Madinah could take the Prophet's ﷺ hand and lead him anywhere in town to help resolve her difficulty.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gently counsel a young man who boldly walked into his gathering asking permission to commit zinā (fornication)?
optionsEn: When companions shouted angrily, he drew the youth close and asked calmly: 'Would you like it for your mother? Your daughter? Your sister? Your aunt?'—then placed his hand on his chest and prayed for his purity!
He refused to speak to him
explanationEn: Instead of shaming the confused youth, Socratic empathy plus loving du'a transformed his heart—and the youth testified he hated nothing more than that sin forever after!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ do when his beloved daughter Fatimah (RA) entered his room—a breathtaking model of honoring daughters?
optionsEn: He told her to wait outside
He stood up to greet her, took her by the hand, kissed her forehead/hand, and seated her in his very own place!
explanationEn: In an era where girls had once been buried alive, the Prophet ﷺ publicly elevated daughters with tenderness, warmth, and honor—and Fatimah (RA) did the exact same whenever he visited her.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Adab); Jami' al-Tirmidhi

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ settle domestic disagreements in his own household—such as when Aishah (RA) and Hafsah or his wives once spoke firmly to him?
optionsEn: With remarkable patience, good humor, and gentle listening—even letting Abu Bakr mediate once while teasing Aishah gently afterward
By banning his wives from speaking
explanationEn: Umar (RA) marveled that whereas Quraysh men dominated their wives harshly, Madinah's Ansar wives conversed boldly—and the Prophet ﷺ patiently let his wives express feelings openly.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ famously express playful romance and partnership with Aishah (RA) during journeys?
optionsEn: He had the caravan move ahead while he foot-raced Aishah (RA) twice—she won the first race when slim, and he won later smiling: 'This one is for that one!'
explanationEn: He also drank from the exact rim of the cup where Aishah's lips touched and leaned in her lap while reciting Qur'an—modeling joyful, respectful companionship in marriage.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Jihad); Sahih Muslim

questionEn: What practical etiquette did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ practice regarding cleanliness, grooming his hair and beard, and wearing pleasant scent?
optionsEn: He kept himself impeccably clean, oiled and combed his hair and beard, loved fragrance (especially musk), and refused to enter gatherings smelling of raw garlic or onions
He wore tattered unwashed rags intentionally
explanationEn: He taught that 'Allah is Beautiful and loves beauty'—clarifying that wearing clean, handsome clothes is NOT arrogance; arrogance is rejecting truth and looking down on people.

questionEn: Which colors and types of clothing did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ most frequently wear and love?
optionsEn: Clean white garments (calling white the best of garments for the living and shrouding the dead), plus Yemeni striped cloaks (hibarah) and green on occasion
explanationEn: While prohibiting pure silk and gold for Muslim men so simplicity prevailed, he loved crisp white cotton and neat Yemeni cloaks.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe the two blessings most people overlook and squander in daily life?
optionsEn: Good health and free time (Al-Sihhah wal-Faragh)
explanationEn: He urged believers to seize five things before five: youth before old age, health before sickness, wealth before poverty, free time before busyness, and life before death.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise when a companion asked him for a single, comprehensive piece of life advice?
optionsEn: 'Do not get angry!' ('La taghdab')—repeating it multiple times when the man kept asking for more
explanationEn: He also taught that the truly strong person is NOT the one who wrestles others down, but the one who controls himself in a moment of anger.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ react when he accidentally learned that a Jewish lender named Zayd ibn Su'nah aggressively grabbed his collar in public demanding early repayment of a loan?
optionsEn: Smiling calmly when Umar jumped to defend him, he told Umar: 'We both needed something better from you—to tell me to repay nicely and tell him to ask nicely!'—then repaid in full plus 20 extra sa's of dates!
explanationEn: Zayd revealed he had deliberately tested the Prophet's ﷺ patience against Torah signs of the final prophet ('his forbearance outstrips his anger')—and embraced Islam on the spot!

questionEn: Which two traits did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ state weigh heaviest on the believer's scale on the Day of Resurrection?
explanationEn: He further promised: 'The most beloved of you to me and the closest to me in seating on the Day of Resurrection are those of you with the best character!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ define true bankruptcy ('Al-Muflis') in his Ummah—warning companions against spiritual self-destruction?
optionsEn: Someone who comes on Judgment Day with mountains of prayer, fasting, and charity, yet insulted, slandered, struck, and cheated others—so his good deeds are transferred to his victims until none remain!
explanationEn: This sobering teaching ties worship directly to ethical accountability toward every fellow human being.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say was the core purpose of his entire prophetic mission regarding human morals?
optionsEn: 'I was sent to build tall towers'
'I was only sent to perfect noble moral character (makarima/saliha al-akhlaq)'
explanationEn: Islam elevates both existing human virtues (honesty, hospitality, courage) and perfects them through sincere devotion to Allah.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond whenever offered a choice between two permissible paths in daily life?
optionsEn: He always chose the easier of the two, so long as it involved no sin—and if it involved sin, he stayed the farthest of all people from it
He always picked the hardest path
explanationEn: This prophetic principle—choosing ease without compromising ethics—shapes Islamic life and pilgrimage ease.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ensure no one felt invisible or inferior when he sat in a circle with his companions?
optionsEn: He sat wherever there was an empty spot in the circle rather than reserving a raised throne, so newcomers often couldn't even tell which man was the Prophet ﷺ until asking!
explanationEn: Traveling Bedouins frequently entered Masjid an-Nabawi asking: 'Which one of you is Muhammad?'—so completely did he blend in with his companions in modesty.

questionEn: What rule of empathy did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach when three people sit together so no one feels excluded or hurt?
optionsEn: 'When you are three, two of you must not whisper secretly excluding the third, for that saddens him!'
explanationEn: Even subtle social exclusion that bruises a companion's heart was gently prohibited by the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ greet companions who were sick, marginalized, or absent—like his regular visits to sick people across Madinah?
optionsEn: He visited the sick even at the farthest edge of Madinah, comforted them gently with 'La ba'sa, tahurun in sha' Allah' (No harm, it is a purification, God willing), and prayed for their healing
explanationEn: He even visited a sick Jewish youth who had served him, sitting kindly by his head and inviting him gently to Islam before his passing.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach his companions about bravery when a terrifying loud noise startled Madinah at night?
optionsEn: Before anyone else even saddled up, the Prophet ﷺ had already ridden Abu Talhah's unsaddled horse bareback toward the sound with his sword slung, returning to reassure them: 'Do not be afraid!'
explanationEn: Ali (RA) testified that whenever battle grew fiercest and eyes turned red, companions took shelter behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who stood closest to the enemy.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ eat with others at a shared platter, teaching table manners to young Umar ibn Abi Salamah (RA)?
optionsEn: 'O boy, mention Allah's Name (Bismillah), eat with your right hand, and eat from what is directly in front of you!'
explanationEn: This brief, warm three-part guidance to his stepson shaped Muslim dining etiquette for every generation.

questionEn: On which side did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ habitually sleep at night—and what did he do with his right hand as he lay down?
optionsEn: On his right side, placing his right hand beneath his right cheek and reciting sleeping adhkar
explanationEn: Even his sleep posture began with wudu, dusting the bed thrice, and entrusting his soul peacefully to Allah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about returning good for good and showing gratitude to people?
optionsEn: 'Whoever does not thank people has not thanked Allah'—and he always returned gifts with equal or greater kindness
explanationEn: He accepted gifts (never charity/sadaqah for himself) and always rewarded givers generously so gratitude remained reciprocal.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Adab); Jami' al-Tirmidhi

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when his companions stood up respectfully as he entered a room?
optionsEn: He disliked people standing up for him out of veneration like Persian/Byzantine kings, saying: 'Do not exaggerate in praising me as the Christians praised the son of Mary; I am only Allah's servant and Messenger'
explanationEn: Anas (RA) noted no person was dearer to the companions than him, yet seeing him enter they did not stand because they knew how strongly he disliked royal pomp.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ treat elderly non-Muslim neighbors and visitors—and what did he teach about respecting all elders?
optionsEn: 'He is not of us who does not show mercy to our young ones and honor to our elders!'
explanationEn: Revering gray-haired elders—giving them priority in speech, serving water to the eldest first unless permitted otherwise—is woven deeply into the Sunnah.

questionEn: When water or milk was served in a gathering where an elder sat on the Prophet's ﷺ left and a young boy (Ibn Abbas) sat on his right, what did the Prophet ﷺ do?
optionsEn: Honoring the Sunnah of passing to the right while respecting the elder, he kindly asked young Ibn Abbas's permission before handing it to the elder—and Ibn Abbas lovingly refused to give up his leftover blessing from the Prophet's ﷺ cup!
He gave it to the elder without asking
explanationEn: Asking a child's explicit permission showed breathtaking fairness and respect for a young person's rightful turn.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise regarding speaking truthfully versus joking or telling white lies to entertain people?
optionsEn: 'Woe to him who tells lies to make people laugh; woe to him, woe to him!'—and 'Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise'
explanationEn: He guaranteed a palace in the highest Paradise for the one who abandons lying even when joking, and a palace in its center for one who stops arguing even when in the right!
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Adab); Sahih al-Bukhari

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ handle criticism or slander leveled against his companions in private?
optionsEn: 'Let none of you tell me anything bad about my companions, for I love to come out to you with a pure, open heart!'
explanationEn: He guarded his own heart against gossip (namimah) so he could meet every companion with unblemished warmth and trust.

questionEn: What advice did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give Abu Dharr (RA) about never looking down on any small good deed?
optionsEn: 'Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful, smiling face!'
explanationEn: Even smiling at a fellow pilgrim or neighbor is an effortless, continuous charity (sadaqah) in the prophetic way.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ view tribal racism or boasting over ancestors ('Asabiyyah)?
optionsEn: 'He is not one of us who calls to tribalism, fights for tribalism, or dies for tribalism'—and 'Leave it, for it is foul!'
explanationEn: When a dispute broke out and someone insulted Bilal's mother's dark skin, the Prophet ﷺ sharply rebuked Abu Dharr: 'You are a man who still has traces of Jahiliyyah in you!'—and Abu Dharr humbled himself placing his cheek on the dust for Bilal to step over!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Iman); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about anyone who enters Paradise—showing how inward purity matters far more than outward status?
optionsEn: 'Indeed Allah does not look at your outward appearance or your wealth, rather He looks at your hearts and your deeds'
explanationEn: This liberating hadith frees believers from vanity and anchors spirituality in sincerity of heart (ikhlas).

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gently resolve a dispute between Abu Bakr and Umar (RA) when Abu Bakr hurried to apologize and Umar briefly turned away?
optionsEn: When Umar arrived full of remorse, the Prophet ﷺ stood defending Abu Bakr: 'Allah sent me to you and you said You lie, while Abu Bakr said He speaks the truth—will you not leave my companion alone for me?!'
He exiled both for a week
explanationEn: After that gentle yet firm defense of his loyal friend, nobody ever wounded Abu Bakr (RA) again.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about his love for good omens (Al-Fa'l al-Hasan) versus superstition/evil omens (Tiyarah)?
optionsEn: He believed owls bring bad luck
He forbade pessimistic superstitions (tiyarah), yet loved an optimistic hopeful word (fa'l) such as a pleasing name
explanationEn: Replacing fatalistic superstition with hopeful trust in Allah kept his heart buoyant even in dark seasons.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ react when people gave someone a gloomy or harsh name?
optionsEn: He gently changed negative names (like 'Harb'/War or 'Hazn'/Hardship) to hopeful ones like 'Sahl' (Ease) or 'Jamilah' (Beautiful)
explanationEn: For instance, he changed a woman's name from 'Asiyah' (Disobedient) to 'Jamilah' (Beautiful), reflecting his sensitivity to uplifting speech.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ model financial integrity when borrowing money or paying workers?
optionsEn: He commanded: 'Give the hired worker his wages before his sweat dries!' and always repaid loans with something even better ('The best of you are those best in repaying debts')
explanationEn: Fair labor dignity and generous repayment were hallmarks of his leadership.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah (Kitab al-Ruhun); Sahih al-Bukhari

questionEn: What remarkable compassion did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ show regarding funeral prayers for a Muslim who died owing an unpaid debt?
optionsEn: Initially he had companions pray over indebted deceased until Allah opened Madinah's treasury—whereupon he announced: 'Whoever leaves wealth, it is for his heirs; and whoever leaves a debt or helpless dependents, bring them to me, for I am their guardian and will pay their debts!'
explanationEn: Creating a social safety net from the public treasury meant no widow, orphan, or indebted soul was ever abandoned.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ treat an enslaved boy or worker in his care, according to his universal teaching on brotherhood?
optionsEn: 'Your servants are your brothers whom Allah placed under your authority; feed them from what you eat, clothe them from what you wear, and do not burden them beyond their capacity—or help them yourselves!'
explanationEn: He also strictly forbade calling them 'my slave' or 'my slave-girl,' instructing instead 'my young man / my young lady' to uphold human dignity.

questionEn: When traveling on campaigns or journeys with companions, how did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ divide chores like collecting firewood for cooking?
optionsEn: He refused special exemption, insisting 'I hate to be singled out above you, for Allah dislikes seeing His servant distinguish himself over his companions'—and went to gather firewood himself!
He assigned all work to Bilal
He stayed in his tent resting
explanationEn: True prophetic leadership led from the front—sharing hunger, brick-laying, trench-digging, and camp firewood equally.

questionEn: Where did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ routinely ride in a traveling caravan—at the front with scouts or at the back?
optionsEn: Often at the rear of the caravan, to help the weak, lift tired travelers behind him on his mount, and pray for stragglers
explanationEn: A shepherd of souls always checks on the slowest and weakest members of the flock.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach travelers returning home from a journey—including pilgrims returning from Umrah or Hajj?
optionsEn: Fast for three days upon return
Not to arrive unannounced at night startling their families, and to stop first at the mosque to pray two rak'ahs before greeting loved ones with joy
explanationEn: His travel etiquette blended spiritual gratitude (two rak'ahs in the masjid) with considerate tenderness toward one's spouse and household.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise about love for one's neighbor, regardless of closeness?
optionsEn: 'Jibril kept advising me so continuously about caring for the neighbor that I thought he was going to make the neighbor an heir!'
explanationEn: He even urged when cooking broth to add extra water so a portion could be shared warmly with the neighbor next door!

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach believers to judge whether they have true faith when thinking of others' happiness?
optionsEn: 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself'
explanationEn: This golden rule of empathetic brotherhood uproots envy and nurtures sincere well-wishing.

questionEn: What was Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ reaction whenever he heard a companion say something harsh against the wind, fever, or time?
optionsEn: He forbade cursing the wind, fever, rooster, or time—reminding them that Allah sends the wind for mercy and 'Do not curse time, for Allah is the Creator/Controller of Time!'
explanationEn: Even in discomfort, prophetic speech remained free of profanity, curses, and complaints against Allah's decree.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when he saw companions arguing loudly at the door of Aishah's room over an unpaid debt (Ka'b ibn Malik and Ibn Abi Hadrad)?
optionsEn: He drew back the curtain smiling, motioned with his hand asking Ka'b to forgive half the debt—and when Ka'b immediately agreed, told the debtor: 'Rise and pay him!'
explanationEn: Gentle mediation paired with encouraging voluntary generosity healed conflict in seconds.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to a companion who asked if a person who loves his own people is guilty of tribal bigotry?
optionsEn: 'No! Bigotry is helping your people in injustice (zulm)'—affirming healthy love for family and homeland as natural, while forbidding defending wrong
explanationEn: Just as he deeply loved Makkah and Madinah, he drew a crystal-clear line between wholesome belonging and blind injustice.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Adab); Sunan Ibn Majah

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ honor his longtime wet-nurse's foster family and Khadijah's (RA) elderly friends long after Khadijah passed away?
optionsEn: Whenever he slaughtered a sheep, he personally cut portions and said: 'Send this to Khadijah's friends'—explaining simply: 'I loved her!'
explanationEn: When Khadijah's sister Halah once knocked at the door sounding just like Khadijah, the Prophet ﷺ started tenderly in joyful remembrance: 'O Allah, let it be Halah!'

questionEn: What simple everyday habit did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ never forget when seeing himself in a mirror?
optionsEn: He praised Allah and prayed: 'O Allah, just as You made my physical form handsome, make my moral character beautiful!'
explanationEn: Turning an ordinary glimpse in the mirror into a du'a for inner beauty reflects his constant God-consciousness.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when companions asked him to invoke a curse against the polytheists during intense persecution?
optionsEn: 'I was not sent as a curser (la'anan); rather, I was sent solely as a mercy!'
explanationEn: His self-understanding echoed Allah's words in Surah Al-Anbiya (21:107): 'We have not sent you except as a mercy to all the worlds.'
reference: Sahih Muslim (Kitab al-Birr wal-Silah); Surah Al-Anbiya 21:107

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about the power of a gentle tone ('Rifq') in every human interaction?
optionsEn: 'Gentleness is never placed in anything except that it adorns it, and never removed from anything except that it disfigures it!'
explanationEn: He told Aishah (RA): 'Indeed Allah is Gentle (Rafiq) and loves gentleness, and gives for gentleness what He never gives for harshness!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ treat an enslaved girl in Madinah who was afraid of being punished after delaying an errand?
optionsEn: When Aishah (RA) freed/helped or when Anas delayed, Anas testified the Prophet ﷺ never once said 'Uff!' or asked 'Why did you do this?' or 'Why didn't you do that?' across ten full years!
explanationEn: Even when the Prophet's ﷺ own household members blamed young Anas, the Prophet ﷺ defended him gently: 'Leave him! If it had been decreed, it would have happened.'

questionEn: What physical posture did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ strictly maintain regarding not hurting or embarrassing people's feelings during sermons?
optionsEn: He called out names from the minbar
He praised good in public and corrected mistakes anonymously ('What is wrong with people who...'), preserving personal dignity
explanationEn: This timeless prophetic pedagogy corrects behavior effectively while protecting every believer's honor.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Nikah); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ react when a companion once sneezed inside prayer and another companion whispered 'Yarhamukallah'—and then others slapped their thighs to hush him?
optionsEn: He ordered the prayer restarted forcefully

After finishing Salah, Mu'awiyah ibn al-Hakam testified: 'By Allah, I never saw a better teacher before or after him! He neither scolded, struck, nor insulted me—he simply explained gently that human speech isn't allowed in Salah!'
explanationEn: Mu'awiyah's heartfelt testimony captures the warmth that drew thousands to learn at the Prophet's ﷺ feet.

questionEn: What was Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ favorite way to cheer up a weeping or anxious companion—such as Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) riding a slow, exhausted camel back from a campaign?
optionsEn: He dropped back beside Jabir, tapped the camel gently with a blessing so it outpaced the army, chatted warmly about Jabir's recent marriage to care for his orphaned sisters, and bought the camel while gifting it back to Jabir too!
explanationEn: By buying Jabir's camel at a generous price and then gifting both the price and the camel back to help Jabir's orphaned sisters, he eased Jabir's dignity without making him feel like a charity case!

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ask Jabir (RA) why he married an older experienced woman rather than a young maiden—and bless Jabir's reason?
optionsEn: When Jabir explained his father died at Uhud leaving seven young sisters needing an experienced mother-figure to comb their hair and care for them, the Prophet ﷺ warmly blessed his selfless sacrifice!
He asked for half his dates
He told him to divorce her
explanationEn: Even in personal family advice, the Prophet ﷺ respected noble sacrifices made for orphaned siblings.

questionEn: What special honor did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pay to guests—even a non-Muslim guest who dirtied his bedding overnight and fled in embarrassment at dawn?
optionsEn: Finding the soiled bed, the Prophet ﷺ quietly washed it with his own hands—and when the stunned man returned for his forgotten sword, the Prophet ﷺ greeted him warmly, leading the man to embrace Islam!
explanationEn: Humility and hospitality turned shame into awe and immediate faith.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ model punctuality and keeping promises even before his prophethood?
optionsEn: Waiting three full days at a meeting spot until his forgetful associate Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hamsa remembered and returned, saying gently only: 'You caused me trouble, young man—I have been waiting here three days for you!'
explanationEn: Extreme fidelity to one's word defined him both before and after revelation.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about envy (Hasad) and harboring hatred between believers?
optionsEn: 'Do not hate one another, do not envy one another, do not turn your backs on one another—be, O servants of Allah, brothers! It is not lawful for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three days'
explanationEn: He further praised the better of two estranged brothers as the very first one to extend Salam!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare about someone whose heart is spotless and whose tongue is truthful—when companions asked 'Who is the best of people?'
optionsEn: 'Every pure-hearted (makhmum al-qalb) and truthful-tongued person'—explaining pure-hearted means God-conscious, pure, free of sin, transgression, malice, and envy!
explanationEn: Prioritizing an unblemished heart free of malice over outer prestige defines Islamic spirituality.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach believers to transform ordinary daily habits—like smiling, removing a harmful thorn from the road, or feeding one's spouse—into acts of worship?
optionsEn: By declaring that even placing a morsel of food lovingly into one's spouse's mouth seeking Allah's reward counts as charity (Sadaqah)!
explanationEn: Through sincere intention (niyyah), every act of kindness inside the home becomes worship.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the companion Julaybib (RA), a poor, socially marginalized man in Madinah whom nobody wanted to marry?
optionsEn: He told Julaybib to stay single

He personally proposed to a noble Ansar family on Julaybib's behalf, whose pious daughter accepted saying 'Would I refuse the Messenger of Allah?!'—and after Julaybib fell as a hero in battle, the Prophet ﷺ held him in his own arms saying: 'He is of me and I am of him!'
explanationEn: After burying Julaybib with his own hands, the Prophet's ﷺ blessing made that widow's household one of the most honored and generous in Madinah.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ show deep sensitivity to people's differing spiritual capacities when leading prayer or teaching?
optionsEn: 'Whoever leads people in prayer should keep it light, for among them are the weak, the sick, and the elderly; when praying alone, lengthen it as much as you wish!'
explanationEn: When Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA) once recited Surah Al-Baqarah in Isha causing a tired farmer to leave early, the Prophet ﷺ gently rebuked Mu'adh three times: 'Are you putting people to trial (A-fattanun anta), O Mu'adh?!'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise his companions about visiting one another or attending Friday sermons with modesty and mutual care?
optionsEn: Never to force someone out of their seat to take it, rather 'Make room and spread out' (Surah 58:11), and let everyone sit comfortably together
explanationEn: Even seating inside the mosque mirrored prophetic egalitarianism.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ react when a person gave him a small humble gift—even a simple sheep's trotter or a bowl of buttermilk?
optionsEn: He accepted even the smallest gift graciously, saying 'Even if I were invited to a meal of a sheep's foot, I would accept; and if gifted a shoulder or foot, I would accept!'
explanationEn: Accepting humble offerings gratefully protected the dignity of the poor and fostered love ('Exchange gifts, and you will love one another!').

questionEn: What gentle habit did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ practice whenever he felt deeply joyful or grateful for good news?
optionsEn: He immediately fell into Sujud al-Shukr (prostration of gratitude) to Allah
explanationEn: Both in triumph and small personal blessings, his instinct was instant physical humility before Allah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say whenever he saw someone afflicted with a visible hardship or illness?
optionsEn: He taught believers to say quietly (without the person hearing): 'Praise be to Allah who spared me what He tested you with and favored me greatly over many whom He created'
explanationEn: Gratitude paired with tactful silence prevented ever hurting an afflicted person's feelings.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ instruct believers to respond if someone insults them while they are fasting or angry?
optionsEn: 'Let him not behave ignorantly or shout; if someone fights or insults him, let him simply say twice: Indeed I am fasting!'
explanationEn: Fasting in the prophetic school trains the tongue and temper just as much as the stomach.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ handle someone who confessed a grave sin privately out of deep remorse, begging to be purified?
optionsEn: He repeatedly turned his face away offering opportunities for quiet private repentance to Allah first, showing Allah loves concealing sins when someone repents sincerely
He turned them out of Madinah
explanationEn: For instance, when a man came saying 'I committed a sin requiring punishment,' and then prayed behind him, the Prophet ﷺ smiled after prayer saying: 'Did you not pray with us just now? Allah has forgiven your sin!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise believers on balancing worldly effort with complete trust in Allah (Tawakkul)?
optionsEn: When a Bedouin asked 'Should I leave my camel untied and trust Allah?' he replied: 'Tie her first, and THEN trust in Allah!'
explanationEn: 'I'qilha wa tawakkal' ('Tie your camel and rely on Allah') remains one of the sharpest, most practical principles in Islamic spirituality.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the three qualities of a true believer's moderation in life, warning against religious extremism?
optionsEn: 'Indeed this religion is ease (Yusr); no one overburdens himself in religion except that it overwhelms him—so aim for steady moderation, seek nearness, and take glad tidings!'
explanationEn: When three men vowed to pray all night forever, fast daily forever, and never marry, the Prophet ﷺ corrected them firmly: 'I pray and sleep, I fast and break fast, and I marry—whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me!'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) when Abdullah wanted to recite the entire Qur'an in one night and fast every single day?
optionsEn: 'Your body has a right over you, your eyes have a right over you, and your wife has a right over you—fast three days a month (or alternate days like Dawud) and finish Qur'an once a month or week!'
explanationEn: Balancing spiritual devotion with bodily health and family love is the enduring hallmark of Prophetic Sunnah.

questionEn: Which comprehensive Qur'anic verse sums up Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ compassionate leadership style toward his companions?
optionsEn: 'So by mercy from Allah, you were lenient with them; had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have dispersed from around you' (Surah Aal Imran 3:159)
'By time, indeed mankind is in loss' (103:1-2)
'Read in the name of your Lord' (96:1)
explanationEn: Allah Himself praised His Messenger's ﷺ gentleness, pardon, du'a for others, and consultation (Shura) as the secret that bound hearts around him.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ continue standing in night prayer (Tahajjud) until his blessed feet cracked and swelled, even though Allah had already forgiven all his past and future sins?
optionsEn: He answered Aishah (RA): 'Should I not then be a grateful servant (Abdan Shakura)?'
Because he could not sleep in Madinah
explanationEn: His night worship flowed not from fear of punishment alone, but from overflowing gratitude and love for Allah.

questionEn: How many units (rak'ahs) did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ usually pray in his regular night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl / Tahajjud including Witr), as narrated by Aishah (RA)?
optionsEn: Eleven (or thirteen) rak'ahs, never exceeding that in Ramadan or outside Ramadan—prayed with extraordinary length and beauty
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) marveled: 'Do not ask about their beauty and length!'—praying four, then four, then three Witr, or in pairs followed by Witr.

questionEn: What tender words did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ frequently say to Bilal (RA) when the time for Salah approached, showing what prayer meant to his soul?
optionsEn: 'O Bilal, call the Iqamah and give us comfort through it (Arihna biha, ya Bilal)!'
explanationEn: Far from viewing Salah as a chore to get over with, the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The coolness (comfort/delight) of my eyes has been placed in Salah!'
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Adab); Sunan al-Nasa'i

questionEn: What did Companions hear coming from Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ chest whenever he stood in deep prayer before Allah?
optionsEn: A sound like the simmering of a boiling cooking pot from his quiet weeping out of awe of Allah
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir (RA) described seeing him pray with a low bubbling sob inside his chest like a boiling kettle.

questionEn: Which two voluntary sunnah rak'ahs did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ guard more consistently than any other voluntary prayer—even saying they are better than the entire world and all it contains?
optionsEn: The two Sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr prayer
explanationEn: Even while traveling, he never left the two light Sunnah rak'ahs of Fajr (al-Fajr Sunnah) or Witr at night.

questionEn: How many regular voluntary Sunnah prayers (Rawatib) did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise earn a house built in Paradise for whoever maintains them daily?
optionsEn: Twelve rak'ahs: 4 before Dhuhr, 2 after Dhuhr, 2 after Maghrib, 2 after Isha, and 2 before Fajr
explanationEn: Umm Habibah (RA) narrated this promise from the Prophet ﷺ and never abandoned those 12 Rawatib rak'ahs afterward.

questionEn: What morning prayer did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise Abu Hurayrah and Abu al-Darda (RA) never to abandon, explaining it fulfills charity for every one of the 360 joints in the human body?
explanationEn: Two rak'ahs of Duha after sunrise suffice as gratitude for all 360 joints of the body.

questionEn: When was Prophet Muhammad ﷺ closest to his Lord during Salah, as he specifically instructed believers to multiply their personal du'as?
explanationEn: He taught: 'The closest a servant comes to his Lord is when he is in prostration, so increase your supplications therein!'

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ urge believers to pray voluntary (Nafl) prayers at home rather than turning their homes into 'graves'?
optionsEn: To bring barakah and spiritual light into family life and model worship before children, while keeping obligatory prayers in congregation
explanationEn: He also encouraged reciting Surah Al-Baqarah inside one's home so Shaytan flees from it.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ step back after leading three nights of congregational Ramadan night prayer (Tarawih/Qiyam) in Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Out of deep mercy, fearing it might become obligatory upon his Ummah and overwhelm them
explanationEn: When crowds packed the mosque on the fourth night, he waited inside until Fajr and explained tenderly why he stayed home—showing his constant concern not to overburden believers.

questionEn: What spiritual retreat did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ consistently observe during the last ten nights of every Ramadan in Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: I'tikaf (secluding himself inside the mosque to seek Laylat al-Qadr in uninterrupted worship and remembrance)
Fasting without breaking fast for ten days
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) noted that when the last ten nights entered, the Prophet ﷺ tightened his waist-wrapper, stayed awake all night, and woke his family gently for worship.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Fadl Laylat al-Qadr & Kitab al-I'tikaf)

questionEn: Which short, profoundly comprehensive du'a did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach Aishah (RA) to recite on Laylat al-Qadr?
optionsEn: 'Allahumma innaka 'Afuwwun tuhibbul-'afwa fa'fu 'anni' ('O Allah, You are Pardoning and love to pardon, so pardon me!')
explanationEn: Asking Allah for 'Afw (erasing sins completely without trace) captures the highest spiritual aspiration of Ramadan's most sacred night.

questionEn: Which days of every lunar month and week did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ most commonly observe voluntary fasting?
optionsEn: Mondays and Thursdays, plus the three White Days (13th, 14th, and 15th of each lunar month), and extensively in Sha'ban
explanationEn: He explained deeds are presented to Allah on Mondays and Thursdays, and he loved having his deeds presented while fasting.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ institute fasting the Day of Ashura (10th of Muharram)—and instruct Muslims to also fast the 9th day alongside it?
optionsEn: Because Allah saved Musa (AS) and Bani Isra'il from Pharaoh on Ashura ('We have more right to Musa than they!'), adding the 9th to maintain distinct Islamic identity
explanationEn: Fasting Ashura expiates the sins of the previous year, while fasting Arafah (9 Dhul-Hijjah, for non-pilgrims) expiates the past and coming year!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise about fasting six days in Shawwal right after completing Ramadan?
optionsEn: It is rewarded as if one fasted the entire year (360 days, since every good deed is multiplied tenfold)
explanationEn: Thirty days of Ramadan plus six days of Shawwal (36 x 10 = 360) equals a full year of continuous reward.

questionEn: How frequently did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ personally seek Allah's forgiveness (Istighfar) every single day, even though he was sinless?
optionsEn: More than 70 times (and up to 100 times in a single sitting) daily
explanationEn: His constant Istighfar taught humility and continuous spiritual elevation—never feeling self-satisfied before Allah.

questionEn: What touching incident occurred when Prophet Muhammad ﷺ asked Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) to recite the Qur'an to him?
optionsEn: When Ibn Mas'ud reached Surah Al-Nisa (4:41: 'How will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you as a witness against these?'), the Prophet ﷺ said 'Enough!'—and Ibn Mas'ud looked up to see tears streaming down his face!
The Prophet ﷺ corrected every word
explanationEn: Asked why he asked Ibn Mas'ud to recite when the Qur'an was revealed to him, he replied tenderly: 'I love to hear it recited by someone else!'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA) that made Ubayy weep with overwhelming joy?
optionsEn: 'Indeed Allah commanded me to recite Surah Al-Bayyinah (98) to you!'—and when Ubayy asked 'Did Allah mention me by name?!', he replied: 'Yes!'
explanationEn: Recognizing Ubayy as the foremost Qur'an reciter of the Ummah showed how dearly Allah treasures sincere devotion to His Book.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ compare the difference between one who remembers Allah (makes Dhikr) and one who does not?
optionsEn: Like the difference between the living and the dead!
explanationEn: Dhikr is the breath and pulse of the believer's soul—without it, the heart grows spiritually lifeless.

questionEn: What are the 'two words light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful' taught at the very close of Sahih al-Bukhari?
explanationEn: Effortless to whisper while walking, waiting, or making Tawaf, these two phrases carry immense eternal weight.

questionEn: Which short, potent phrase did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) as 'one of the treasures of Paradise'?
optionsEn: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah ('There is no power nor strength except through Allah')
explanationEn: Surrendering personal helplessness and leaning entirely upon Allah's strength unlocks inner calm and treasures of Jannah.

questionEn: What four phrases did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say were dearer to him than everything upon which the sun rises?
optionsEn: SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, and Allahu Akbar
explanationEn: These four beloved remembrances ('al-Baqiyat al-Salihat') plant trees in Paradise for the believer who repeats them.

questionEn: Which comprehensive du'a did Anas (RA) report was the single most frequent supplication of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar' (Surah 2:201)
explanationEn: Asked between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone during Tawaf and in daily prayer, this Qur'anic gem gathers every good of both worlds.

questionEn: What du'a did Umm Salamah (RA) note Prophet Muhammad ﷺ repeated most often inside his own home regarding steadfastness of faith?
optionsEn: 'Ya Muqallib al-qulub, thabbit qalbi 'ala dinik' ('O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm upon Your religion!')
explanationEn: Even the sinless Messenger of Allah ﷺ constantly begged Allah to anchor his heart, reminding believers never to take faith for granted.

questionEn: What touching promise did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA) after taking his hand and saying 'By Allah, I love you, O Mu'adh,' advising him never to omit what du'a after every obligatory prayer?
optionsEn: 'Allahumma a'inni 'ala dhikrika wa shukrika wa husni 'ibadatik' ('O Allah, help me to remember You, thank You, and worship You in the best manner')
explanationEn: Even remembering, thanking, and worshiping Allah properly requires Allah's loving assistance.

questionEn: How many times in total did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ perform Umrah during his lifetime after the Hijrah?
optionsEn: Four times (Hudaybiyyah [intended/blocked], Umrat al-Qada, Umrat al-Ji'ranah, and the Umrah combined with his Farewell Hajj)
explanationEn: All four of the Prophet's ﷺ Umrahs occurred in the month of Dhul-Qa'dah (counting Hudaybiyyah as intended and rewarded, plus Qada, Ji'ranah, and the Qiran Umrah initiated in Dhul-Qa'dah before his 10 AH Hajj).

questionEn: How many times did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ perform Hajj after Hijrah to Madinah?
optionsEn: Once—the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat al-Wada) in 10 AH
explanationEn: Though he performed Hajj before prophethood/Hijrah in Makkah, after the Hijrah he performed Hajj exactly once, teaching every detail cleanly to over 100,000 pilgrims.

questionEn: What spiritual reward did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise for visiting Masjid Quba in Madinah with pure intention and praying two rak'ahs there?
optionsEn: Whoever purifies himself at home and comes to Masjid Quba solely to pray inside it earns the reward equivalent to an Umrah!
explanationEn: True to his own habit, the Prophet ﷺ visited Masjid Quba every Saturday—riding or walking—to pray two rak'ahs there.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Fadl al-Salah fi Masjid Makkah wal-Madinah); Sunan Ibn Majah

questionEn: How much more reward did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare one prayer inside his Mosque (Al-Masjid an-Nabawi) holds compared to any other mosque except Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: One thousand times better (while prayer in Al-Masjid al-Haram is 100,000 times better!)
explanationEn: For Duya pilgrims visiting Makkah and Madinah, every single Salah inside these sacred sanctuaries multiplies spiritual blessings beyond measure.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Fadl al-Salah fi Masjid Makkah wal-Madinah); Sunan Ibn Majah

questionEn: What sacred area inside Al-Masjid an-Nabawi did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ call 'a garden from the gardens of Paradise' (Rawdah min Riyad al-Jannah)?
optionsEn: The space between his house (Aishah's chamber) and his pulpit (Minbar)
explanationEn: Pilgrims today cherish praying peacefully in Al-Rawdah al-Sharifah, honoring the exact ground where the Prophet ﷺ prayed, taught, and stood on his pulpit.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Fadl al-Salah fi Masjid Makkah wal-Madinah)

questionEn: Only to which three mosques on earth did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say one should undertake special religious travel (Shadd al-Rihal)?
optionsEn: Al-Masjid al-Haram (Makkah), his Mosque (Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah), and Al-Masjid al-Aqsa (Jerusalem)
explanationEn: These three sacred sanctuaries hold unique divine distinction for pilgrimage and spiritual journeys.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Fadl al-Salah fi Masjid Makkah wal-Madinah)

questionEn: What special blessing did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ invoke upon Madinah—echoing Prophet Ibrahim's (AS) blessing upon Makkah?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, Ibrahim was Your servant, Khalil, and prophet, and I am Your servant and prophet; he prayed to You for Makkah, and I pray to You for Madinah for twice as much blessing as he asked for Makkah!'
explanationEn: He also prayed: 'O Allah, bless us in our dates, bless us in our city, bless us in our Sa' and bless us in our Mudd!'

questionEn: What spiritual protection did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ announce guards the entrances of Madinah against both plagues and the False Messiah (Al-Dajjal)?
optionsEn: Angels stand guard at the mountain passes/entrances of Madinah so neither plague nor Dajjal can ever enter it!
explanationEn: This divine protection makes Madinah Al-Munawwarah an enduring sanctuary of peace until the end of time.

questionEn: What unique promise did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give to believers who patiently bear hardship in Madinah and die there?
optionsEn: 'No one bears Madinah's hardship patiently except that I will be a witness or intercessor for him on the Day of Resurrection'—and 'Whoever can die in Madinah, let him die there!'
explanationEn: His deep affection for the City of the Prophet ﷺ inspires millions of Muslims to long to visit, live near, or rest in Jannat al-Baqi.

questionEn: How does sending Salawat (peace and blessings) upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ benefit a believer according to his authentic promise?
optionsEn: 'Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah sends blessings (mercy) upon him ten times, erases ten sins, and raises him ten degrees!'
explanationEn: Especially on Fridays and when visiting his Mosque, sending Salawat ('Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad...') connects a believer's heart directly to him.

questionEn: What happens when any believer anywhere on earth sends Salam upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ—and how does Allah inform him?
optionsEn: Traveling angels convey the believer's Salam directly to the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah returns his soul to him so he personally returns the Salam!
Only travelers in Madinah reach him
explanationEn: Whether standing before his chamber in Madinah or praying miles away at home, every sincere 'Al-Salamu alayka ya Rasul Allah' is received and answered!
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Manasik); Sunan al-Nasa'i

questionEn: Who did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warn is truly 'the miser' (al-Bakhil) when his blessed name is mentioned?
optionsEn: 'The true miser is the one in whose presence I am mentioned yet he fails to send Salawat upon me!'
explanationEn: Whispering 'Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam' whenever hearing his name is a cherished mark of love and gratitude.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ instruct believers to recite upon entering any mosque—and what upon exiting—reflecting humility and seeking mercy?
optionsEn: Upon entering: 'O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy'; upon exiting: 'O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty'
Upon entering: sing poetry; upon exiting: run fast
explanationEn: Entering with the right foot praying for mercy and stepping out into work with the left foot praying for lawful bounty weaves worship seamlessly into daily life.

questionEn: What travel du'a did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ regularly recite as soon as he mounted his camel or vehicle to set out on a journey?
optionsEn: Three Takbirs, then 'Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin...' (Surah 43:13-14) asking for righteousness, piety, and safe return to family
explanationEn: Today millions of pilgrims still begin every flight and bus ride to Makkah and Madinah with these exact prophetic words.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say whenever his traveling party ascended a high hill or descended into a valley?
optionsEn: They said 'Allahu Akbar' when climbing upward and 'SubhanAllah' when descending downward
explanationEn: Climbing high reminds the heart Allah is Greater than every peak; descending reminds the heart of Allah's transcendence—turning travel topography into contemplation.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ forbid companions from kissing or touching the Black Stone forcefully by pushing others during Tawaf, advising Umar (RA) gently?
optionsEn: 'O Umar, you are a strong man—do not crowd the Black Stone hurting the weak! If you find space, touch it; otherwise face it, say Allahu Akbar, and move on!'
explanationEn: Safety, gentleness, and consideration for fellow pilgrims always outweigh physically touching a stone.

questionEn: What words did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ speak aloud upon first approaching Mount Safa to begin Sa'i during his Farewell Pilgrimage?
optionsEn: 'Indeed Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah' (Surah 2:158), adding: 'We begin with what Allah began with!'—starting at Safa
explanationEn: Facing the Kaaba atop Safa and Marwah, he made Takbir, Tahlil ('La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah...'), and long heartfelt du'as three times.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say when a companion told him his riding camel had knocked down a pilgrim or when he himself rode al-Qaswa through Sa'i/Tawaf so people could see him?
optionsEn: Riding elevated so vast crowds could witness his rituals clearly and ask him questions freely without crushing him, answering patiently all day
explanationEn: Being accessible to thousands of unlettered pilgrims—even from his mount—exemplified his devotion as an educator.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare about the spiritual purity of a person who performs Hajj solely for Allah without foul speech or sin?
optionsEn: 'He returns home completely purified of sins, like the very day his mother gave birth to him!'
explanationEn: And of Umrah to Umrah, he promised: 'One Umrah to the next expiates all sins committed between them, and an accepted Hajj (Hajj Mabrur) has no reward less than Paradise!'

questionEn: Who did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ call 'Allah's guests' (Wafd Allah)—promising that Allah answers their prayers and grants their forgiveness?
optionsEn: Pilgrims performing Hajj and Umrah ('If they call upon Him, He answers them; and if they ask His forgiveness, He forgives them!')
explanationEn: Understanding oneself as Allah's honored guest transforms every hardship of pilgrimage into sweet spiritual privilege.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach is the 'best supplication' of all on the Day of Arafah (9 Dhul-Hijjah)?
optionsEn: 'La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lahu, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in Qadir'
explanationEn: Standing in the plain of Arafah from Dhuhr until sunset glorifying Allah's absolute Oneness was the spiritual peak of the Prophet's ﷺ Farewell Pilgrimage.

questionEn: When Prophet Muhammad ﷺ departed Arafah for Muzdalifah with huge crowds surging around him, what calm advice did he call out holding back his camel's reins?
optionsEn: 'O people, tranquility, tranquility! (Al-sakinah, al-sakinah!) True righteousness is NOT in rushing ahead!'
explanationEn: Calmness, patience, and gentleness toward fellow pilgrims define true prophetic pilgrimage etiquette.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ permit weak women, elderly pilgrims, and children (like his wife Sawdah and Umm Habibah's family) to depart Muzdalifah early after midnight before the morning rush?
optionsEn: Out of compassionate foresight so vulnerable pilgrims would avoid the dangerous crushing crowds at Jamrat al-Aqabah at dawn
explanationEn: Making thoughtful accommodations for vulnerable pilgrims demonstrates how mercy guides every prophetic ruling.

questionEn: What size stones did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ instruct Ibn Abbas (RA) to pick up at Muzdalifah for stoning the Jamarat—and what warning did he give against extremism?
optionsEn: Tiny pebble-sized stones ('the size of a chickpea/bean'), saying: 'Beware of extremism (ghuluw) in religion, for those before you perished because of extremism!'
explanationEn: Using tiny pebbles symbolized spiritual rejection of Shaytan without fanaticism or harm to fellow pilgrims.
reference: Sunan al-Nasa'i (Kitab Manasik al-Hajj); Sunan Ibn Majah

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when asked why he prayed Istikhara (the Prayer of Seeking Counsel) with his companions—teaching them it just like a Surah from the Qur'an?
optionsEn: He taught it only to Abu Bakr
