He taught them to pray two voluntary rak'ahs and recite the Istikhara du'a consulting Allah's infinite knowledge and power before any important decision
He taught it only for battles
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ taught Istikhara for every affair with the same care he taught Surahs of the Qur'an.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach is the 'Master of Seeking Forgiveness' (Sayyid al-Istighfar), promising Paradise to anyone who says it with firm conviction morning and evening?
optionsEn: 'Allahumma Anta Rabbi la ilaha illa Anta, khalaqtani wa ana 'abduka...' acknowledging Allah's favors and confessing one's shortcomings humbly
explanationEn: Reciting Sayyid al-Istighfar with heartfelt certainty each morning and night is one of the grandest protective Sunnahs.

questionEn: What special prayer did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ perform whenever severe drought struck Madinah and crops dried up?
optionsEn: Salat al-Istisqa (going humbly outside to the open prayer ground with reversed cloak and upturned palms praying for rain)
explanationEn: Once, right on the Friday pulpit, a villager cried out that livestock were dying; the Prophet ﷺ raised his hands immediately, clouds formed like a shield over Madinah, and rain poured for a full week until the same man begged him to ask Allah to clear the skies!

questionEn: What beautiful habit did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ maintain whenever actual rain began to fall from the sky?
optionsEn: He uncovered part of his garment/shoulders to let fresh raindrops touch his skin, saying: 'It has just newly come from its Lord!'—and prayed 'Allahumma sayyiban nafi'an!'
explanationEn: Celebrating rainfall as fresh mercy directly from Allah teaches deep spiritual wonder at creation.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Kitab Salat al-Istisqa); Sahih al-Bukhari

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ whisper into the ears of his companions about how Allah responds when any believer sincerely raises both hands in du'a?
optionsEn: 'Indeed your Lord is Shy (Hayiyy) and Most Generous; He feels shy when His servant raises his hands to Him to turn them back empty!'
explanationEn: No sincere du'a is ever wasted: Allah either grants what was asked, wards off an equal evil, or stores greater treasure in the Hereafter.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Witr); Jami' al-Tirmidhi

questionEn: Which two moments did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ highlight when the doors of heaven are especially open for answered du'a?
optionsEn: During the final third of the night, between the Adhan and Iqamah, during rain, and an hour on Friday
explanationEn: In the last third of every night, Allah descends in a manner befitting His Majesty asking: 'Who is calling upon Me that I may answer him? Who is seeking My forgiveness that I may forgive him?'
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Tahajjud); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: What warning did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give regarding a believer who prays for something impatiently and stops making du'a?
optionsEn: 'The supplication of any one of you is answered so long as he does not grow hasty and say: I prayed and prayed, yet I was not answered!'
explanationEn: Persistence in du'a is itself beloved worship and proof of trusting Allah's wisdom and timing.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ regularly recite three times every morning and evening for total spiritual protection (Al-Mu'awwidhat)?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Ikhlas, Surah Al-Falaq, and Surah Al-Nas (plus Ayat al-Kursi and the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah at night)
explanationEn: Before sleeping, he also cupped his hands, recited the three Quls, blew gently into his palms, and wiped over his body three times.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Fada'il al-Qur'an); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: What calming du'a of relief did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach believers to recite in moments of deep anxiety, sorrow, or grief ('Du'a al-Karb')?
optionsEn: 'La ilaha illallahul-Azimul-Halim, la ilaha illallahu Rabbul-Arshil-Azim, la ilaha illallahu Rabbus-samawati wa Rabbul-ardi wa Rabbul-Arshil-Karim'
explanationEn: Anchoring distressed hearts in Allah's Majesty, Forbearance, and Sovereignty over the Mighty Throne melts anxiety into peace.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise believers to do whenever they woke up from a frightening nightmare?
optionsEn: Spit dryly three times to the left, seek refuge in Allah from Shaytan and the dream's harm, change sleeping sides, and never mention it to anyone—for then it can never harm them
explanationEn: Conversely, a good peaceful dream comes from Allah and should be shared only with someone who loves you.

questionEn: What protective du'a did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach travelers whenever they stopped to camp or check into a new lodging along a journey?
optionsEn: 'A'udhu bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min sharri ma khalaq' ('I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created')
explanationEn: He promised nothing will harm a traveler who recites those words until they depart from that stopping place.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about the 'most virtuous form of charity' when companions couldn't afford gold or silver?
optionsEn: Saying 'SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar,' enjoining good, removing harm from a path, smiling, and speaking a kind word!
explanationEn: In Islam's egalitarian spirituality, even the poorest believer can outpace kings in daily charity.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ explain that hidden charity cools Allah's anger and earns Shade on the Day when no other shade exists?
optionsEn: Announcing every gift on the pulpit
Among the seven sheltered beneath Allah's Throne-shade on Judgment Day is a man who gives charity so secretly that his left hand does not know what his right hand spent!
explanationEn: Discreet giving shields the recipient's dignity and purifies the giver's sincerity from showing off (riya').

questionEn: What happened when the Prophet ﷺ was once offered the option to ask Allah to turn the mountain of Uhud into solid gold for himself?
optionsEn: He shared it with Abu Sufyan
He declined, preferring instead to eat his fill one day and thank Allah, and go hungry the next day and humbly supplicate to Allah!
explanationEn: Choosing voluntary simplicity kept his heart perpetually turned toward Allah in gratitude and dependence.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ define true richness ('Al-Ghina') to Abu Hurayrah (RA)?
optionsEn: 'Richness is NOT an abundance of worldly goods; rather, true richness is richness/contentment of the soul (Ghina al-Nafs)!'
explanationEn: Contentment (Qana'ah) makes even a modest pilgrim feel richer than restless monarchs.

questionEn: What simple perspective on worldly attachment did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ offer Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) while placing both hands kindly on his shoulders?
optionsEn: 'Be in this world as though you were a stranger or a traveler passing through!'
explanationEn: A traveler carries light baggage, stays focused on the destination, and never lets temporary inns steal his heart.

questionEn: Which two acts of worship did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ specifically connect to guaranteeing Paradise when practiced faithfully: guarding what lies between one's jaws and what lies between one's legs?
optionsEn: Guarding the tongue (and lawful food) and guarding chastity/modesty
explanationEn: 'Whoever guarantees me what is between his two jawbones and between his two legs, I guarantee him Paradise!'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about the immense virtue of making Wudu thoroughly even when water is cold or inconvenient?
optionsEn: Wait until warm noon to pray
It is among the 'Kaffarat' (expiators of sins) and 'Darajat' (elevators of rank), alongside taking many steps to the mosque and waiting eagerly from one prayer to the next!
explanationEn: He famously taught that on Judgment Day his followers will shine brightly ('Ghurran Muhajjalin') from the radiant traces of their Wudu!

questionEn: What du'a did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach believers right after completing Wudu—promising all eight gates of Paradise open before them?
optionsEn: 'Ashhadu an la ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lahu wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluhu' (and 'Allahummaj'alni minat-tawwabin waj'alni minal-mutatahhirin')
explanationEn: Linking outer water purification with renewed testimony of Tawhid and repentance prepares the soul perfectly for standing before Allah.

questionEn: Which companion's footsteps did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ hear ahead of himself in Paradise during a vision—because of that companion's constant habit of praying two rak'ahs after every Wudu?
explanationEn: Asked what hopeful deed he practiced most, Bilal (RA) answered humbly: 'Whenever I lose ablution by day or night, I immediately make Wudu and pray whatever Allah decrees for me!'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about anyone who walks quietly to Masjid al-Haram, Masjid an-Nabawi, or any mosque for obligatory prayer?
optionsEn: With every step he takes, one sin is erased and one degree is raised—both walking to the mosque and walking back home!
explanationEn: Even Banu Salamah's plan to move closer to Masjid an-Nabawi was gently dissuaded by the Prophet ﷺ so their longer walk from afar would continue recording sacred footprints!

questionEn: What special hour on Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah) did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ encourage believers to seek earnestly with du'a?
optionsEn: A blessed moment during Friday in which no Muslim stands praying and asking Allah for good except that Allah grants it (widely sought when the Imam sits or in the final hour before Maghrib)
explanationEn: Calling Friday 'the best day on which the sun rises,' he urged believers to combine extra Salawat, Surah Al-Kahf, early arrival, and heartfelt du'a.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pray when entering Masjid al-Haram in Makkah and beholding the Sacred Kaaba?
optionsEn: He proceeded calmly toward the Kaaba, touched/kissed or pointed to the Black Stone, began seven circuits of Tawaf anti-clockwise keeping the Kaaba on his left, and prayed two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim
explanationEn: Reciting 'Wattakhidhu min Maqami Ibrahima musalla' (2:125), he recited Surah Al-Kafirun and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim, then drank Zamzam water.

questionEn: What heartfelt du'a did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ regularly recite between the Yemeni Corner (Rukn al-Yamani) and the Black Stone during every circuit of Tawaf?
optionsEn: 'Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar' (Surah 2:201)
explanationEn: Touching the Yemeni Corner gently when possible (without kissing it) and repeating 2:201 unites every pilgrim's Tawaf directly with the Prophet's ﷺ footsteps.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ drink Zamzam water during his pilgrimage—teaching an enduring Sunnah for pilgrims today?
optionsEn: He drank Zamzam standing facing the Qiblah (or as offered directly by Banu Abd al-Muttalib), saying 'Zamzam water is for whatever purpose it is drunk for,' and poured some on his head!
explanationEn: Combining sincere intention and du'a when drinking Zamzam water makes it nourishment, healing, and spiritual refreshment.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Hajj); Sunan Ibn Majah

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to Aishah (RA) when she wept during the Farewell Pilgrimage because menstruation prevented her from performing Tawaf with the other pilgrims?
optionsEn: He comforted her gently: 'This is something Allah has decreed for the daughters of Adam—perform all the rites of Hajj that every pilgrim performs, except do not make Tawaf around the House until you become pure!'
He told her Hajj was ruined
He sent her back to Madinah
explanationEn: After Hajj concluded, he tenderly arranged for her brother Abdur-Rahman to take Aishah to al-Tan'im so she could perform a complete separate Umrah and feel completely fulfilled!

questionEn: Where did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stay overnight inside Makkah's valley on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah or before departing after Farewell Pilgrimage—at al-Abtah (Khayf Banu Kinanah)?
optionsEn: He camped peacefully at al-Muhassab / al-Abtah in the valley of Makkah after Tawaf al-Wada before riding back to Madinah
explanationEn: Even during the intense Farewell Pilgrimage, he observed simple desert encampments at Mina, Arafah, Muzdalifah, and al-Abtah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the immense reward of praying over a deceased believer's funeral (Janazah) and staying until burial?
optionsEn: Praying Janazah earns one Qirat (like Mount Uhud in reward), and staying through burial earns two Qirats—two Mount Uhuds of reward!
explanationEn: Upon hearing this, Ibn Umar (RA) exclaimed in regret: 'We have missed out on so many Qirats!'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say is the best remembrance after Fajr or during the day that equals freeing ten slaves, records 100 good deeds, erases 100 sins, and shields from Shaytan all day?
optionsEn: Saying 100 times: 'La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lahu, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in Qadir'
explanationEn: Simple, steady daily Dhikr transforms ordinary mornings into an unbreakable spiritual shield.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach believers to conclude every social gathering or conversation cleanly in case idle or careless words slipped out?
optionsEn: With Kaffarat al-Majlis: 'Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika, ashhadu an la ilaha illa Anta, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk'
explanationEn: This brief concluding repentance wipes away minor slips from the gathering like a spiritual seal.
reference: Jami' al-Tirmidhi (Kitab al-Da'awat); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ remind his companions about the continual value of three ongoing deeds ('Sadaqah Jariyah') even after a person dies?
optionsEn: Ongoing charity (Sadaqah Jariyah), beneficial knowledge left behind, and a righteous child who prays for them!
explanationEn: Notice how every single one—building a well like Uthman's Bi'r Rumah, teaching Duya/Qur'an knowledge, and raising praying children—remains open to every believer.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ respond when asked what the 'best of Islam' is by a companion seeking practical daily guidance?
optionsEn: 'To feed the hungry and to extend Salam (peace) to both those you know and those you do not know!'
explanationEn: Hospitality and universal peace-greetings capture Islam's warm social heart.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about the excellence of praying in the congregation (Jama'ah) versus praying alone?
optionsEn: Prayer in congregation is 25 or 27 degrees superior to praying alone!
explanationEn: Especially Isha and Fajr in congregation carry immense promise—equal to praying half or the entire night!

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ react when he noticed a man rushing hastily through his prayer—pecking like a crow without stillness in bowing (Ruku') and prostration (Sujud)?
optionsEn: He banished him from the mosque
He gently told him three times: 'Go back and pray, for you have not prayed!'—then calmly taught him step-by-step the essential stillness (Tuma'ninah) in every posture
explanationEn: Known as the hadith of 'Al-Musi' fi Salatih,' it teaches that unhurried presence and calm stillness are pillars of valid Salah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ instruct believers to do when entering or looking toward the graveyard (such as Jannat al-Baqi or Uhud martyrs)?
optionsEn: To knock on headstones for favors
To greet the buried believers warmly: 'Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of the believing dwellings; we shall surely join you, and we ask Allah for well-being for us and you!'
explanationEn: Visiting graves reminds the heart of the Hereafter while offering sincere du'a for those who preceded us—never invoking them for help.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the immense spiritual merit of reciting Surah Al-Kahf on Friday?
optionsEn: It must be read only at night
Whoever recites Surah Al-Kahf on Friday will have a spiritual light shining for him from one Friday to the next (and memorizing its first ten verses protects from Dajjal)!
explanationEn: This cherished weekly Sunnah fills Fridays with light and reflection on four trials: faith, wealth, knowledge, and power.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about the superiority of continuous, modest good deeds over sporadic bursts of exhaustion?
optionsEn: 'The most beloved deeds to Allah are those done consistently (regularly), even if they are small!'
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) noted that whenever the Prophet ﷺ adopted a practice of worship, he kept it steady and consistent.

questionEn: What special du'a did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ regularly seek refuge in after every Salah—specifically in the final Tashahhud before Salam?
optionsEn: Seeking refuge in Allah from four things: torment of Hellfire, torment of the grave, trials of life and death, and the evil trial of the False Messiah (Al-Masih al-Dajjal)
explanationEn: Every Muslim learns this protective fourfold supplication directly before ending every Salah with Salam.

questionEn: What advice did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give a believer struggling with debt and overwhelming anxiety—like Abu Umamah (RA) sitting sorrowfully in the mosque outside prayer times?
optionsEn: He told him to leave Madinah

He taught him the morning-and-evening supplication: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, helplessness and laziness, cowardice and stinginess, and from being overwhelmed by debt and overpowered by men!'
explanationEn: Abu Umamah recited this sincere prophetic du'a faithfully and testified Allah removed all his grief and cleared his debts!

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach believers to seek blessings when eating and drinking—and what happens when someone forgets 'Bismillah' at the start?
optionsEn: Say 'Bismillah' at the start; if forgotten, say 'Bismillahi fi awwalihi wa akhirihi' (In Allah's Name at its beginning and its end), and praise Allah ('Alhamdulillah') upon finishing!
explanationEn: Even a forgetful moment is graciously covered by Prophetic ease and mindfulness.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-At'imah); Jami' al-Tirmidhi

questionEn: What rule of physical moderation in eating did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ establish—long affirmed by modern wellness science?
optionsEn: 'No human fills a vessel worse than his stomach; a few morsels suffice—if he must eat more, then one-third for food, one-third for drink, and one-third for breath!'
explanationEn: This one-third rule prevents sluggishness and keeps body and mind alert for worship and service.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the immense spiritual bond formed when two people love each other purely for the sake of Allah?
optionsEn: On Judgment Day they are shaded under Allah's Throne, sit on pulpits of light envied by prophets and martyrs—and if one loves a brother, he should tell him: 'Indeed I love you for Allah's sake!'
explanationEn: When a companion said 'I love that man,' the Prophet ﷺ asked 'Have you told him?'—teaching believers to express pure, uplifting brotherhood openly.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Adab); Sahih Muslim

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach a traveler to pray when witnessing a stunning new town, sunrise, or crescent moon (Hilal)?
optionsEn: Upon sighting the new crescent moon: 'O Allah, let it appear over us with security and faith, safety and Islam; my Lord and your Lord is Allah!'
explanationEn: Every lunar month—from Ramadan to Dhul-Hijjah—opens with a joyful proclamation of pure Tawhid.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ transform his own sadness when bad news struck or anxiety pressed upon him?
optionsEn: Whenever any matter distressed him, he immediately hastened to Salah (prayer) to converse peacefully with Allah
explanationEn: Hudhayfah (RA) narrated this consistent prophetic refuge: Salah was always his immediate sanctuary in crisis.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise about someone who teaches even one good verse or guides another person to a righteous deed?
optionsEn: 'Whoever guides someone to goodness will receive a reward equal to the one who acts upon it, without diminishing the doer's reward at all!'
explanationEn: Every parent, teacher, and friend sharing Islamic wisdom participates in endless multiplied reward.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about seeking sacred knowledge—encouraging lifelong learning for every believer?
optionsEn: 'Whoever treads a path seeking knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise!'
explanationEn: And he famously prayed: 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge!' (Surah 20:114) and 'O Allah, benefit me with what You have taught me, teach me what benefits me, and increase me in knowledge!'
reference: Sahih Muslim (Kitab al-Dhikr); Sunan Ibn Majah

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about maintaining hope in Allah's mercy even after committing grave sins?
optionsEn: 'Every son of Adam sins frequently, and the best of frequent sinners are those who constantly repent!'—and Allah rejoices more over a servant's repentance than a stranded desert traveler finding his lost camel loaded with food and water!
explanationEn: That unforgettable parable of the stranded desert traveler captures Allah's overflowing joy when a sinner turns back home to Him.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the state of one's heart during 'Muraqabah' (mindful awareness of Allah) when asked by Jibril (AS) 'What is Ihsan (excellence)?'?
optionsEn: 'Ihsan is to worship Allah as though you see Him; and even though you cannot see Him, indeed He sees you!'
explanationEn: In Hadith Jibril (Sahih Muslim), this pinnacle definition of spiritual excellence crowns Islam (submission) and Iman (faith).

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ weep sometimes when reciting Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:118)—or Surah Ibrahim (14:36)—raising his hands through the night?
optionsEn: Out of overwhelming love and compassion for his Ummah, crying: 'O Allah, my Ummah, my Ummah!' until Allah sent Jibril promising: 'We will please you concerning your Ummah and never grieve you!'
explanationEn: Even centuries before we were born, the Prophet ﷺ wept in night prayer pleading with Allah for our salvation and mercy!

questionEn: What unique special du'a ('Da'wah Mustajabah') did every Prophet receive from Allah—and what did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ choose to do with his?
optionsEn: Every other prophet used his guaranteed supplication in this world, whereas Prophet Muhammad ﷺ saved his exclusively as Intercession (Shafa'ah) for his Ummah on the Day of Resurrection!
He used it for rain in Madinah
explanationEn: Holding back his single most precious personal gift for his struggling followers on Judgment Day reveals love beyond words.

questionEn: Where did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise his devoted followers he will meet and quench them with his own blessed hands on the Day of Judgment?
optionsEn: At Al-Hawd (his blessed Cistern/Pool), whose water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, from which whoever drinks a single sip will never thirst again!
explanationEn: Describing its two spouts flowing from Al-Kawthar in Paradise, he lovingly awaits his Ummah there—warning only against altering his pure Sunnah.

questionEn: Which title did the Qur'an bestow upon all the wives of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:6), prohibiting anyone from marrying them after him?
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ahzab (33:6) declares: 'The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers,' honoring their lifelong sacred spiritual motherhood.

questionEn: Who among the Mothers of the Believers was praised by the Prophet ﷺ as one of the four perfected women of human history alongside Maryam, Asiyah, and Fatimah?
explanationEn: Khadijah (RA) supported him with her wealth, wisdom, and unwavering faith when the entire world rejected him.

questionEn: How did Sawdah bint Zam'ah (RA) touch the Prophet's ﷺ heart in her later years when she offered her turn of his time to Aishah (RA)?
optionsEn: Wishing solely to be resurrected on Judgment Day as the Prophet's ﷺ wife, she graciously gifted her nights to Aishah (RA) whom he deeply loved
explanationEn: Sawdah (RA) was also famously generous—when Umar (RA) sent her a sack of dirhams years later, she distributed every single coin to the poor immediately!

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers narrated over 2,210 hadiths, served as a foremost legal jurist (faqihah) whom senior companions consulted, and memorized vast Qur'an and poetry?
explanationEn: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA) testified: 'Never was any hadith difficult for us companions of the Prophet ﷺ and we asked Aishah except that we found clear knowledge of it with her!'

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers—praised by Jibril as 'frequently fasting and praying at night'—entrusted and safeguarded the first unified written copy (Mushaf) of the Qur'an compiled under Abu Bakr?
explanationEn: Literate, deeply devout, and trusted by Caliph Abu Bakr and Caliph Umar, Hafsah (RA) preserved the master Mushaf later used by Caliph Uthman (RA) to standardize official copies.

questionEn: Which prophetic du'a did Umm Salamah (RA) faithfully recite upon her husband Abu Salamah's passing—wondering who could possibly be better than Abu Salamah—until Allah blessed her with marriage to the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un; O Allah, reward me in my calamity and replace it with something better!'
explanationEn: Her sincere surrender to Allah's promise in crisis became a treasured source of comfort for grieving believers forever.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ predict about which of his wives would be the very first to join him after his passing—and how did Zaynab bint Jahsh (RA) fulfill it?
optionsEn: The one living farthest from the mosque

'The first of you to join me is the one with the longest hand (atwalukunna yadan)'—which they realized meant 'longest in giving charity,' as Zaynab crafted leather goods with her own hands and gave all earnings to the poor!
explanationEn: When Zaynab bint Jahsh (RA) passed away first during Umar's caliphate, the wives immediately remembered his prophetic metaphor for open-handed generosity.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tenderly console Safiyyah bint Huyayy (RA) when she wept after hearing someone disparage her Jewish ancestry?
optionsEn: 'Why did you not reply to them: How can you be better than me when my husband is Muhammad, my father is Harun (Aaron), and my uncle is Musa (Moses)?!'
explanationEn: His loving defense transformed an insult into timeless dignity, affirming both her prophetic lineage and her full honor as Mother of the Believers.

questionEn: What memorable spiritual habit characterized Juwayriyah bint al-Harith (RA) when the Prophet ﷺ left her room at Fajr and returned late in the forenoon?
optionsEn: She was still seated on her prayer mat absorbed in Dhikr—prompting him to teach her the four weighty phrases ('SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi, 'adada khalqihi...') that outweigh hours of uncounted Dhikr!
explanationEn: While affirming her long hours of worship, he gifted the entire Ummah four concise phrases multiplied by the expanse of Allah's creation, throne, and words.

questionEn: How did Umm Habibah (RA) express faithfulness to the Prophet's ﷺ Sunnah when her father Abu Sufyan visited Madinah and later passed away?
optionsEn: She mourned for two full years
She refused to attend his funeral
When Abu Sufyan passed away years later, she called for yellow perfume on the third day solely to show obedience to the Prophet's ﷺ rule limiting mourning for non-husbands to three days!
explanationEn: Demonstrating exemplary obedience over personal custom, she visibly proved how prophetic guidance superseded pre-Islamic prolonged mourning.

questionEn: How did Aishah (RA) praise Maymunah bint al-Harith (RA)—the last Mother of the Believers—after Maymunah passed away?
optionsEn: 'By Allah, Maymunah has passed on, and she was the most God-fearing among us and the keenest among us in upholding family ties (Silat al-Rahim)!'
explanationEn: Even after the Prophet ﷺ passed away, Maymunah (RA) ensured she was buried at Sarif—the very spot where her blessed marriage with him took place.

questionEn: Which Mother of the Believers was also known for skillfully transmitting the Prophet's ﷺ detailed rulings on Hajj and Umrah—such as how he performed Ghusl and Wudu?
optionsEn: Maymunah bint al-Harith (RA) (alongside Aishah and Umm Salamah)
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA), her nephew, stayed overnight in her home specifically to observe and preserve the Prophet's ﷺ night prayer, Wudu, and Tahajjud practices!

questionEn: Which two daughters of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ passed away in Madinah during his lifetime while married to Uthman ibn Affan (RA)?
optionsEn: Ruqayyah (RA) (at Badr, 2 AH) and Umm Kulthum (RA) (9 AH)
explanationEn: When Umm Kulthum passed away in 9 AH, the Prophet ﷺ sat beside her grave with tears flowing and affectionately told Uthman: 'Had I a third daughter, I would have married her to you!'

questionEn: Which eldest daughter of the Prophet ﷺ suffered a miscarriage from Makkan hostility while escaping to Madinah after Badr, and passed away in 8 AH?
explanationEn: Her little daughter Umamah bint Abi al-As was the beloved toddler whom the Prophet ﷺ lovingly carried on his shoulders while leading prayer!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Salah); Seerah Ibn Hisham

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about his youngest daughter Fatimah al-Zahra (RA) whenever anyone threatened to grieve her?
optionsEn: 'Fatimah is a part of me (bad'atun minni); whatever angers her angers me, and whatever distresses her distresses me!'
explanationEn: Calling her 'Leader of the women of the believing worlds / women of Paradise,' he honored her beyond measure while still teaching her never to rely on lineage without righteous deeds.

questionEn: What precious spiritual gift did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give Fatimah (RA) and Ali (RA) when Fatimah's hands grew blistered from grinding grain and asked for a servant?
optionsEn: 'Shall I not guide you both to something better than a servant? When you go to bed, say SubhanAllah 33 times, Alhamdulillah 33 times, and Allahu Akbar 34 times!' (Tasbih Fatimah)
explanationEn: Known forever as Tasbih al-Zahra, Ali (RA) testified he never missed reciting it a single night after that—not even on the night of Siffin!

questionEn: Who are the ten noble companions famously grouped as 'Al-Asharah al-Mubashsharun bil-Jannah' (The Ten Promised Paradise in one famous hadith)?
optionsEn: Khalid, Amr, Ikrimah, Abu Sufyan, Suhayl, Hakim, Wahshi, Thumamah, Buraydah, and Adi
Hamzah, Abbas, Ja'far, Zayd, Usamah, Hasan, Husayn, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Jabir
Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talhah, al-Zubayr, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Sa'id ibn Zayd, and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah (RA)
Bilal, Salman, Suhayb, Ammar, Khabbab, Abu Dharr, Ibn Mas'ud, Mu'adh, Ubayy, and Anas
explanationEn: Though many other companions were also promised Paradise individually (like Khadijah, Bilal, Ukashah, Fatimah, Hasan, Husayn), these ten were named together in one famous authentic narration.
reference: Jami' al-Tirmidhi (Kitab al-Manaqib); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: Which one of the Ten Promised Paradise earned the unique prophetic title 'Amin hadhihil-Ummah' (The Trustworthy Guardian of this Nation)?
explanationEn: When Najran's Christian delegation asked for a totally trustworthy judge, the Prophet ﷺ stood and appointed Abu Ubaydah (RA) as 'the Amin of this Ummah.'

questionEn: Which cousin of the Prophet ﷺ (son of his aunt Safiyyah) was honored with the title 'Hawari Rasulillah' (The Disciple/Helper of the Messenger of Allah)?
explanationEn: During the Battle of the Trench when the Prophet ﷺ asked who would scout Banu Qurayzah alone in freezing danger, only al-Zubayr volunteered repeatedly—earning 'Every prophet has a disciple (hawari), and my disciple is al-Zubayr!'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) when explaining who among humanity had benefited him most in companionship and wealth?
optionsEn: 'No one has favored me in companionship and wealth more than Abu Bakr; had I taken a Khalil (closest bosom friend) other than my Lord, I would have taken Abu Bakr as my Khalil—yet brotherhood in Islam remains!'
explanationEn: Reserve 'Khalil' solely for Allah, the Prophet ﷺ placed Abu Bakr's brotherhood above all other earthly friendships.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) regarding divine inspiration and Shaytan's reaction to Umar's presence?
optionsEn: 'Among earlier nations were people inspired by Allah (muhaddathun); if there is one in my Ummah, it is Umar!'—and 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, Shaytan never meets you walking down a street except he takes another path!'
explanationEn: Multiple Qur'anic verses—such as praying behind Maqam Ibrahim and prohibition of wine—also aligned directly with Umar's heartfelt wishes (Muwafaqat Umar)!

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ swiftly adjust his uncovered leg when Uthman ibn Affan (RA) asked permission to enter his home—after remaining relaxed when Abu Bakr and Umar entered?
optionsEn: 'Should I not feel shy before a man before whom even the angels feel shy?!'
explanationEn: Uthman's extraordinary modesty (Haya') was honored even by the angels of heaven.

questionEn: Which two titles did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ bestow upon Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) and how did Ali earn the affectionate kunyah 'Abu Turab' (Father of Dust)?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ found Ali sleeping on the dusty floor of Masjid an-Nabawi after a minor domestic disagreement with Fatimah, brushed dust off his back playfully, and called: 'Get up, O Abu Turab!'
explanationEn: Ali (RA) loved no nickname more dearly than 'Abu Turab' because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself coined it affectionately while reconciling his home!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Salah & Kitab Fada'il Ashab al-Nabi)

questionEn: Which companion of the Prophet ﷺ was praised for having a du'a guaranteed to be answered—after the Prophet ﷺ prayed: 'O Allah, answer Sa'd whenever he calls upon You!'?
explanationEn: Because of this prophetic blessing, people in Kufah later feared provoking Sa'd's du'a when falsely accusing him—and Sa'd became the victorious commander at al-Qadisiyyah!

questionEn: What made Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf (RA) declare that if he lifted a stone in Madinah, he felt sure he would find gold or silver beneath it?
optionsEn: The Prophet's ﷺ personal du'a blessing Abdur-Rahman's honest trade ('Barakallahu laka fi safqati yaminik')
explanationEn: Blessed abundantly, Abdur-Rahman (RA) financed entire armies, freed hundreds of slaves, and supported all the Mothers of the Believers after the Prophet's ﷺ passing.

questionEn: Which companion among the Ten Promised Paradise was Umar ibn al-Khattab's brother-in-law and son of the pre-Islamic monotheist Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl?
explanationEn: Sa'id and his wife Fatimah bint al-Khattab accepted Islam among the earliest converts in Makkah and catalyzed Umar's own conversion.

questionEn: Which devout Ansar companion had such an angelic voice reciting Surah Al-Kahf at night that horses leaped near him and a cloud of heavenly light descended above his home?
explanationEn: When Usayd reported seeing canopy lights like lamps hovering above, the Prophet ﷺ smiled: 'Keep reciting, Ibn Hudayr! Those were the angels drawing near to listen to your voice—had you continued until dawn, people would have seen them openly!'

questionEn: Which young cousin of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ received the Prophet's ﷺ special embrace and prayer: 'O Allah, grant him deep understanding (Fiqh) of the religion and teach him interpretation (Ta'wil) of the Qur'an!'?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) ('Hibr al-Ummah' — Scholar of the Nation)
explanationEn: Answering that prophetic prayer, Ibn Abbas (RA) became the supreme Qur'anic commentator (Tarjuman al-Qur'an) whom even senior Caliphs consulted.

questionEn: Which companion—son of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)—was famous for following even the tiniest physical footsteps of the Prophet ﷺ during Hajj and travel, down to stopping under the exact same trees?
explanationEn: Once when Aishah (RA) noticed how closely Ibn Umar mirrored every turn of the Prophet's ﷺ pilgrimage mounts, she admired his extraordinary devotion to the Sunnah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) when companions chuckled at Ibn Mas'ud's thin shins as he climbed an arak tree to gather miswak sticks?
optionsEn: 'Do you laugh at the thinness of his shins? By Him in whose hand is my soul, they will both be heavier on the Scale on Judgment Day than Mount Uhud!'
explanationEn: A humble former shepherd of Makkah, Ibn Mas'ud's Qur'anic mastery and sincere heart towered over mountains in Allah's sight.

questionEn: Which companion was affectionately known as 'Sahib al-Sirr' (The Keeper of the Prophet's Secrets) because Prophet Muhammad ﷺ confided the secret list of Madinah's hypocrites solely to him?
explanationEn: So deeply did Caliph Umar (RA) trust Hudhayfah's knowledge that Umar wouldn't even pray Janazah over someone until checking whether Hudhayfah attended!

questionEn: Which Persian truth-seeker traveled from Zoroastrianism through Christian monasteries in Syria and Mosul until enslaved and brought to Madinah, recognizing the Prophet ﷺ by three signs: refusing charity, accepting gifts, and the Seal of Prophethood?
explanationEn: Companions personally helped Salman plant 300 date palms for his freedom contract, and the Prophet ﷺ proudly embraced him saying: 'Salman is one of us, Ahl al-Bayt!'

questionEn: Which companion did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ praise as 'The most knowledgeable of my Ummah regarding what is halal and haram'?
explanationEn: Radiant in scholarship, humility, and devotion, Mu'adh (RA) was entrusted with teaching all of Yemen and later succumbed peacefully to the Emmaus plague.

questionEn: Which ascetic companion was praised by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ with the words: 'The earth has not carried nor the sky shaded anyone more truthful in speech than him'?
optionsEn: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA): 'The earth has not carried nor the sky shaded anyone more truthful in speech than Abu Dharr!'
explanationEn: Living without hoarding wealth and speaking fearless truth to power, Abu Dharr fulfilled the Prophet's ﷺ prophecy that he would walk alone, die alone, and be resurrected alone!

questionEn: Who was the wise Ansar woman—mother of Anas ibn Malik (RA)—whose extraordinary devotion led the Prophet ﷺ to grant her the miracle of her marriage gift (Mahr) with Abu Talhah being solely Abu Talhah's acceptance of Islam?
explanationEn: Abu Talhah embraced Islam solely to win Umm Sulaym's hand, and scholars said no woman ever received a nobler dowry than Islam itself; the Prophet ﷺ later saw her in a vision of Paradise!

questionEn: How did Umm Sulaym (RA) display astonishing patience when her young child died while her husband Abu Talhah was out fasting—feeding him first before gently breaking the news?
optionsEn: She asked Abu Talhah: 'If a family lent someone a deposit and asked for it back, should they refuse?'—then gently told him Allah had reclaimed His deposit, earning the Prophet's ﷺ blessing on their night resulting in pious Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah!
explanationEn: Their newborn Abdullah later produced nine sons, every single one of whom memorized and mastered the Qur'an!

questionEn: Which Ansar woman's heartfelt plea to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ against her husband's unjust pre-Islamic oath (Zihar) caused Allah to hear her from above seven heavens and reveal Surah Al-Mujadilah (58:1)?
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) marveled that she sat right inside the room barely able to hear Khawlah's whispers, yet Allah heard her across the heavens—and years later Caliph Umar (RA) stopped his entire entourage just to listen respectfully to elderly Khawlah!

questionEn: Which Ansar woman—known as 'Khatibat al-Nisa' (The Spokeswoman of Women)—asked Prophet Muhammad ﷺ how women earn the same vast rewards as men who go out for battle?
explanationEn: Delighted by her eloquence, the Prophet ﷺ told her to inform all women that caring lovingly for one's home and family with good partnership equals every reward men earn outside!

questionEn: Which aunt of Anas ibn Malik (RA)—whose house in Madinah the Prophet ﷺ used to rest in—received the joyful prophetic promise of joining the very first Muslim naval expedition across the sea?
explanationEn: Years later during Uthman's caliphate, Umm Haram sailed in the first Muslim naval voyage to Cyprus, fell from her mount upon landing, and was martyred and buried there in exact fulfillment of his dream!

questionEn: Which young Ansar companion learned Syriac/Hebrew script in just ~15–17 days on Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ order so the Prophet ﷺ could correspond safely with foreign rulers and scribes?
explanationEn: Zayd's brilliance made him the chief scribe of revelation, an expert in inheritance law ('the most knowledgeable of my Ummah in Fara'id'), and later head of compiling the Qur'an.

questionEn: Which companion's testimony alone did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare equal to two witnesses because of his sharp, unwavering trust in revelation?
explanationEn: When a Bedouin denied buying a horse from the Prophet ﷺ demanding a witness, Khuzaymah testified immediately—explaining 'I believe you regarding news from heaven morning and night, so how would I doubt you over a horse?'

questionEn: Which generous Ansar companion immediately donated his prized orchard of Bayruha' opposite Masjid an-Nabawi when Surah Aal Imran (3:92) was revealed?
explanationEn: Hearing 'You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love' (3:92), Abu Talhah immediately donated his prized orchard Bayruha'—where the Prophet ﷺ loved drinking cool fresh water—to his poor kinsmen!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Zakah); Surah Aal Imran 3:92

questionEn: Which eloquent Ansar companion served as the official Orator of the Prophet ﷺ (Khatib Rasulillah) and was promised Paradise after fearing Surah Al-Hujurat (49:2)?
explanationEn: Thabit ibn Qays had a booming voice; when Surah Al-Hujurat (49:2) warned against raising voices above the Prophet's ﷺ, humble Thabit wept inside his home fearing his deeds were ruined—until the Prophet ﷺ sent word promising he was among the people of Paradise!

questionEn: Which companion of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was affectionately nicknamed 'Dhu al-Nur' (Possessor of the Light) because a bright light shone at the tip of his whip or staff guiding him back to his tribe at night?
explanationEn: When al-Tufayl prayed for a sign to guide Banu Daws, light appeared on his forehead; fearing people might mistake it for a blemish, he asked it to shift to his whip, illuminating his dark path!

questionEn: Which companion—known for his tender devotion to his aging mother in Yemen—never met the Prophet ﷺ in person yet was praised by name by the Prophet ﷺ to Umar (RA), telling Umar to ask him to pray for his forgiveness?
optionsEn: Uways al-Qarani (of the Tabi'un, praised by the Prophet ﷺ by name)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ described Uways's exact appearance and his spotless devotion to his mother, advising Umar to seek his du'a—showing how honoring parents can elevate an unseen believer above renowned figures!

questionEn: Which brave Ansar companion's body was shielded by bees/wasps when Quraysh tried to mutilate his corpse after the betrayal of Al-Raji'?
explanationEn: Asim had vowed never to touch or be touched by a polytheist; when enemies came for his head after his martyrdom, Allah sent a swarm of wasps guarding him until nightfall when a flash flood carried his body away safely!

questionEn: Who was the freedman companion of the Prophet ﷺ whom he trusted to handle his personal water jar, sandals, and siwak—and who asked for one unforgettable wish when invited to ask anything?
optionsEn: Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b al-Aslami (RA), who asked: 'I ask for your companionship in Paradise!'—prompting the Prophet ﷺ to say: 'Then help me for yourself by increasing your prostrations!'
explanationEn: While most might ask for wealth, humble Rabi'ah asked purely to be near his beloved Messenger in Jannah, learning that frequent voluntary sujud unlocks that closeness.

questionEn: Which Ansar chief did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ honor as leader of Banu Salamah over a wealthier rival, declaring miserliness to be a grave moral flaw?
optionsEn: Bishr ibn al-Bara (when Banu Salamah called al-Jadd ibn Qays their chief despite his miserliness, the Prophet ﷺ asked: 'What disease is worse than miserliness? Rather, your leader is white-skinned, curly-haired Bishr ibn al-Bara!')
explanationEn: True leadership in the prophetic worldview belongs to generosity and noble character, never stinginess.

questionEn: Which devoted young convert was nicknamed 'Dhu al-Bijadayn' (He of the Two Coarse Garments) after sacrificing all worldly goods to migrate, and had the Prophet ﷺ descend into his grave at Tabuk?
explanationEn: Tearing a single rough blanket in two for an upper and lower wrap to migrate for Allah's sake, he died at Tabuk; witnessing the Prophet ﷺ lay him gently into his grave praying 'O Allah, I am pleased with him, so be pleased with him,' Ibn Mas'ud wished he had been the occupant of that grave!

questionEn: Which young female companion—sister of Aishah (RA)—lived to age 100 without losing a single tooth or her sharp mind, famously advising her son Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) with fearless faith?
explanationEn: Dhat al-Nitaqayn remained a towering pillar of truthfulness, charity, and courage throughout the century.

questionEn: Which blind companion had a special honor in Masjid an-Nabawi: when he told the Prophet ﷺ he had no guide to bring him from afar, the Prophet ﷺ initially permitted praying at home—then called him back asking 'Do you hear the Adhan?' and urged him to attend?
explanationEn: Even as a blind elder, Ibn Umm Maktum carried the battle standard with astonishing courage later at al-Qadisiyyah!

questionEn: Which companion—known for his piercing intelligence and sharp diplomatic intuition—became known as 'The Conqueror of Egypt' after accepting Islam alongside Khalid ibn al-Walid in 8 AH?
explanationEn: When Amr came to Madinah fearing his past hostility, the Prophet ﷺ assured him: 'Islam wipes out everything that came before it!'

questionEn: Which early companion from Najd/Makkah became the Prophet's ﷺ special caller to prayer inside Makkah itself after the Conquest, trained personally in the sweet cadence of Adhan?
explanationEn: When young Abu Mahdhurah mocked the Adhan loudly at Hunayn/Ji'ranah, the Prophet ﷺ called him over gently, stroked his forehead, taught him the Adhan, and appointed him Mu'adhdhin of Makkah—whose descendants held the honor for generations!
reference: Sahih Muslim (Kitab al-Salah); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: Who was the companion known as 'The Rider of the Prophet's ﷺ Mount' (Ridfu Rasulillah) who rode directly behind the Prophet ﷺ on his camel at Arafah and Muzdalifah during the Farewell Pilgrimage?
optionsEn: Usamah ibn Zayd (RA) (from Arafah to Muzdalifah) and al-Fadl ibn Abbas (RA) (from Muzdalifah to Mina)
explanationEn: Placing young freedman-descendant Usamah ibn Zayd directly behind him before 100,000+ pilgrims silently shattered every trace of racial or class snobbery.

questionEn: Which devout companion of Ahl al-Suffah—renowned for living in simple poverty—was once instructed by the Prophet ﷺ on how to earn his own living with an axe and rope rather than begging?
optionsEn: An Ansar man whom the Prophet ﷺ helped sell his bowl and rug for two dirhams—buying food with one and an axe-head with the other, telling him to cut and sell firewood for 15 days!
explanationEn: Fifteen days later the man returned having earned ten dirhams and clothed himself—teaching Islamic dignity of honest manual labor over dependency.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Zakah); Sunan Ibn Majah

questionEn: In the famous hadith honoring individual strengths among senior companions, which seven leaders were praised respectively for mercy, strength in Allah's command, modesty, judicial insight, Qur'an recitation, halal/haram knowledge, and inheritance law?
optionsEn: In that famous prophetic hadith: Abu Bakr (most merciful), Umar (strongest in Allah's command), Uthman (most genuinely modest), Ali (best judge), Ubayy (best Qur'an reciter), Mu'adh (most knowledgeable of halal/haram), and Zayd (most expert in inheritance)!
Only one person held all titles
explanationEn: Recognizing each companion's distinct God-given strength reflects the Prophet's ﷺ genius in nurturing diverse talents across the community.

questionEn: What personal care did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) show Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) when Jabir fell gravely ill in Madinah?
optionsEn: He told him to move to Makkah

The Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr walked on foot to visit Jabir when he was unconscious, made wudu and sprinkled water over Jabir to revive him, and guided his inheritance question—revealing Surah Al-Nisa (4:176)!
explanationEn: Jabir later became one of the chief narrators of the Prophet's ﷺ Farewell Pilgrimage and lived long enough to teach in Masjid an-Nabawi in his twilight years.

questionEn: Which faithful companion of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was famous for always carrying the Prophet's ﷺ water pitcher and sandals—and became known as 'Sahib al-Siwak wal-Na'layn'?
explanationEn: So intimately trusted was Ibn Mas'ud inside the Prophet's ﷺ home that newcomers even mistook him and his mother for members of the Prophet's own family!

questionEn: Which formerly hostile Makkan did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warmly welcome back after the Conquest with the words: 'Welcome to the rider-emigrant (Al-Rakib al-Muhajir)'?
optionsEn: Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl (RA) when he returned from Yemen to Makkah after the Conquest
explanationEn: Welcoming Abu Jahl's own repentant son with open arms ('Welcome to the rider-emigrant!') showed zero resentment toward the past.

questionEn: Which companion of the Prophet ﷺ was affectionately called 'Dhu al-Yadayn' (He of the Two Long Hands) and respectfully reminded the Prophet ﷺ when he once accidentally ended a four-rak'ah prayer after two rak'ahs?
optionsEn: Al-Khirbaq (Dhu al-Yadayn) (RA), who asked politely: 'Has prayer been shortened, O Messenger of Allah, or did you forget?'—teaching Sujud al-Sahw (prostration of forgetfulness)!
explanationEn: Checking with Abu Bakr and Umar, the Prophet ﷺ humbly stood back up, completed the remaining two rak'ahs, and made two prostrations of forgetfulness—giving the Ummah a crystal-clear legal precedent!

questionEn: Which companion's house did the Prophet ﷺ regularly pray in—an elderly blind Ansar man named Itban ibn Malik—to bless a spot in his home as a private prayer corner?
optionsEn: Itban ibn Malik (RA), whom the Prophet ﷺ visited with Abu Bakr despite the heat, prayed two rak'ahs in his chosen corner, and shared a meal with his family
explanationEn: When flash floods blocked elderly blind Itban from walking to his clan mosque, the Prophet ﷺ honored his humble invitation personally.

questionEn: Which companion of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was so remarkably handsome that Angel Jibril (AS) sometimes appeared to the Prophet ﷺ in his likeness?
explanationEn: Dihyah al-Kalbi (RA) was also the trusted envoy who carried the Prophet's ﷺ historic letter to Byzantine Emperor Heraclius.

questionEn: Which faithful nurse and freedwoman did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ affectionately call 'my mother after my mother,' whom Abu Bakr and Umar (RA) continued visiting after his passing?
optionsEn: Umm Ayman (Barakah) (RA), whom Abu Bakr and Umar visited regularly after the Prophet's ﷺ passing just as the Prophet ﷺ used to visit her!
explanationEn: When Abu Bakr and Umar visited elderly Umm Ayman after the Prophet's ﷺ passing, she wept not because she didn't know he was with Allah in a better place, but because revelation from heaven had ended!

questionEn: Which faithful Ansar companion stood watch all night outside the Prophet's ﷺ tent on campaigns—such as before Allah revealed Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:67): 'And Allah will protect you from the people'?
optionsEn: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) (and Abbad ibn Bishr / Hudhayfah on various nights), until the Prophet ﷺ poked his head out saying: 'O people, depart in peace, for Allah has guaranteed my protection!'
explanationEn: From the moment Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:67 descended, the Prophet ﷺ dismissed all personal bodyguards completely, walking fearlessly under Allah's sole protection.

questionEn: Which Ansar companion's radiant staff or spear shone brightly in the pitch dark as he and Usayd ibn Hudayr walked home after conversing late with the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Abbad ibn Bishr (RA), whose staff shone like a lantern until their paths split—when the light split into two, lighting each man all the way home!
explanationEn: Abbad ibn Bishr (RA) also famously kept praying calmly at night during Dhat al-Riqa' even while struck by three consecutive enemy arrows so as not to break his sweet Qur'an recitation!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Salah); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: Which companion of the Prophet ﷺ became known as 'The First to Shoot an Arrow in Islam' and also served as governor of Kufah?
explanationEn: Sa'd (RA) also uniquely served as commander at al-Qadisiyyah and was among the six shura councilors appointed by Umar (RA).

questionEn: Which two grandsons of the Prophet ﷺ were described by Abu Bakr (RA) and companions as closely resembling Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in physical appearance?
optionsEn: Al-Hasan ibn Ali (RA) (chest to head) and al-Husayn ibn Ali (RA) (along with Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith)
explanationEn: Carrying Hasan on his shoulders, the Prophet ﷺ prayed aloud: 'O Allah, I love him, so love him and love whoever loves him!'

questionEn: What prophetic prediction did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ make about his young grandson Al-Hasan ibn Ali (RA) while holding him beside the pulpit?
optionsEn: 'Indeed this son of mine is a Sayyid (noble leader), and perhaps Allah will use him to bring peace between two great factions of Muslims!'
explanationEn: Decades later in 41 AH ('The Year of Unity'), Al-Hasan (RA) selflessly stepped aside from the caliphate to spare Muslim bloodshed and unite the Ummah—fulfilling his grandfather's prophecy to the letter!

questionEn: Which companion eagerly stood up when Prophet Muhammad ﷺ described 70,000 believers entering Paradise without reckoning and secured the promise: 'You are among them'?
optionsEn: Ukashah ibn Mihsan (RA), who jumped up immediately when the Prophet ﷺ described 70,000 entering Paradise without reckoning and asked 'Pray to Allah I am among them!'—receiving 'You are among them!'
explanationEn: When another man immediately stood up asking the same, the Prophet ﷺ smiled tactfully: 'Ukashah beat you to it!'—teaching eagerness for eternal good.

questionEn: Which fearless Ansar companion—brother of Anas ibn Malik—had unkempt hair and dusty clothes yet the Prophet ﷺ said of him: 'Many a disheveled, dusty person turned away from doors—if he swears an oath by Allah, Allah fulfills it; among them is al-Bara ibn Malik!'?
explanationEn: During the desperate siege of Tustar, companions reminded al-Bara of that hadith, and al-Bara prayed for victory and his own martyrdom—and Allah granted both that very day!

questionEn: Which companion of the Prophet ﷺ was praised for having such deep humility that when Caliph Umar appointed him governor of Homs, he wore patched wool and lived like the poorest resident?
explanationEn: Witnessing Khubayb's martyrdom in Makkah had transformed Sa'id's heart so deeply that he gave away his governor salary and fainted remembering Khubayb's faith.

questionEn: Which companion, known as 'al-Rumi,' surrendered all his Makkan gold to Quraysh to buy safe passage during the Hijrah and earned praise in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:207)?
explanationEn: Greeting Suhayb in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ said twice: 'The trade has profited, O Abu Yahya!'—and Allah praised such selfless sacrifice in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:207).

questionEn: Which early Makkan convert and son of Islam's first martyr was tenderly wiped free of dust by the Prophet ﷺ while building Masjid an-Nabawi?
explanationEn: While building Masjid an-Nabawi in 1 AH, the Prophet ﷺ brushed dust off Ammar's hair tenderly and uttered that famous prophecy.

questionEn: Which female companion of Madinah accompanied expeditions alongside Umm Sulaym and Nusaibah to supply water, nurse the wounded, and carry martyrs home?
optionsEn: Al-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh (RA), who accompanied campaigns providing water, treating wounded, and carrying martyrs back to Madinah
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, al-Rubayyi' narrated how dedicated Muslim women served on the frontlines of mercy and medical relief.

questionEn: Which young Ansar boy was entrusted by the Prophet ﷺ with confidential errands in Madinah and kept his secret so faithfully that he refused to tell even his own mother Umm Sulaym?
optionsEn: Anas ibn Malik (RA), earning his mother's praise: 'Keep the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and never tell anyone!'
explanationEn: Training youth in discretion and trustworthiness made Anas a lifelong model of reliability.

questionEn: What three blessings did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pray for Anas ibn Malik (RA) when Umm Sulaym asked the Prophet ﷺ to supplicate for her young son?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, increase his wealth and his children, and bless him in what You grant him!'
explanationEn: Anas lived over 100 years, saw over a hundred children and grandchildren, and had date orchards bearing fruit twice a year instead of once!

questionEn: Which companion of the Prophet ﷺ was praised for having the sweetest, most melodious Qur'an recitation—leading the Prophet ﷺ to remark 'You have been given one of the flutes (musical beauty) of the family of Dawud!'?
explanationEn: Hearing the Prophet ﷺ had secretly listened to his night recitation outside, Abu Musa smiled joyfully: 'Had I known you were listening, I would have beautified it even more for you!'

questionEn: Which companion of the Prophet ﷺ—famous for leading prayer at Quba and fighting heroically until Yamamah—was named among the four Qur'an masters whom the Prophet ﷺ said 'Take the Qur'an from four people'?
optionsEn: Bilal, Salman, Suhayb, and Abu Dharr
Abu Sufyan, Khalid, Amr, and Ikrimah
Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Salim (freedman of Abu Hudhayfah), Mu'adh ibn Jabal, and Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA)
explanationEn: These four towering scholars anchored Qur'anic recitation and memorization across the earliest generation.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ praise Abu Qatadah al-Ansari (RA) as 'The best of our horsemen' (Khayru fursanina)?
optionsEn: Because he won a race in Makkah
Because Abu Qatadah (RA) single-handedly pursued raiders who stole the Prophet's ﷺ camels at Dhu Qarad, recovering them bravely and defending the rear!
Because he traded horses in Syria
explanationEn: Alongside foot-runner Salamah ibn al-Akwa' ('the best of our foot soldiers'), Abu Qatadah showed fearless dedication.

questionEn: Which loyal companion of the Prophet ﷺ was nicknamed 'The Best of Our Foot Soldiers' (Khayru rajjalatina) after outrunning mounted raiders on foot at Dhu Qarad?
explanationEn: Swift as a desert gazelle and deadly with arrows, Salamah held off an entire raiding party alone until reinforcements arrived!

questionEn: Which companion from Madinah was promised by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: 'May Allah brighten the face of a person who hears my words, remembers them, and conveys them accurately to others!'?
optionsEn: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) (along with Ibn Mas'ud and Jubayr ibn Mut'im who narrated this blessing for every hadith carrier)
explanationEn: Hadith scholars for 1,400 years have sought the radiance promised in this prophetic du'a by preserving his authentic words faithfully.
reference: Jami' al-Tirmidhi (Kitab al-Ilm); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: Which female companion—a wise physician/surgeon in Makkah and Madinah who learned literacy before Islam—taught Hafsah (RA) writing and supervised Madinah's marketplace hygiene under Umar?
explanationEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warmly encouraged al-Shifa (RA) to teach his wife Hafsah writing and healing practices—showing his active support for women's education.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Tibb); Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: Which companion assisted the Prophet ﷺ with water at Tabuk and heard him establish the ruling of wiping over leather socks (Khuffayn)?
optionsEn: Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah (RA), who bent down to pull off the Prophet's ﷺ socks until he gently said: 'Leave them, for I put them on while both feet were pure!'
explanationEn: That tender moment at Tabuk established the beloved concession of wiping over leather socks (Masah alal-Khuffayn) for travelers and residents alike!

questionEn: Which companion of the Prophet ﷺ was affectionately nicknamed 'Abu Hurayrah' ('Father of the Little Kitten') because of his gentle compassion toward a stray kitten tucked in his sleeve?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ himself delighted in calling him 'Abu Hurayrah' fondly, matching Islam's gentle care for small animals.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ cure Abu Hurayrah's (RA) forgetfulness so he became the greatest preserver of Prophetic Hadith?
optionsEn: He ordered him to move to Makkah
He quizzed him daily for ten years
He told Abu Hurayrah to spread out his garment, scooped his blessed hands symbolically into it, and told him to press it to his chest—after which Abu Hurayrah never forgot a single word he heard!
explanationEn: Over 5,300 hadith narrations trace back to Abu Hurayrah's (RA) extraordinary blessed memory.

questionEn: Which young female companion—granddaughter of the Prophet ﷺ via Zaynab—was affectionately loved by both the Prophet ﷺ and later her aunt Fatimah (RA)?
explanationEn: When a necklace of onyx arrived as a gift, the Prophet ﷺ told his wives he would give it to the dearest of his family to him—and walked gently over to drape it around little Umamah's neck!

questionEn: Which great poet embraced Islam so sincerely that he stopped composing secular poetry, earning the Prophet's ﷺ praise for 'the truest line of Arab poetry ever spoken'?
optionsEn: Labid ibn Rabi'ah (RA): 'Indeed everything apart from Allah is fleeting/vain!'
explanationEn: Great pre-Islamic poet Labid embraced Islam so sincerely that he stopped composing secular poetry, saying Surah Al-Baqarah had replaced all poetry for him!

questionEn: Which noble woman—sister of Umm al-Fadl and aunt of Ibn Abbas—witnessed the Conquest of Makkah and was praised as 'The Believing Sisterhood' of four sisters whose faith the Prophet ﷺ attested?
optionsEn: Hind, Umm Jamil, Atikah, and Barrah
Maymunah, Umm al-Fadl (Lubabah), Asma bint Umays, and Salma bint Umays (RA)
explanationEn: These four believing sisters (two full sisters, two maternal half-sisters) married pillars of the early Ummah including the Prophet ﷺ, Abbas, Ja'far/Abu Bakr/Ali, and Hamzah!

questionEn: Which companion—converted at Makkah early, tortured, yet became a master of Qur'an and later governor/teacher in Kufah—had his mother Umm Abd live right beside the Prophet's ﷺ home?
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ famously said: 'Whoever wishes to recite the Qur'an as fresh as the day it was revealed, let him recite it according to the recitation of Ibn Umm Abd (Abdullah ibn Mas'ud)!'

questionEn: Which two senior companions did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell the Ummah to follow closely in example right before his passing ('Follow the two who come after me...')?
explanationEn: Their exemplary harmony, justice, and devotion guided the Muslim community smoothly through the turbulent days after the Prophet's ﷺ passing.

questionEn: For what legendary nightly hospitality was the generous Ansar chief Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA) famous around Al-Masjid an-Nabawi?
optionsEn: Feeding Ahl al-Suffah and travelers every single night—hosting up to eighty poor guests at once in his courtyard!
explanationEn: Sa'd ibn Ubadah's nightly platter of broth and meat at Masjid an-Nabawi sustained poor emigrants and travelers year after year.

questionEn: Which companion of the Prophet ﷺ—from Yemen's Azd/Daws—asked 'O Messenger of Allah, give me a concise command in Islam I won't need to ask anyone else about afterward!'?
optionsEn: Sufyan ibn Abdullah al-Thaqafi (RA), whom the Prophet ﷺ told: 'Say: I believe in Allah—and then remain steadfast (Thumma istaqim)!'
explanationEn: Pure faith in the heart paired with steady uprightness (Istiqamah) in action sums up the entire Islamic life.

questionEn: Which companion was affectionately addressed by Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as 'Abul-Mundhir' after answering 'Which verse in Allah's Book is the greatest?'
optionsEn: Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA), who correctly answered Ayat al-Kursi (2:255)—prompting the Prophet ﷺ to tap his chest affectionately saying: 'May knowledge bring you joy, O Abul-Mundhir!'
explanationEn: Affirming a companion's scholarly insight warmly encouraged lifelong love for understanding the Qur'an.

questionEn: Which companion of the Prophet ﷺ had his freed slave-status honored so deeply that Umar (RA) used to say 'Abu Bakr is our master, and he freed our master'?
explanationEn: Calling formerly enslaved Bilal 'Sayyiduna' (Our Master) immortalized Islam's complete abolition of racial hierarchy.

questionEn: What joyful reassurance did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give Umm Harithah when she wept asking about her son Harithah, who was killed by a stray arrow at Badr?
optionsEn: Umm Harithah (al-Rubayyi' bint al-Nadr) (RA), whom the Prophet ﷺ cheered saying: 'O mother of Harithah, there are many gardens in Paradise—and your son has attained Al-Firdaws al-A'la (the very highest Paradise)!'
explanationEn: Struck by a stray arrow while drinking water at Badr, young Harithah earned the highest level of Jannah—lifting his mother's grief into radiant joy!

questionEn: What unforgettable promise did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give a humble Bedouin who confessed he had prepared nothing for the Hour except love for Allah and His Messenger?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ replied: 'What have you prepared for it?'—and when the man answered humbly 'Only love of Allah and His Messenger,' the Prophet ﷺ gave the joyous promise: 'You will be with those whom you love!'
He gave an exact calendar year
explanationEn: Anas (RA) testified that nothing ever brought the companions greater joy than those five words: 'Anta ma'a man ahbabta' ('You will be with whom you love!').

questionEn: Who was the Prophet's ﷺ deeply beloved freedman and former adoptive son whose own son Usamah was cherished by the Prophet ﷺ like a grandson?
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) noted that whenever Zayd arrived in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ went out to greet him, embraced him, and kissed him.

questionEn: Which Ansar companion's footsteps or Qur'an recitation did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ hear inside a vision of Paradise because of his extraordinary devotion to his elderly mother?
optionsEn: Zayd ibn Harithah / Harithah ibn al-Nu'man (RA)—hearing him recite Qur'an in Paradise because of his extraordinary, tender devotion to caring for his elderly mother!
explanationEn: Hearing someone reciting in a vision of Paradise, the Prophet ﷺ asked who it was and learned it was Harithah ibn al-Nu'man—remarking 'Such is the reward of dutifulness to parents!'

questionEn: Which two companions of the Prophet ﷺ were praised for standing beside him in every single major crisis from early Makkah to Madinah—described as his 'two eyes and ears' or 'two ministers on earth'?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)
explanationEn: In Jami' al-Tirmidhi, the Prophet ﷺ said every prophet has two heavenly ministers (Jibril and Mika'il) and two earthly ministers—and his were Abu Bakr and Umar (RA).

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ ensure the collective honor of ALL his faithful companions against disrespect from future generations?
optionsEn: 'Do not revile my companions! By Him in whose hand is my soul, if any one of you spent gold the size of Mount Uhud in charity, it would not equal a single handful (mudd) of one of them, nor even half of it!'
explanationEn: Honoring the sacrifices of the Sahabah who carried Islam with their lives and wealth is a timeless mark of gratitude in every believer's heart.

questionEn: What is universally recognized by Islamic scholars as the greatest, eternal miracle bestowed upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: The Holy Qur'an—preserved verbatim across centuries, unmatched in eloquence, guidance, and transformative power
explanationEn: Unlike past prophets' temporary physical miracles witnessed only by contemporaries, the Qur'an remains a living miracle accessible to every generation until Judgment Day.

questionEn: What celestial miracle occurred in Makkah when Quraysh demanded a sign from Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, recorded in the opening verse of Surah Al-Qamar (54:1)?
optionsEn: The splitting of the moon (Shaqq al-Qamar) into two distinct halves above Mount Hira before rejoining
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud (RA) and Anas (RA) testified seeing the moon split cleanly into two parts on either side of the mountain while travelers arriving from outside Makkah confirmed witnessing it too.

questionEn: What miraculous water phenomenon did hundreds of companions witness directly from Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ hands when water ran out at Hudaybiyyah and on other journeys?
optionsEn: Saltwater turned sweet in the sea
Pure water gushed abundantly like springs from right between his blessed fingers until 1,400–1,500 companions drank and made wudu!
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) declared that even if they had numbered a hundred thousand, the water flowing from between the Prophet's ﷺ fingers would have sufficed them all!

questionEn: How did Allah miraculously multiply the humble food Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) prepared for just a few men during the digging of the Trench?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ blessed the dough and meat pot with his saliva and du'a, then invited ALL 1,000 diggers in groups of ten—and when everyone ate full, the pot and dough remained as full as at the start!
explanationEn: Jabir and his wife were astounded watching an entire army feast tirelessly from a single small goat kid and one sa' of barley.

questionEn: What happened when starving Abu Hurayrah (RA) brought a single bowl of milk gifted to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ told him to invite ALL of Ahl al-Suffah?
optionsEn: They saved it for next week

Every single one of the ~70+ hungry Suffah scholars drank from that one bowl until completely full, followed by Abu Hurayrah repeatedly until he laughed 'I have no room left!'—and then the Prophet ﷺ drank the remainder last!
explanationEn: Even after every hungry guest drank to total satisfaction, the milk level inside the bowl hadn't dropped—modeling both divine barakah and a leader drinking last!

questionEn: What miracle involving food occurred in Abu Talhah's (RA) house when Umm Sulaym sent young Anas with a few tiny barley loaves wrapped in a cloth for the hungry Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ invited the 70–80 companions sitting with him to eat in groups of ten from those few small loaves until every single man ate his fill!
explanationEn: Anas (RA) saw all 70–80 guests leave satisfied while crumbs still remained on the platter.

questionEn: What miracle did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ perform for Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) after Jabir's father died at Uhud leaving massive date debts to harsh creditors?
optionsEn: He asked creditors to wait 20 years

The Prophet ﷺ walked around Jabir's small date heaps praying for blessing, sat beside them, and ordered Jabir to pay every creditor—leaving all debts fully settled AND Jabir's entire original heap untouched!
explanationEn: Even the stunned creditors gazed in disbelief seeing the heap barely diminished after taking every measure owed them.

questionEn: What miraculous testimony did companions repeatedly witness inside Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ hands regarding small pebbles held in his palm?
optionsEn: Companions clearly heard tiny pebbles in the Prophet's ﷺ palm glorifying Allah (making Tasbih) like the hum of bees—and heard the same in Abu Bakr's, Umar's, and Uthman's hands!
explanationEn: Even inanimate stones recognized their Creator and glorified Him in the presence of His Messenger ﷺ.

questionEn: What miraculous interaction with trees did companions witness when Prophet Muhammad ﷺ needed shelter on a treeless plain during a journey?
optionsEn: Trees bent down fruit from afar
Two separate trees uprooted smoothly, drew together to form a shaded screen for him, and returned cleanly to their original places afterward!
He grew palms in one second
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) witnessed this in awe—echoed by the well-known account of a Bedouin embracing Islam immediately after seeing a tree walk to the Prophet ﷺ at his call!

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ heal Abdullah ibn Atik (RA) when Ibn Atik broke his leg leaping down stairs in the dark during a mission?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ gently stroked the broken leg with his blessed hand—and Ibn Atik testified it healed instantaneously as though nothing had ever hurt it!
He splinted it for six months
explanationEn: Similarly, he healed Ali's severely inflamed eyes at Khaybar and Salamah ibn al-Akwa's wounded shin instantaneously by Allah's permission.

questionEn: What prophetic miracle occurred to Abu Hurayrah's (RA) empty leather pouch of dates after the Prophet ﷺ touched a few leftover dates inside and prayed for barakah?
optionsEn: It turned into dates forever until tomorrow only

Abu Hurayrah ate from that single small pouch, fed companions, and gave away sackfuls for decades—estimating he distributed over 50 camel-loads from it until it was finally lost on the day Uthman (RA) was martyred!
explanationEn: For more than twenty-five years, Abu Hurayrah never put his whole hand in to measure—taking out handfuls faithfully just as the Prophet ﷺ instructed!

questionEn: What happened when a runaway, aggressive male camel in an Ansar garden terrified everyone until Prophet Muhammad ﷺ walked calmly inside?
optionsEn: The raging camel froze, walked quietly up to the Prophet ﷺ, knelt down meekly, and rested its forehead on the ground before him!
explanationEn: Animals recognized his gentleness immediately—prompting amazed companions to say even beasts bowed before him while humans stubbornly resisted!

questionEn: What prophecy did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ announce to his daughter Fatimah (RA) and wives regarding the succession of his passing—and how was it fulfilled?
optionsEn: He gave exact dates of earthquakes
He told Fatimah she would be the first of his family to join him (fulfilled in 6 months), and told his wives the 'longest-handed' in charity would follow first (fulfilled by Zaynab bint Jahsh)
He said all would live 100 years
explanationEn: Both intimate prophecies unfolded with astonishing precision right after his departure.

questionEn: Which remarkable prophecy about Muslim sailors crossing the sea did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell Umm Haram (RA) while resting in Madinah—years before Muslims even owned a navy?
optionsEn: He smiled seeing in a dream 'people of my Ummah riding the green ocean like kings upon thrones!'—fulfilled under Mu'awiyah when the first fleet sailed to Cyprus!
He meant only fishing boats in Jeddah
explanationEn: At the time of that vision in Madinah, Muslims barely controlled an oasis—yet within twenty years of his passing they launched a victorious Mediterranean fleet!

questionEn: What eerie prediction did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ make about a fierce fire that would erupt in the Hijaz centuries after his passing?
optionsEn: 'The Hour will not come until a fire emerges from the land of Hijaz that illuminates the necks of camels in Bosra (Syria)!'—historically recorded verbatim by chroniclers in 654 AH (1256 CE) near Madinah!
explanationEn: In 654 AH, a massive volcanic eruption in Madinah's eastern Harrah lit up the night sky brightly enough that observers in Bosra, Syria, read letters by its glow—recorded by Imam al-Nawawi and Abu Shamah as eyewitness history!

questionEn: What prophecy did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell Abu Dharr and his companions regarding Egypt long before Amr ibn al-As's campaign?
optionsEn: 'You will conquer Egypt—a land where the qirat is mentioned—so treat its people with kindness, for they have ties of protection and kinship with us!'
explanationEn: Both Prophet Ibrahim's wife Hajar (mother of Ismail) and the Prophet's own wife Mariyah al-Qibtiyyah hailed from Egypt, inspiring his explicit command of kindness toward Egyptians!

questionEn: What prophetic promise did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give regarding the future conquest of Constantinople (Istanbul) centuries before it occurred?
optionsEn: 'Verily you shall conquer Constantinople: what a wonderful commander will its commander be, and what a wonderful army will that army be!'
explanationEn: Generations of believers—from elderly Abu Ayyub al-Ansari to Sultan Mehmed II—strived joyfully to earn the Prophet's ﷺ praise.

questionEn: What subtle prophecy did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ utter standing atop Mount Uhud alongside Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman (RA) when the mountain trembled beneath their feet?
optionsEn: 'Be still, O Uhud! For upon you stand a Prophet, a Siddiq (Abu Bakr), and two martyrs (Umar and Uthman)!'
explanationEn: Years later, Caliph Umar (RA) and Caliph Uthman (RA) both died as martyrs just as the Prophet ﷺ foretold on Uhud.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe the spiritual miracle of the Qur'an's preservation and the Ummah's unity around truth despite vast trials?
optionsEn: 'A group from my Ummah will always remain steadfast upon the truth, unharmed by those who forsake or oppose them, until Allah's command arrives!'
explanationEn: Across fourteen centuries of rise and decline, sincere scholars and believers have unfailingly carried the torch of Islam.

questionEn: What surprising socio-economic prophecy in Hadith Jibril did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ state as a visible sign of later eras—now starkly familiar in the Arabian Peninsula?
optionsEn: 'You will see barefoot, naked, destitute shepherds competing with one another in constructing towering skyscrapers!'
explanationEn: Uttered in 7th-century desert Madinah where most lived in one-story mud huts, this prediction captures modern Gulf megacities with uncanny precision.

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Ahzab (33:21) describe Prophet Muhammad ﷺ as the timeless living blueprint for every believer?
optionsEn: 'Certainly in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example (Uswah Hasanah) for anyone whose hope is in Allah and the Last Day and who remembers Allah abundantly'
explanationEn: His comprehensive humanity—as orphan, trader, husband, father, neighbor, leader, and worshiper—makes him an actionable role model in every sphere of life.

questionEn: Which lofty Qur'anic verse testifies directly to the supreme nobility of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ moral character?
optionsEn: 'And indeed, you are of a tremendous moral character (Khuluqin Azim)' (Surah Al-Qalam 68:4)
'Read in the name of your Lord' (96:1)
explanationEn: Allah's direct oath in Surah Al-Qalam praising his character outweighs every earthly title.
