questionEn: Which two divine names of Allah's own mercy—Al-Ra'uf (Full of Kindness) and Al-Rahim (Merciful)—did Allah uniquely bestow upon Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Surah Al-Tawbah (9:128)?
optionsEn: 'There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer, deeply concerned for you, and to the believers he is full of kindness (Ra'uf) and merciful (Rahim)!'
explanationEn: Sharing those two tender names underscores how deeply the Prophet ﷺ feels every pain and joy of his followers.

questionEn: What universal title does Surah Al-Ahzab (33:40) confirm for Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, affirming no prophet will ever arise after him?
optionsEn: Khatam al-Nabiyyin (The Seal of the Prophets)
explanationEn: He himself illustrated this clearly: earlier prophets built a magnificent palace leaving one corner brick missing—'I am that final brick, and I am the Seal of the Prophets!'

questionEn: Which radiant description does Surah Al-Ahzab (33:45-46) give of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ five-fold mission to humanity?
optionsEn: A witness, bringer of glad tidings, warner, caller to Allah by His permission, and an illuminating lamp (Sirajan Munira)
explanationEn: Calling him 'a shining lamp' highlights how one lit candle kindles millions of hearts without ever dimming its own light.

questionEn: What did Allah promise Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Surah Al-Isra (17:79) as a unique station reserved solely for him on Judgment Day when praying Tahajjud?
optionsEn: Maqam Mahmud (The Praiseworthy Station—the Grand Intercession when all humanity turns to him to begin Judgment)
explanationEn: That is why after every Adhan across the globe, Muslims pray for Allah to grant Prophet Muhammad ﷺ al-Wasilah, al-Fadilah, and the promised Maqam Mahmud!

questionEn: How does Allah elevate Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ remembrance alongside His own Name in Surah Al-Sharh (94:4)—'And We raised high for you your renown'?
optionsEn: Whenever Allah is mentioned in the Shahadah, Adhan, Iqamah, Tashahhud, or Friday sermons across the globe, Muhammad ﷺ is mentioned right alongside Him!
explanationEn: Every second of the day somewhere on earth, voices ring out proclaiming 'Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasul Allah!'

questionEn: What command in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:56) unites Allah, His angels, and all believers in eternal reverence toward Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: 'Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with worthy peace (Taslima)!'
explanationEn: This singular verse anchors the continuous worship of sending Salawat and Salam upon him daily.

questionEn: When companions heard Surah Al-Ahzab (33:56) and asked 'O Messenger of Allah, we know how to give you Salam, so how do we send Salawat upon you?', what wording did he personally teach them?
optionsEn: Al-Salat al-Ibrahimiyyah ('Allahumma salli 'ala Muhammadin wa 'ala ali Muhammadin kama sallayta 'ala Ibrahima...')
explanationEn: Recited in every Muslim's daily Tashahhud, Al-Salat al-Ibrahimiyyah links the blessed families of Ibrahim and Muhammad ﷺ forever.

questionEn: What measure of love for Prophet Muhammad ﷺ did he state is essential for true completeness of faith (Iman)?
optionsEn: 'None of you truly believes until I am dearer to him than his father, his child, and all of mankind!'
'Love him only as a distant king'
explanationEn: When Umar (RA) candidly said 'You are dearer to me than everything except my own self,' the Prophet ﷺ gently guided him until Umar realized he loved him even more than his own self—'Now, O Umar!'

questionEn: Which three sweet qualities did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare allow a believer to taste the genuine sweetness of faith ('Halawat al-Iman')?
optionsEn: Loving Allah and His Messenger more than anything else, loving another person solely for Allah's sake, and hating to return to disbelief as intensely as hating being thrown into fire!
explanationEn: Loving Allah and His Messenger ﷺ awakens joy in worship that transforms hardship into spiritual delight.

questionEn: How does the Qur'an in Surah Aal Imran (3:31) define the ultimate test and proof of claiming to love Allah?
optionsEn: 'Say: If you truly love Allah, then follow me (Prophet Muhammad ﷺ); Allah will love you and forgive your sins!'
explanationEn: True love is demonstrated by walking joyfully in the footsteps of the Prophet's ﷺ character, mercy, and worship.

questionEn: What warning did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give about anyone who knowingly rejects or turns away from his authentic Sunnah—and what reward for reviving a forgotten Sunnah?
optionsEn: 'Everyone of my Ummah will enter Paradise except one who refuses!'—explaining 'Whoever obeys me enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys me has refused!'
explanationEn: Following the Prophet ﷺ is the clearest bridge between sincere love and eternal Paradise.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warn believers against religious exaggeration toward himself personally, unlike earlier communities?
optionsEn: 'Do not exaggerate in praising me as the Christians praised the son of Mary; I am only His servant—so say: The Servant of Allah and His Messenger!'
explanationEn: Honoring him as Allah's beloved servant and final Messenger preserves pure Tawhid while keeping love boundless.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell his companions in one hadith that he has five noble names (or several descriptive names) summarizing his role?
optionsEn: 'I am Muhammad (the Praised), Ahmad (most Praiseworthy), al-Mahi (through whom Allah erases disbelief), al-Hashir (at whose feet humanity is gathered), and al-Aqib (the Last Prophet after whom comes none)'
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim he also added 'Nabiyy al-Tawbah' (Prophet of Repentance) and 'Nabiyy al-Rahmah' (Prophet of Mercy).

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ express his close brotherhood with all previous Prophets of Allah—such as Musa, Isa, and Ibrahim (AS)?
optionsEn: 'The prophets are paternal brothers: their mothers are different, yet their religion is one!'—and 'Do not give me superiority over Musa or Yunus ibn Matta out of partisan boast!'
explanationEn: Humility toward fellow prophets like Musa and Yunus (AS) underscores the unified chain of divine revelation.

questionEn: In what six special ways did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say Allah uniquely favored him over earlier prophets (per Sahih Muslim)?
optionsEn: Granted concise comprehensive speech (Jawami' al-Kalim), aided by awe, spoils made lawful, the entire earth made a pure mosque and means of purification (Tayammum), sent to ALL humanity (not one nation), and closing the line of prophethood!
explanationEn: Making the entire earth a clean mosque means a believer—whether on a desert highway, airport, or mountain—can pray cleanly anywhere without needing a dedicated temple!

questionEn: What does 'Jawami' al-Kalim'—one of the unique miracles granted to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ—mean?
optionsEn: Concise, crystal-clear short expressions containing oceans of profound legal, spiritual, and ethical wisdom
explanationEn: Three-word gems like 'Actions are by intentions' ('Innamal-a'malu bin-niyyat') or 'Do not get angry' summarize entire books of ethics!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Bad' al-Wahy & Kitab al-Ta'bir)

questionEn: Which hadith opens Imam al-Bukhari's entire Sahih collection, capturing the core spiritual secret of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ teaching?
optionsEn: 'Indeed, actions are judged only by their intentions (Niyyat), and every person shall receive only what they intended—so whoever migrated for Allah and His Messenger, his migration is for Allah and His Messenger!'
explanationEn: Spoken in the context of the Hijrah, this foundational hadith transforms every step of a pilgrim's journey depending on the purity of their heart.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe the beauty of brotherhood across the global Ummah—deeply felt during Umrah and Hajj?
optionsEn: 'The parable of the believers in their mutual affection, mercy, and compassion is like a single body: when one limb aches, the entire body responds with sleeplessness and fever!'
explanationEn: Standing shoulder to shoulder in white Ihram around the Kaaba embodies this living single-body Ummah.

questionEn: What architectural image did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ use to describe how believers support and strengthen one another?
optionsEn: Interlacing his fingers tightly, he said: 'A believer to another believer is like a solidly built structure (bunyan), each part reinforcing the next!'
explanationEn: Interlaced fingers vividly illustrate mutual care, patience, and shared strength.

questionEn: What famous metaphor did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give about good company versus harmful company?
optionsEn: 'The example of a righteous companion and a bad companion is like a seller of musk and a blacksmith's bellows: the musk-seller either gifts you scent, sells you scent, or leaves you smelling sweet, while the bellows burns clothes or leaves foul smoke!'
explanationEn: Choosing spiritually uplifting friends—especially on pilgrimage and in community life—perfumes the soul.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ illustrate the danger of passive indifference to public corruption in his famous 'Ship Parable'?
optionsEn: Passengers on the lower deck decided to drill a hole in the hull for easy water rather than walking upstairs—if those on the upper deck stop them out of care, everyone is saved; if they stay silent, the entire ship sinks!
explanationEn: This brilliant parable teaches collective civic responsibility, gentle enjoining of good, and preventing harm before everyone suffers.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ explain the believer's unmatched spiritual resilience in both joy and hardship?
optionsEn: 'How wonderful is the affair of the believer! All his affairs are good—if blessed with joy he gives thanks and it is good; if struck by hardship he shows patience and it is good—and that belongs to no one except the believer!'
explanationEn: Gratitude (Shukr) in ease and Patience (Sabr) in adversity turn every season of life into spiritual victory.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare about how Allah treats anyone who takes even one small step toward Him?
optionsEn: In Hadith Qudsi: 'If My servant draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by an arm's length; if he walks toward Me, I come to him at speed!'
explanationEn: Allah's eager grace always outpaces our smallest sincere effort.

questionEn: What comforting Hadith Qudsi did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ convey regarding Allah's mercy outweighing His wrath—especially comforting pilgrims seeking forgiveness?
optionsEn: 'When Allah completed creation, He wrote in His Book above His Throne: Indeed My Mercy prevails over My Wrath (Inna Rahmati taghlibu ghadabi)!'
explanationEn: Inscribed above the Mighty Throne itself, Allah's prevailing Mercy welcomes every repentant soul.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reassure a despairing man who thought his sins were too huge—citing the Hadith Qudsi 'O son of Adam, so long as you call upon Me and hope in Me...'?
optionsEn: 'Even if your sins reached the clouds of the sky and then you asked My forgiveness, I would forgive you without minding! And if you came with an earthful of sins without associating partners with Me, I would meet you with an earthful of forgiveness!'
explanationEn: Pairing pure Tawhid with sincere repentance wipes away mountains of past errors instantly.

questionEn: What profound promise did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ make regarding seeing him in a true dream?
optionsEn: 'Whoever sees me in a dream has truly seen me, for Shaytan cannot take my likeness!'
explanationEn: Scholars clarify this refers to seeing the Prophet ﷺ in his authentic description recorded in the Shama'il, bringing joy and spiritual encouragement—while all Islamic law remains grounded solely in the Qur'an and Sunnah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ tell his companions about the exact reward of visiting Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah and Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah while maintaining pure manners?
optionsEn: Prayers in Makkah earn 100,000 times reward and in Madinah 1,000 times—while any act of injustice or sin inside the Haram carries grave gravity, teaching pilgrims utmost reverence!
explanationEn: Combining immense prayer reward with heightened mindfulness (Taqwa) makes pilgrimage spiritually transformative.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say to comfort believers who deeply long to have lived in his own blessed lifetime?
optionsEn: 'Blessed (Tuba) is he who saw me and believed in me—and blessed seven times (Tuba, sevenfold!) is he who believed in me without ever having seen me!'
explanationEn: His sevenfold blessing upon unseen future believers affirms that longing for him across the centuries is deeply cherished by Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

questionEn: Which miraculous event occurred when the Prophet ﷺ prayed for rain during a Friday sermon—after which heavy downpour flooded Madinah's alleys for days until the same villager begged him to ask Allah to stop it?
optionsEn: The Prophet ﷺ smiled, raised his hands and prayed: 'O Allah, around us and not upon us—upon the hills, valleys, and tree-groves!'—and the clouds parted cleanly in a ring around Madinah instantly!
explanationEn: Witnessing clouds open like a crown over Madinah right as he pointed in every direction left the entire congregation marveling at Allah's swift answer.

questionEn: What miraculous blessing occurred to Umm Malik's small leather butter-skin (Ukkah) in Madinah after she regularly gifted butter from it to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Because she regularly gifted butter from it to the Prophet ﷺ, he prayed for blessing and told her never to squeeze it dry—and it kept pouring fresh butter for years until her impatient sons finally squeezed it empty!
explanationEn: When she finally squeezed it out of curiosity, she realized the Prophet's ﷺ exact instruction had sustained the miraculous flow all along!

questionEn: What miraculous event occurred at both Badr and Hunayn when Prophet Muhammad ﷺ threw a handful of desert pebbles toward the enemy ranks crying 'Shahatil-wujuh!'?
optionsEn: Allah miraculously carried particles of that single handful of dust into the eyes of every enemy soldier across the battlefield, blinding and scattering them—referenced in Surah Al-Anfal (8:17): 'You threw not when you threw, rather it was Allah who threw!'
explanationEn: Even a handful of desert pebbles became an unstoppable instrument of victory by Allah's direct command.

questionEn: What prophetic promise regarding future believers did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give when describing the scene at his Hawd (Cistern) on Judgment Day?
optionsEn: He will recognize his followers instantly by the radiant light (Ghurran Muhajjalin) shining from their foreheads, hands, and feet from Wudu—'Like a white-blazed horse among pitch-black horses!'
explanationEn: Every daily ablution made carefully in life illuminates the believer visibly before the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Resurrection!

questionEn: What special permission did Allah grant Prophet Muhammad ﷺ on Judgment Day when prophets Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa (AS) each politely say 'Nafsi, nafsi' ('Myself, myself')?
optionsEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ will step forward crying 'Ummati, Ummati!' ('My nation, my nation!'), prostrate beneath Allah's Throne, and be granted 'Al-Shafa'ah al-Uzma' (The Grand Intercession) to commence Judgment and rescue believers!
explanationEn: Allah will tell him: 'O Muhammad, raise your head! Ask and you shall be given; intercede and your intercession shall be accepted!'

questionEn: Which two people will Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say hold the keys to being the first human beings to enter the gates of Paradise?
optionsEn: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself will knock first at Paradise's gate, and the angel keeper Ridwan will say: 'I was commanded not to open it for anyone before you!'—followed earliest by his Ummah including Abu Bakr (RA)
explanationEn: Though chronologically the final nation in human history, Muhammad's ﷺ Ummah will be the very first nation honored to enter Jannah!

questionEn: What heartfelt message did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ leave for believers regarding how Allah handles intentions even when someone plans a good deed and cannot complete it?
optionsEn: If a person sincerely intends a good deed and cannot do it, Allah still writes a full complete good deed; if they do it, Allah multiplies it from 10 up to 700 times or infinitely more!
explanationEn: Conversely, intending a bad deed without doing it earns a full GOOD deed for restraining oneself for Allah's sake!

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ explain the astonishing generosity of Allah toward His Ummah compared to earlier nations in his famous 'Parable of the Laborers'?
optionsEn: Earlier nations worked from dawn to midday and midday to Asr for one qirat; Muslims worked only from Asr to sunset yet Allah gave them TWO full qirats of reward out of sheer grace!
explanationEn: Living in a shorter historical span and shorter lifespans (~60–70 years), this Ummah receives multiplied blessings like Laylat al-Qadr—worth more than a thousand months!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about maintaining gratitude and awe during times of ease so Allah remembers a believer during times of hardship?
optionsEn: 'Know Allah in times of ease and prosperity, and He will know you in times of hardship and distress!' (Part of his timeless advice to young Ibn Abbas RA)
explanationEn: Remembering Allah consistently in health, youth, and calm builds an unshakeable bond ready for life's sudden storms.
reference: Jami' al-Tirmidhi (Kitab Sifat al-Qiyamah); Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: In that same priceless counsel to young Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) riding behind him on his mount, what profound truth about destiny and courage did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach?
optionsEn: 'Know that if the entire nation gathered to benefit you with anything, they could only benefit you with what Allah already wrote for you; and if they gathered to harm you, they could only harm you with what Allah wrote—the pens have been lifted and the pages have dried!'
explanationEn: This liberating teaching frees believers from anxiety and fear of human beings, anchoring courage solely in Allah.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warn regarding a person who tries to deceive, cheat, or exploit fellow Muslims in trade or daily trust?
optionsEn: When he found damp wheat hidden beneath dry wheat in a Madinah market basket, he placed the wet grain on top so buyers could see and declared: 'Whoever cheats us is not of us (Man ghashshana fa-laysa minna)!'
explanationEn: Even a handful of wet grain in a basket drew immediate public accountability from the Prophet ﷺ—establishing consumer ethics in Islam.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ praise honest, trustworthy merchants in business—linking trade directly to spiritual nobility?
optionsEn: 'The truthful, trustworthy merchant will be with the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth (Siddiqin), and the martyrs!'
explanationEn: Resisting greed and dishonesty in daily work elevates an honest merchant to the company of prophets and martyrs!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the immense merit of earning lawful (Halal) livelihood through one's own hands?
optionsEn: 'Nobody has ever eaten food better than what they earn by the work of their own hands—and Prophet Dawud (AS) used to eat solely from the work of his own hands!'
explanationEn: Dignifying honest work—just as the Prophet ﷺ tended sheep and traded—combats laziness and nurtures independence.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about the spiritual danger of unlawful (Haram) earnings when a dusty traveler raises his hands in du'a?
optionsEn: He described a weary traveler shouting 'O Lord, O Lord!' while his food, drink, and clothing are Haram: 'How can such a person's du'a be answered?!'
explanationEn: Purity of income (Halal Rizq) is one of the essential keys to answered supplications—especially vital for every pilgrim heading to Makkah and Madinah!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise about Allah's help for a pilgrim who sets out with pure Halal savings—or even a believer trying to settle honest debt?
optionsEn: 'Indeed Allah is Pure (Tayyib) and accepts only what is pure!'—and whoever takes debt intending genuinely to repay it, Allah helps him repay it!
explanationEn: Sincerity and lawful provision turn every journey into accepted worship (Hajj/Umrah Mabrur).

questionEn: What prophetic prophecy did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ state about knowledge being lifted—warning why believers must study the Qur'an and Sunnah earnestly?
optionsEn: 'Allah does not snatch knowledge away abruptly from people's chests; rather He takes away knowledge by taking away the scholars until none remain, and ignorant leaders issue rulings without knowledge—going astray and leading others astray!'
explanationEn: Preserving authentic scholarship and respecting scholars guards the Ummah from confusion.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the immense virtue of gathering quietly to recite and study the Book of Allah together?
optionsEn: 'No group gathers in one of the houses of Allah reciting the Book of Allah and studying it together except that tranquility (Sakinah) descends upon them, mercy covers them, angels surround them, and Allah mentions them to those in His presence!'
explanationEn: Every study circle in a mosque carries those four breathtaking heavenly gifts.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe the two types of people who hear divine guidance—using the vivid 'Parable of Abundant Rain'?
optionsEn: Like rain falling on soil: fertile soil absorbs it and grows lush pasture (scholars who learn and teach), hard basins hold it so people drink (memorizers who transmit to others), while barren flat land neither holds water nor grows plants!
explanationEn: Whether one understands deeply or preserves faithfully to share with others, every sincere seeker benefits from the rain of revelation.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ declare about why he was sent as a 'Mercy to the Worlds'—even regarding how Muslims treat animals during sacrifice or slaughter?
optionsEn: 'Indeed Allah has prescribed excellence (Ihsan) in all things: so when you slaughter, slaughter well—let each of you sharpen his blade and spare the animal distress!'
explanationEn: He even scolded a man for sharpening his knife in front of a sheep: 'Do you wish to kill it twice?!'

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach about the reward of showing kindness to ANY living creature—even a thirsty stray dog?
optionsEn: 'In every living creature (with a moist liver) there is a reward!'—relating how a sinner was forgiven solely for climbing down a well and filling his leather shoe with water for a panting dog!
explanationEn: Universal compassion toward all sentient life flows naturally from recognizing Allah as Creator of every creature.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe as the 'greatest goodness' regarding caring for one's aging parents?
optionsEn: Repeated three times 'Your mother, then your mother, then your mother, then your father!'—and saying Paradise lies beneath the mother's feet!
Sending only money once a year
explanationEn: When a young man sought permission to fight in battle, the Prophet ﷺ asked 'Are your parents alive?'—and told him: 'Then strive in serving them (fa-fihima fa-jahid)!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise believers to maintain family ties (Silat al-Rahim) even when relatives treat them coldly or cut them off?
optionsEn: 'The true upholder of family ties is NOT the one who merely reciprocates; rather, the true upholder is the one who reconnects ties whenever his relatives cut them off!'
explanationEn: Returning kindness for estrangement breaks cycles of family bitterness and expands blessing in lifespan and sustenance.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ state about the sacred bond of marriage—encouraging gentleness and mutual respect between spouses?
optionsEn: 'The most complete believers in faith are those with the best character, and the best of you are those who are best to their wives!'
explanationEn: He also advised husbands never to resent their wives over a minor flaw: 'If he dislikes one trait in her, he will surely be pleased by another!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe the spiritual miracle of two believers meeting—such as pilgrims greeting one another in Makkah or Madinah?
optionsEn: 'No two Muslims meet and shake hands warmly except that their sins drop away before they even part!'
explanationEn: Warm, sincere brotherhood washes away minor daily sins like autumn leaves falling from a tree.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud (Kitab al-Adab); Jami' al-Tirmidhi

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ identify as the three characteristics by which a hypocrite (Munafiq) is known—warning believers to purify their own integrity?
optionsEn: Wearing plain wool, living simply, and traveling
When he speaks he lies, when he makes a promise he breaks it, and when entrusted with something he betrays the trust!
Speaking quietly, fasting Mondays, and walking slowly
explanationEn: Guarding truth in speech, fidelity in promises, and honesty with trusts immunizes a believer against hypocrisy.

questionEn: What advice did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give about avoiding harmful speech—especially backbiting (Ghibah) and spreading rumors?
optionsEn: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should either speak good or remain silent!'—explaining backbiting is mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes even if true!
explanationEn: Defining Ghibah clearly as saying true things someone dislikes behind their back—and Buhtan (slander) if false—guards community peace.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ warn about 'Namimah' (tale-bearing / stirring discord between two people by repeating hurtful remarks)?
optionsEn: 'A tale-bearer (Nammam / Qattat) will not enter Paradise!'
explanationEn: Conversely, he permitted benevolent tactful words SOLELY to reconcile two quarreling people and restore peace!

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ define the best form of Jihād (spiritual striving) before a believer even confronts external hardship?
optionsEn: 'The true Mujahid is the one who strives earnestly against his own lower ego (nafs) in obeying Allah!'—alongside speaking a word of truth before a tyrannical ruler!
explanationEn: Mastering one's own anger, greed, pride, and laziness is the lifelong daily struggle of every faithful soul.
reference: Jami' al-Tirmidhi (Kitab Fada'il al-Jihad); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: What profound rule of personal responsibility did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ state in: 'Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving alone what does not concern him'?
optionsEn: Focus energy on purposeful worship, service, and self-improvement rather than meddling in fruitless gossip or idle distractions
explanationEn: Protecting focus and mental peace keeps a believer productive and serene.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ encourage believers never to despair when learning the Qur'an despite stumbling over difficult Arabic pronunciation?
optionsEn: 'The skilled, fluent reciter of the Qur'an is with the noble, obedient angels; and the one who recites it stammering with difficulty receives TWO rewards!'
explanationEn: Awarding double reward—one for recitation and one for sincere struggle—encourages every convert and beginner worldwide!

questionEn: What vivid comparison did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give for a believer who recites the Qur'an and acts upon it—comparing him to a fragrant citrus fruit?
optionsEn: Like an Utrujjah (citron): its fragrance is sweet and its taste is sweet!
explanationEn: Whereas one who doesn't recite yet acts rightly is like a sweet date without aroma—encouraging both outward recitation and inward character!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the immense rank of the people who learn the Qur'an and teach it to others?
optionsEn: 'The very best among you (Khayrukum) are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it!'
explanationEn: Uthman ibn Affan (RA) spent decades teaching the Qur'an in Madinah's mosque purely out of love for this single prophetic praise!

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about anyone who relieves a fellow believer of a worldly hardship, eases a debtor's burden, or shields a Muslim's mistake?
optionsEn: 'Allah will relieve him of a hardship on the Day of Resurrection; Allah will make easy for him in this world and the Next; and Allah continues helping the servant so long as the servant helps his brother!'
explanationEn: Service to humanity triggers direct divine assistance in our own moments of greatest need.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ define the core pillars of Islamic ethics in one brief sentence to Wabisah ibn Ma'bad (RA): 'Consult your heart!'?
optionsEn: 'Righteousness (Birr) is good character, and sin (Ithm) is whatever wavers uneasily in your heart and you would hate for people to discover!'
explanationEn: A pure, revelation-nurtured conscience brings inner serenity whenever walking in truth.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Kitab al-Birr wal-Silah); Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: What warning did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give about even a tiny mustard-seed speck of arrogance ('Kibr') in the heart?
optionsEn: 'No one with an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise!'—defining arrogance as 'rejecting the truth (batr al-haqq) and looking down on people (ghamt al-nas)!'
explanationEn: Humility opens the heart to truth from anyone—even a child or stranger—and honors every human being.

questionEn: What three surprising paradoxes did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ swear by oath never decrease a person's dignity or wealth?
optionsEn: 'Charity never decreases wealth; forgiving others only increases a servant's honor; and whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah raises him high!'
explanationEn: Prophetic wisdom overturns worldly illusions: giving, forgiving, and humility are the true pathways to lasting honor.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ advise believers to say when feeling envious upon seeing a sibling's or friend's blessing—to protect them from the evil eye ('Ayn)?
optionsEn: Say 'Allahumma barik 'alayh' / 'Masha'Allah la quwwata illa billah'—praying for Allah's blessing upon them rather than coveting it!
explanationEn: When Sahl ibn Hunayf fell ill from an envious compliment, the Prophet ﷺ taught: 'Why did one of you not pray for blessing (Tabarak) upon his brother?!'

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ summarize the essential wisdom of Prophet Luqman and earlier prophets preserved in his short saying: 'If you feel no shame, then do whatever you wish'?
optionsEn: Modesty (Haya') before Allah and people is the protective moral anchor of faith—when Haya' disappears, no barrier stops wrongdoing
explanationEn: Calling Haya' a vital branch of Iman ('Modesty brings nothing except good'), he made inner moral dignity central to Muslim identity.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say about the immense eternal reward of weeping quietly in private out of awe and love for Allah?
optionsEn: 'Two eyes will never be touched by the Fire: an eye that wept out of fear/awe of Allah, and an eye that stayed awake standing guard in the path of Allah!'
explanationEn: Also counted among the seven shaded under Allah's Throne is 'a person who remembered Allah in solitude until his eyes overflowed with tears.'
reference: Jami' al-Tirmidhi (Kitab Fada'il al-Jihad); Sahih al-Bukhari

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach believers to handle illness and physical pain with spiritual dignity?
optionsEn: 'No fatigue, illness, sorrow, grief, harm, or distress afflicts a Muslim—even the prick of a thorn—except that Allah expiates some of his sins through it!'—while still encouraging seeking medical treatment!
explanationEn: Combining spiritual patience with practical medicine ('Seek medical treatment, O servants of Allah, for Allah created a cure for every disease') models balanced Islamic wellness.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Marda); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe as the sweetest consolation for a believer who patiently endures the loss of a beloved child or loved one?
optionsEn: In Hadith Qudsi: 'When I take away a believer's beloved of this world and he bears it patiently seeking reward, I have no lesser reward for him than Paradise!'
explanationEn: Known himself as a grieving father who buried six of his seven children in his own lifetime, the Prophet ﷺ comforted bereaved parents with unmatched empathy and eternal hope.

questionEn: Which prophetic instruction encourages hope, good thoughts about Allah (Husn al-Zann), and peaceful readiness in a believer's final moments?
optionsEn: 'Let none of you die except having good expectations of Allah!'—and instructing companions gently to prompt the dying with 'La ilaha illallah'
explanationEn: Speaking the Shahadah gently at the threshold of eternity ('Whoever's last words are La ilaha illallah enters Paradise') crowns a life of faith.
reference: Sahih Muslim (Kitab al-Jannah); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ describe the beauty of Paradise awaiting his faithful followers—encouraging steadfast hope through earthly trials?
optionsEn: 'Allah says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has never even crossed a human heart!'
explanationEn: Above every delight of Paradise is Allah's greatest gift: beholding the Countenance of the Most Merciful Lord Himself and earning His eternal Pleasure!
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab Bad' al-Khalq); Sahih Muslim

questionEn: What miraculous prophecy did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give about how Islam would spread peacefully into every dwelling across the globe?
optionsEn: 'This matter (Islam) will reach wherever night and day reach; Allah will not leave a house of brick or a tent of camel-hair except that He will cause this religion to enter it, bringing honor or humility!'
explanationEn: Today over 1.9 billion Muslims from every continent gather toward one Qiblah in Makkah and Madinah—living proof of that prophecy.

questionEn: What did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ promise about his own ongoing awareness and spiritual connection when believers visit Al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah?
optionsEn: He taught pilgrims to offer Salah inside his mosque (worth 1,000 prayers), pray in Al-Rawdah (a garden of Paradise), and send peaceful Salam upon him and his two companions with dignity and quietness
explanationEn: Following Surah Al-Hujurat (49:2), pilgrims lower their voices reverently in Masjid an-Nabawi just as companions did in his living presence.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Tafsir); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: Why did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ emphasize that true love for him must translate into gentleness toward his family, companions, and all creation?
optionsEn: Because 'Merciful people are shown mercy by the Most Merciful; show mercy to those on earth, and the One above the heavens will show mercy to you!'
explanationEn: This prophetic 'Hadith of Mercy' (al-Musalsal bil-Awwaliyyah) is traditionally the very first hadith scholars transmit to new students of sacred knowledge!
reference: Jami' al-Tirmidhi (Kitab al-Birr wal-Silah); Sunan Abi Dawud

questionEn: What timeless two-part guarantee did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ leave for every believer seeking safety from misguidance in any era?
optionsEn: 'I have left among you two things; you will never go astray so long as you hold fast to them: the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger!'
explanationEn: Holding fast to the Qur'an and authentic Prophetic Sunnah keeps the heart anchored on the straight path across every generation.

questionEn: How did Prophet Muhammad ﷺ teach believers to maintain unwavering hope in Allah's constant nearness whenever making du'a during pilgrimage or at home?
optionsEn: When companions raised their voices loudly shouting Takbir on a journey, he gently calmed them: 'O people, go easy on yourselves! You are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent—rather you are calling upon One who is All-Hearing, Ever-Near, and closer to you than the neck of your riding beast!'
explanationEn: Allah's intimate nearness ('And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near' — 2:186) transforms every whispered prayer into direct communion.

questionEn: Which concise supplication of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gathers every good he ever asked for and seeks refuge from every evil he ever fled from—ideal for pilgrims making heartfelt du'a at Arafah or Zamzam?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, I ask You for all good—immediate and future, what I know and what I do not know; and I seek refuge in You from all evil—immediate and future... and I ask You for every good that Your servant and Prophet asked You for!'
explanationEn: He taught this comprehensive du'a directly to Aishah (RA) so any believer can encompass all prophetic goodness in one heartfelt prayer.
reference: Sunan Ibn Majah (Kitab al-Du'a); Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: What ultimate spiritual purpose ties every chapter of Prophet Muhammad's ﷺ Seerah—from Cave Hira to the Farewell Pilgrimage—to a believer's journey with Duya?
optionsEn: Renewing pure Tawhid, walking in his merciful Sunnah, cultivating humble character, and yearning to worship Allah with sincerity at His Sacred Sanctuaries until meeting the Prophet ﷺ at Al-Hawd and in Paradise
explanationEn: Studying the Seerah is not mere history—it is an invitation to love, follow, and embody the living mercy of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in every step of faith and pilgrimage.
